Protruding snake head and rapidly tapering short tail
Limbless small animal scaled by leaves
Elusive natural mysterious woodland mood

basis_claims.quote: Tsuchinoko is a mallet-shaped, thick-bodied serpentine monster said to be sighted in mountain paths, fields, and the thickets of riverbanks.

statement.id: Tsuchinoko digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip ular bertubuh tebal yang terlihat di jalan gunung, ladang, dan tepian sungai.
statement.en: Tsuchinoko is a thick-bodied snake-like figure said to appear on paths, fields, and riverbanks.

basis_claims.quote: a creature about thirty to eighty centimeters long, with a head protruding from a body thick as a beer bottle

statement.id: Gambaran setempat menyebut panjang 30–80 sentimeter dan badan setebal botol.
statement.en: Accounts describe a thirty to eighty centimeter creature with a bottle-thick body.

basis_claims.quote: the national scale of sightings from Iwate Prefecture in the north to Kagoshima Prefecture in the south

statement.id: Laporan penampakan disebut tersebar dari Iwate sampai Kagoshima.
statement.en: Reported sightings range from Iwate to Kagoshima.

basis_claims.quote: The multitude of local names indicates that the Tsuchinoko was not a uniform character nationwide.

statement.id: Nama tsuchinoko bervariasi menurut daerah.
statement.en: Tsuchinoko has varied local names and is not a uniform national figure.

basis_claims.quote: a legendary reptilelike creature the existence of which had never been scientifically confirmed.

statement.id: Keberadaan tsuchinoko belum dikonfirmasi secara ilmiah.
statement.en: Tsuchinoko has not been scientifically confirmed.

amabie.depicted_variant: 1846 kawaraban likeness preserved Kyoto University, naturalistic interpretation
visual_requirements: Long hair and projecting beaklike mouth
Fish-scaled compact body without arms
Exactly three fin-leg appendages visible

basis_claims.quote: Amabie (アマビエ) is one of yōkai (妖怪), a class of mythological and supernatural spirits or monsters in Japanese folklore.

statement.id: Amabie adalah yōkai dalam cerita rakyat Jepang.
statement.en: Amabie is a yōkai in Japanese folklore.

basis_claims.quote: It is said to have appeared in Higo no kuni, today’s Kumamoto prefecture, in 1846

statement.id: Kisah tahun 1846 menempatkan kemunculan Amabie di Higo, Kumamoto kini.
statement.en: The 1846 story places Amabie in Higo, now Kumamoto.

basis_claims.quote: A glowing object appeared every night in the sea of Higo Province [today’s Kumamoto prefecture].

statement.id: Dalam kisah awal, cahaya tampak tiap malam di laut Higo.
statement.en: The early story describes a recurring light in the sea off Higo.

basis_claims.quote: I live in the sea. My name is Amabié. Good harvest will continue for six years. At the same time disease will spread. Draw me and show me to the people as soon as possible.

statement.id: Amabie mengaku hidup di laut, meramalkan panen baik dan penyakit, serta meminta rupanya digambar dan ditunjukkan.
statement.en: Amabie says it lives in the sea, predicts harvest and disease, and asks that its image be shown.

lyngbakr.depicted_variant: The immense whale-like Lyngbakr floating half-submerged with island-like heather growing across its exposed back.
visual_requirements: An enormous whale-like sea creature
Heather-covered back resembling an island
Whale head and flukes visible beneath water
Threatening northern sea atmosphere
lyngbakr.aura: Vast deceptive oceanic threat, awe and dread beneath apparent tranquility.

basis_claims.quote: Lyngbakr (Icelandic, lyngi "heather" + bak "back") is the name of a massive whale-like sea monster reported in the Örvar-Odds saga to have existed in the Greenland Sea. According to the saga, Lyngbakr would bait seafarers by posing as a heather-covered island, and when a crew landed on his back, he sank into the sea, drowning the crew.

statement.id: Lyngbakr (Islandia: lyngi, "heather", + bak, "punggung") adalah monster laut raksasa mirip paus yang menurut Örvar-Odds saga hidup di Laut Greenland; ia memancing pelaut dengan menyamar sebagai pulau berlapis heather, dan bila awak mendarat di punggungnya, ia tenggelam dan menenggelamkan mereka.
statement.en: Lyngbakr (Icelandic lyngi 'heather' + bak 'back') is a massive whale-like sea monster said in the Örvar-Odds saga to live in the Greenland Sea; it baited seafarers by posing as a heather-covered island, then sank when a crew landed on its back, drowning them.

basis_claims.quote: Vignir explained to Oddr that, had they landed sooner, the crew would have surely drowned. The "rocks" and "island" must have been two sea monsters—Lyngbakr, the greatest whale in the world, and hafgufa

statement.id: Vignir menjelaskan kepada Oddr bahwa bila mereka mendarat lebih cepat, awak pasti tenggelam; "batu" dan "pulau" itu tentulah dua monster laut, Lyngbakr, paus terbesar di dunia, dan hafgufa.
statement.en: Vignir explained to Oddr that had they landed sooner the crew would surely have drowned; the 'rocks' and 'island' must have been two sea monsters, Lyngbakr, the greatest whale in the world, and hafgufa.

basis_claims.quote: Lyngbakurinn var talinn vera stærstur allra dýra í sjó og lá hann oft þannig á hálfu kafi að hann virtist vera eyja og leit þá út eins og þar á sé vaxið lyng og því er hann kallaður lyngbakur. Fjölmargar sögur eru um lyngbaka víða frá á Íslandi.

statement.id: Lyngbakur dianggap hewan laut terbesar dan sering terapung setengah tenggelam sehingga tampak seperti pulau yang ditumbuhi heather, karena itu disebut lyngbakur; banyak kisah tentangnya tersebar di Islandia.
statement.en: The lyngbakur was held the largest of all sea creatures, often lying half-submerged so it seemed an island grown with heather, hence its name; many tales of it are told across Iceland.

tilberi.depicted_variant: A small elongated wool-wrapped rib-shaped magical milk thief at the dairy window beside a wooden churn.
visual_requirements: Small rib-derived elongated creature wrapped in grey wool
Flexible stretched form appropriate to milk thief
Icelandic dairy setting
Sinister uncanny atmosphere without violent anatomy
tilberi.aura: Uncanny furtive malicious household magic, small but disturbing.

basis_claims.quote: The tilberi (carrier) or snakkur (spindle) is a creature of Icelandic folklore, created by witches to steal milk. Only women can create and own them.

statement.id: Tilberi atau snakkur adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Islandia yang dibuat penyihir untuk mencuri susu; hanya perempuan yang bisa membuat dan memilikinya.
statement.en: The tilberi or snakkur is an Icelandic folklore creature made by witches to steal milk; only women can make and own one.

basis_claims.quote: To create a tilberi, the woman steals a rib from a recently buried body early on Whitsunday, twists around it grey wool which she must steal for the purpose and keeps it between her breasts. ...  The next three Sundays at communion she spits the sanctified wine on the bundle, which will come more alive each time.

statement.id: Perempuan itu mencuri tulang rusuk jenazah yang baru dikubur pada dini hari Minggu Pentakosta, melilitnya dengan wol kelabu curian, dan menyimpannya di antara payudaranya.
statement.en: The woman steals a rib from a newly buried corpse early on Whitsunday, winds stolen grey wool round it and keeps it between her breasts.

basis_claims.quote: It will return to the window of her dairy and call out "Full belly, Mummy!" or "Churn lid off, Mummy!" and vomit the stolen milk into her butter churn. To suck the milk from the animal's udder, it jumps on her back and lengthens itself to reach down

statement.id: Tilberi kembali ke jendela ruang susu, berseru "Perut penuh, Ibu!", dan memuntahkan susu curian ke pengocok mentega; untuk menyedot ambing ia melompat ke punggung hewan dan memanjangkan diri.
statement.en: It returns to the dairy window, calls 'Full belly, Mummy!' and vomits the stolen milk into the churn; to suck an udder it leaps onto the animal's back and stretches itself down.

basis_claims.quote: The tilberi will then either work itself to death or die because as an evil creature it cannot tolerate the number three. Only the human bone will be left lying in the pasture.

statement.id: Tilberi akan bekerja sampai mati atau mati karena, sebagai makhluk jahat, tak tahan angka tiga; hanya tulang manusia yang tertinggal di padang.
statement.en: The tilberi either works itself to death or dies because, as an evil being, it cannot bear the number three; only the human bone remains in the pasture.

spriggan.depicted_variant: Small shrivelled old-man treasure guardian, not giant transformation
visual_requirements: Small shrivelled old man with disproportionately large childlike head
Human two-arm two-leg form, not tree monster
Cornish cairn/barrow and buried treasure
Eerie foul-tempered mischievous guardian aura

basis_claims.quote: A spriggan /sprɪdʒən/ is a legendary creature from Cornish folklore. Spriggans are particularly associated with West Penwith in Cornwall.

statement.id: Spriggan makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Cornwall (Cornish folklore), terutama West Penwith; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: The spriggan is a legendary creature of Cornish folklore, especially West Penwith.

basis_claims.quote: Spriggan is pronounced /sprɪdʒən/ rather than /sprɪɡən/; the word is borrowed from the Cornish plural spyrysyon 'spirits'.

statement.id: Dari jamak bahasa Cornwall (Cornish) spyrysyon, roh.
statement.en: From the Cornish plural spyrysyon, spirits.

basis_claims.quote: They were said to be found at old ruins, cairns, and barrows guarding buried treasure. Although small in stature, they have often been considered to be the ghosts of giants and retained gigantic strength, and in one story collected by Robert Hunt, they showed the ability to swell to enormous size.

statement.id: Menjaga harta di reruntuhan dan gundukan; hantu raksasa berkekuatan raksasa; menurut Robert Hunt dapat membengkak.
statement.en: They guard treasure at ruins and barrows; ghosts of giants with giant strength; per Robert Hunt able to swell.

basis_claims.quote: They raised sudden whirlwinds to terrify travellers, sent storms to blight crops, and sometimes stole away mortal children, leaving their ugly changelings in their place.

statement.id: Menimbulkan angin puyuh, badai merusak tanaman, mencuri anak dan meninggalkan changeling.
statement.en: They raised whirlwinds, sent storms to blight crops and stole children, leaving changelings.

ryujin.depicted_variant: Deified serpent water kami, Kokugakuin tradition
visual_requirements: Deified serpent water-kami variant
Long coherent scaled limbless serpent
Divine royal protective sea-rain aura
ryujin.aura: Revered stately ocean and rain deity

basis_claims.quote: Ryūjin ("dragon kami") faith is a form of religious thought and practice associated with dragons, a mythical sacred animal of ancient China.

statement.id: Ryūjin berarti kami naga dan berkaitan dengan kepercayaan tentang naga.
statement.en: Ryūjin means dragon kami and names a faith associated with dragons.

basis_claims.quote: Although Japanese ryūjin worship was influenced by China, the Japanese dragon as an object of faith was a deified snake, a symbol of a water kami (suijin).

statement.id: Pemujaan Ryūjin dipengaruhi Tiongkok; naga juga dipahami sebagai ular yang didewakan dan lambang dewa air.
statement.en: Ryūjin worship drew from China, while the dragon could symbolize a deified snake and water kami.

statement.en: Rain prayers took place at rivers, swamps, ponds, and deep pools regarded as Ryūjin’s abodes.

basis_claims.quote: Agricultural rituals, such as prayers for rain and rope pulls, were carried out using a straw rope shaped like a serpent-like dragon.

basis_claims.quote: They carried out festivals for ryūjin, celebrated as the kami of the sea and the kami of the dragon palace.

statement.id: Ryūjin dirayakan dalam festival sebagai kami laut dan istana naga.
statement.en: Festivals celebrated Ryūjin as kami of the sea and dragon palace.

basis_claims.quote: Der Drak (oder auch Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke und Gluswanz genannt) ist ein fliegender Hausgeist. Obwohl er äußerlich einem Drachen ähnelt, hat er mit diesem wohl nichts gemeinsam.

statement.id: Drak (juga disebut Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke, dan Gluswanz) adalah roh rumah terbang; meski tampak seperti naga, ia agaknya tak ada kaitannya dengan naga.
statement.en: The Drak (also called Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke and Gluswanz) is a flying house spirit; though it looks like a dragon it probably has nothing in common with one.

basis_claims.quote: Er ist in Nord- und Mitteldeutschland beheimatet, sowie auch in angrenzenden slawischen Gebieten und bringt dem Bauern durch den Kamin Korn, Getreide, Butter, Speck, Schinken und Gold. Daher wurde vielen wohlhabenden Bauern auch nachgesagt, dass sie einen Drak in ihren Diensten hätten.

statement.id: Drak berasal dari Jerman utara dan tengah (Nord- und Mitteldeutschland) serta wilayah Slavia di sekitarnya, dan membawa gandum, mentega, daging asap, ham, dan emas kepada petani lewat cerobong; karena itu banyak petani kaya diisukan memelihara Drak.
statement.en: The Drak is at home in northern and central Germany (Nord- und Mitteldeutschland) and adjacent Slavic areas and brings the farmer corn, grain, butter, bacon, ham and gold through the chimney; hence many wealthy farmers were said to have a Drak in service.

basis_claims.quote: Das Erscheinungsbild eines Drak ist das eines kleinen Drachen mit glühendem Schweif, mit dem er durch die Lüfte zieht. Im östlichen Pommern kennt man ihn als Alf und mancherorts auch als feurige Schlange mit Entenkopf oder als glühenden Kessel mit Schwanz.

statement.id: Drak berwujud naga kecil berekor menyala yang melayang di udara; di Pomerania (Pommern) timur ia dikenal sebagai Alf, dan di beberapa tempat sebagai ular api berkepala bebek atau kuali menyala berekor.
statement.en: The Drak looks like a small dragon with a glowing tail as it travels through the air; in eastern Pomerania (Pommern) it is called Alf, and in places a fiery snake with a duck's head or a glowing kettle with a tail.

basis_claims.quote: Drac létá vzduchem a do domu vstupuje skrze komín či díru ve střeše. Má podobu hořícího bidla, mužíčka v červené vestě, nebo zvířete jako kuře, kohout či ještěrka. Jindy vypadá jako ohnivá koule či planoucí hvězda. Je úzce spjat s ohněm, což vedlo k ztotožňování s ďáblem, a přebývá v krbu nebo hluboko v peci.

statement.id: Drac terbang di udara dan masuk rumah lewat cerobong atau lubang atap; ia berwujud batang menyala, lelaki kecil berompi merah, atau hewan seperti ayam dan kadal, kadang bola api; ia erat dengan api dan tinggal di perapian atau jauh di dalam tungku.
statement.en: Drac flies through the air and enters by the chimney or a hole in the roof; it takes the form of a burning pole, a little man in a red vest, or an animal such as a hen or lizard, at times a fireball; it is closely bound to fire and lives in the hearth or deep in the oven.

basis_claims.quote: Drac je získáván skrze smlouvu s ďáblem, ale může se zrodit jinými způsoby. Líhne se například z vejce bez žloutku, proto se má takové vejce vyhodit. ... Draca bylo nutno živit, podávaly se mu tak pokrmy jako koláče, maso, mléko nebo jáhlová kaše. Když není krmen, tak se mstí, typicky založením požáru.

statement.id: Drac diperoleh lewat perjanjian dengan iblis atau menetas dari telur tanpa kuning; ia harus diberi makan kue, daging, susu, atau bubur jawawut, dan bila tidak diberi makan ia membalas dendam, biasanya dengan menyulut kebakaran.
statement.en: Drac is gained through a pact with the devil or hatches from a yolkless egg; it must be fed cakes, meat, milk or millet porridge, and if unfed it takes revenge, usually by setting a fire.

statement.id: Umibōzu dapat diterjemahkan sebagai biksu laut.
statement.en: The name umibōzu is glossed as sea monk.

basis_claims.quote: Normally, umibōzu appears to sailors on calm seas which quickly turn tumultuous.

statement.id: Ia muncul di laut tenang yang kemudian bergolak.
statement.en: It appears on calm seas that turn rough.

basis_claims.quote: It either breaks the ship on emergence or demands a bucket or barrel from the sailors and proceeds to drown them.

statement.id: Ia dapat merusak kapal atau meminta wadah untuk menenggelamkannya.
statement.en: It may break or flood a ship.

basis_claims.quote: Utagawa Kuniyoshi's Tōkaidō gojyūsantugi: Kuwana depicts a sailor from Kuwana, named Tokuzo, who encounters a giant umi-bōzu offshore.

statement.id: Cetakan Kuniyoshi menampilkan Tokuzō bertemu umibōzu raksasa.
statement.en: Kuniyoshi depicts Tokuzō meeting a giant umibōzu.

tesso.depicted_variant: Written-tale giant rat manifestation of Raigo's vengeful spirit
visual_requirements: One giant rat
Natural rodent ears muzzle fur and naked tail
Iron-hard strong gnawing teeth and claws
Temple library sacred-book destruction
Vindictive frightening aura
tesso.aura: Embittered destructive revenge and frightening temple intrusion

basis_claims.quote: Tesso (鉄鼠) is a Japanese yōkai related to the vengeful spirit (onryō) of the Heian period monk Raigō and a mouse.

statement.id: Tesso adalah yōkai yang dikaitkan dengan tikus dan arwah pendendam biksu Raigō.
statement.en: Tesso is a rat-associated yōkai linked to the monk Raigō’s vengeful spirit.

basis_claims.quote: As a reward, Raigō requested for the construction of an ordination platform (kaidan) building for Mii-dera, but opposition forces from Enryaku-ji at Mount Hiei obstructed this and prevented it from being granted.

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, pembangunan balai penahbisan yang diminta Raigō dihalangi kuil saingannya.
statement.en: One tale says Raigō’s requested ordination hall was blocked by a rival temple.

basis_claims.quote: In the yomihon versions of the Heike Monogatari such as Enkyōhon (延慶本, alternatively read Enkeihon) and Nagatohon (長門本) and in the different book Genpei Jōsuiki, among other sources, the grudges of Raigō became a giant rat and ate away at the sacred books in Enryaku-ji.

statement.id: Beberapa versi tertulis menggambarkan dendamnya menjadi tikus raksasa yang merusak kitab suci.
statement.en: Some written versions turn his resentment into a giant rat that destroys sacred books.

basis_claims.quote: Its body was as hard as stone and its teeth and claws as strong as iron.

statement.id: Tikus gaib itu digambarkan bertubuh sekeras batu.
statement.en: The monstrous rat is described as having a stone-hard body.

visual_requirements: One natural black crow
Exactly three independent countable legs
Kumano mountain path and solar dawn
Dignified auspicious sacred guide aura

basis_claims.quote: This is a statue of the Yatagarasu, a three-legged crow from Japanese myth.

statement.id: Yatagarasu adalah gagak berkaki tiga dari mitologi Jepang.
statement.en: Yatagarasu is a three-legged crow from Japanese myth.

basis_claims.quote: In the ancient Japanese chronicles Kojiki and Nihon shoki, the Yatagarasu appeared as a servant of Amaterasu-no-Okami, the goddess of the sun.

statement.id: Kojiki dan Nihon Shoki menampilkannya sebagai pelayan Amaterasu.
statement.en: The Kojiki and Nihon Shoki portray it as Amaterasu’s servant.

basis_claims.quote: It was sent to guide the legendary first emperor Jimmu from Kumano to present-day Nara

statement.id: Ia diutus membimbing Jimmu dari Kumano ke Nara.
statement.en: It was sent to guide Jimmu from Kumano to Nara.

basis_claims.quote: The Yatagarasu is both a deity of guidance and a servant of the Kumano deities, including Amaterasu-no-Okami.

statement.id: Yatagarasu disebut dewa penuntun dan pelayan dewa-dewa Kumano.
statement.en: Yatagarasu is called a guiding deity and servant of Kumano deities.

kuraokami.depicted_variant: Serpent form of Kuraokami, consistent with De Visser's 1913 analysis of dragon/snake water deity; not a standardized horned dragon portrait
visual_requirements: Source-supported serpent form of rain/snow dragon-snake divinity
Continuous scaled serpent anatomy
No generic horns wings or limbs
Dark mountain valley pool and rain/snow
Majestic revered divine aura
kuraokami.aura: Ancient sacred water authority, immense tranquil reverent majesty

basis_claims.quote: Okami (淤加美神, Okami-no-kami) in the Kojiki, or in the Nihon Shoki: Kuraokami (闇龗) or Okami (龗), is a legendary Japanese dragon and Shinto deity of rain and snow.

statement.id: Kuraokami adalah dewa naga Jepang yang berkaitan dengan hujan dan salju.
statement.en: Kuraokami is a Japanese dragon deity associated with rain and snow.

basis_claims.quote: The name Kuraokami combines kura 闇 "dark; darkness; closed" and okami 龗 "dragon tutelary of water".

statement.id: Unsur pertama namanya dikaitkan dengan kegelapan.
statement.en: The first element of the name is associated with darkness.

basis_claims.quote: Then, the blood pooling on the hilt of Izanaki’s sword oozed from between his fingers. The deity that thereupon came into existence was named Kura okami no kami 闇淤加美 神. Next [appeared] Kura mitsuha no kami 闇御津羽神 (8).

statement.id: Versi Kojiki menghubungkan Kuraokami dengan darah yang menetes di antara jari Izanaki.
statement.en: The Kojiki version traces Kuraokami to blood dripping through Izanaki’s fingers.

additional_sources.title: Kifune Shrine: About Kifune Shrine
additional_sources.basis: Primary shrine account associates Kuraokami with dark abyss/valley and life-supplying water and rain.

additional_sources.title: Marinus Willem de Visser, The Dragon in China and Japan (1913), Book II chapter I, pp.135–136
additional_sources.basis: Primary scholarly monograph describes original Japanese water gods as serpent- or dragon-shaped and identifies Kura-okami as dragon or snake and rain/snow divinity.

amikiri.depicted_variant: Sekien scorpionlike hybrid image, without later net-cutting story assertion
visual_requirements: Sekien scorpionlike crustacean-serpent-bird hybrid
Two pincer claws and birdlike beak
Full segmented curved body framed
Strange uncanny understated aura

basis_claims.quote: is a Japanese yōkai depicted in the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō by Toriyama Sekien.

statement.id: Amikiri adalah yōkai dalam buku Sekien.
statement.en: Amikiri is a yōkai in Sekien’s book.

basis_claims.quote: depicts a scorpion-like creature (or a cross between a serpent, bird or a lobster with pincer claws similar to that of a crab or a scorpion)

statement.id: Gambar Sekien menunjukkan bentuk mirip kalajengking dengan capit.
statement.en: Sekien depicts a scorpionlike being with pincers.

basis_claims.quote: but since Sekien supplies no explanatory text, it is not certain what kind of yōkai it is.

statement.id: Sekien tidak memberi teks penjelas tentang jenis makhluk.
statement.en: Sekien gives no explanation of the creature’s nature.

basis_claims.quote: Toriyama Sekien does not include a kamikiri in his catalogs, but does draw a scorpion-like yōkai labeled amikiri, or “net cutter.”

statement.id: Foster membedakan kamikiri dari amikiri dalam katalog Sekien.
statement.en: Foster distinguishes kamikiri from Sekien’s amikiri.

karura.depicted_variant: 734 Karura statue-inspired armored birdlike warrior, not Gigaku mask
visual_requirements: Armored birdlike humanoid warrior
Pronounced beak and bird eyes with humanlike ears/hair
Two arms and two legs, selected statue variant
Dignified sacred Buddhist guardian aura

basis_claims.quote: Karura is one of the Eight Kinds of Mythological Beings, representing a bird or birdlike being that devours snakes.

statement.id: Karura adalah makhluk mirip burung pemakan ular dari Delapan Golongan Makhluk Mitologis.
statement.en: Karura is a snake-eating birdlike being among the Eight Kinds.

basis_claims.quote: It is derived from Hindu, Buddhist and Jain mythology in India, and based on Garuda, the mythical bird of Hinduism.

statement.id: Karura berasal dari Garuda dalam mitologi India.
statement.en: Karura derives from India’s mythical Garuda.

basis_claims.quote: Karura is thus depicted as an armored warrior with a prominent beak and avian eyes but humanlike ears and hair.

statement.id: Patung menampilkan prajurit berparuh dan bermata burung tetapi bertelinga serta berambut manusia.
statement.en: The statue has an armored birdlike warrior with humanlike ears and hair.

basis_claims.quote: Karura is a deified bird. In Indian mythology, the Karura was a sacred bird that ate the poisonous snake. When this deity was taken into Buddhism, it became one of the gods who guard the Buddhist faith.

statement.id: Burung suci pemakan ular menjadi pelindung dalam Buddhisme.
statement.en: The sacred snake-eating bird became a Buddhist guardian.

basis_claims.quote: The work is dated to 734 and was made by the hollow-core dry-lacquer sculpting technique.

statement.id: Patung Karura dibuat pada 734.
statement.en: The Karura statue is dated to 734.

waira.depicted_variant: Source-preserved Edo scroll upper-body form; hind-body anatomy deliberately left unseen
visual_requirements: Bulky grotesque lumpy upper-body form
Two forelimbs with exactly one thick claw each
Lower/back half concealed because unknown
Mountain habitat
Uncanny frightening looming aura

basis_claims.quote: The waira (わいら) is a Japanese yōkai from Japanese emaki (handscrolls) such as the Hyakkai Zukan by Sawaki Suushi and books such as Gazu Hyakki Yagyō (1776) by Sekien Toriyama.

statement.id: Waira adalah yōkai yang digambar dalam gulungan dan buku bergambar Jepang.
statement.en: Waira is a yōkai pictured in Japanese scrolls and illustrated books.

basis_claims.quote: Lee Library, Brigham Young University) it is depicted with the body of a giant ox and thick sharp claws growing on each of its front legs.

statement.id: Gambar-gambarnya memberi tubuh mirip sapi dan cakar depan yang tajam.
statement.en: Pictures give it an ox-like body and sharp front claws.

basis_claims.quote: Each of these sources have no explanatory text besides their name, and furthermore there do not exist any documents recording any folk legends about them, so it is unknown what kind of yōkai these were intending to depict.

statement.id: Gambar lama tidak menjelaskan sifatnya, dan catatan rakyat yang jelas belum ditemukan.
statement.en: The old pictures do not explain its nature, and clear folk records are lacking.

basis_claims.quote: All of the pictures depict only the upper body, and there have been no pictures found that depict its lower half, so it is unknown what its whole body looks like.

statement.id: Gambar awal yang dibahas hanya menampilkan bagian atas tubuhnya.
statement.en: Only its upper body is shown in the early pictures discussed.

basis_claims.quote: Behavior : Waira live deep in the mountains, near heavily wooded temples and shrines.

statement.id: Kisah belakangan menempatkannya di pegunungan berhutan dekat tempat ibadah.
statement.en: A later account places it in wooded mountains near religious sites.

additional_sources.title: BYU Library Bakemono: Waira
additional_sources.basis: Institution describes exactly two arms each with one claw and never-depicted back half; visually inspected institution's Edo illustration for lumpy head, bulging eyes and broad muzzle.

feldgeister.depicted_variant: Human-shaped Corn Mother among the last harvest stalks
visual_requirements: Human-shaped Corn Mother among the last harvest stalks
Coherent anatomy and documented mythic scene
feldgeister.aura: Presence through source-backed form and physical scene; no generic glow, ribbons or magical mist.

basis_claims.quote: During harvest season Feldgeister flee deeper into the fields to escape the mowers. With the last cornstalks the corn spirit becomes trapped. Either it is killed by cutting the grain heads, threshing the corn or it is brought to the village in a ceremonial manner, shaped as a corn doll. Direct contact to the Feldgeist causes illness.

statement.id: Feldgeister (Feldgeist, Korndämonen) adalah roh gandum dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang sering juga roh angin; saat panen mereka lari makin dalam ke ladang, terperangkap di batang terakhir, lalu dibunuh dengan dipotong atau diirik, atau dibawa ke desa dengan upacara sebagai boneka gandum; sentuhan langsung menyebabkan sakit.
statement.en: Feldgeister (Feldgeist, Korndämonen) are corn spirits of German folklore, often also wind spirits; at harvest they flee deeper into the field, are trapped in the last stalks, then killed by cutting or threshing, or brought ceremonially to the village as a corn doll; direct contact causes illness.

basis_claims.quote: The Roggenwolf ("rye wolf"), Getreidewolf ("grain wolf") or Kornwolf ("corn wolf") is a field spirit shaped as a wolf. The Roggenwolf steals children and feeds on them.

statement.id: Roggenwolf ("serigala gandum hitam") adalah roh ladang berwujud serigala yang mencuri dan memakan anak-anak; contoh lain mencakup Roggenmuhme, Hafermann, dan Kornkind yang berwujud manusia.
statement.en: The Roggenwolf ('rye wolf') is a wolf-shaped field spirit that steals and eats children; other examples include the human-shaped Roggenmuhme, Hafermann and Kornkind.

basis_claims.quote: Die Anwesenheit eines Korndämons wird im Wogen des Korns gesehen und findet sich auch in Redensarten wie „Die Kornmutter ist im Feld“ wieder.

statement.id: Kehadiran setan gandum terlihat pada gandum yang bergelombang dan tercermin dalam ungkapan seperti "Ibu Gandum (Kornmutter) ada di ladang" (Corn Mother).
statement.en: A corn demon's presence is seen in the waving of the grain and appears in sayings like 'the Corn Mother (Kornmutter) is in the field'.

artistic_changes: Painterly square composition
Clothing, weather and exact setting details are editorial unless identified in claims

presentation_revision.rationale: Replaces ordinary animal presentation with Human-shaped Corn Mother among the last harvest stalks

visual_requirements: No facial eyes
One open eye in each palm
Old blind-guildsman-like figure

basis_claims.quote: Tenome (手の目, eyes of hand, or rather hand eyes) is a Japanese yōkai that appeared in the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō by Toriyama Sekien.

statement.id: Tenome adalah yōkai Jepang yang digambar Toriyama Sekien.
statement.en: Tenome is a Japanese yōkai illustrated by Toriyama Sekien.

basis_claims.quote: They appear as a zatō (a kind of member of the blind persons' guild such as the tōdōza or a ranking of members of related groups such the Anma, moxibustion practitions, and members of the biwa hōshi, among other organizations) with both eyes not on the face, but on the palm of each hand.

statement.id: Ia menyerupai anggota perkumpulan orang tunanetra dengan mata di telapak tangan, bukan di wajah.
statement.en: It resembles a blind guildsman with eyes in the palms rather than the face.

basis_claims.quote: Once, a man went on a trial of guts (or "test of courage") to the graveyard at Shichijogawara in Kyoto when a monster who appeared to be an old person around 80 years in age came after him, and this monster had eyeballs on each palm of the hand.

statement.id: Satu kisah menempatkan perjumpaan dengannya di pemakaman Kyoto.
statement.en: One tale places an encounter in a Kyoto graveyard.

isonade.depicted_variant: Ehon Hyaku Monogatari submerged-body barbed-tail form
visual_requirements: Sharklike submerged body with long tail
Only barbed hooked tail fin above water
Coastal Japanese sea and boat scale
Stealthy dangerous predatory aura

basis_claims.quote: The Isonade (磯撫で; "beach stroker") is an enormous, shark-like sea monster said to live off the coast of Matsuura and other places in Western Japan.

statement.id: Isonade adalah monster laut mirip hiu dalam cerita Jepang barat.
statement.en: Isonade is a shark-like sea monster in western Japanese lore.

basis_claims.quote: イソナデは尾の長い鮫。磯端で尾で打つ。海辺で死んだ人がいると「磯ナデになでられたんだろう」などという。

statement.id: Catatan Kumano menggambarkan Isonade sebagai hiu berekor panjang yang memukul tepi pantai.
statement.en: A Kumano record describes Isonade as a long-tailed shark striking the shore.

basis_claims.quote: According to the Ehon Hyaku Monogatari, its body has never been seen, as it is always "hidden beneath the waves, save for its huge tail fin which is covered in small barbs."

statement.id: Menurut Ehon Hyaku Monogatari, tubuhnya tersembunyi di bawah air kecuali sirip ekor berduri.
statement.en: Ehon Hyaku Monogatari says its body stays underwater except for a barbed tail fin.

basis_claims.quote: It approaches boats stealthily and uses its hooked tail to snare sailors and drag them into the sea, where it devours them.

statement.id: Sebuah versi menyebut Isonade menangkap pelaut dengan ekor berkait dan menyeretnya ke laut.
statement.en: One version says Isonade hooks sailors with its tail and drags them into the sea.

nuribotoke.depicted_variant: Edo scroll black back-hair form; not debated catfish-tail form
visual_requirements: Pitch-dark animated humanlike corpse
Both eyeballs clearly dangling below sockets
Long black back-hair variant
Household Buddhist altar
Disturbing eerie corpse-spirit menace without gore

basis_claims.quote: The Nuribotoke (塗仏) is a yōkai found in Japanese yōkai emaki such as the Hyakkai Zukan by Sawaki Suushi.

statement.id: Nuribotoke adalah yōkai yang digambar dalam gulungan makhluk gaib Jepang.
statement.en: Nuribotoke is a yōkai pictured in Japanese supernatural scrolls.

basis_claims.quote: They are also depicted in the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō by Toriyama Sekien.

statement.id: Toriyama Sekien juga menggambarnya dalam kumpulan ilustrasi.
statement.en: Toriyama Sekien also depicted it in an illustrated collection.

basis_claims.quote: They are depicted as an animated corpse with darkened skin and dangling eyeballs.

statement.id: Gambarnya menyerupai mayat hidup berkulit gelap.
statement.en: Its image resembles a dark-skinned animated corpse.

basis_claims.quote: Occasionally they try to trick foolish humans by giving false prophecies.

statement.id: Kisah belakangan menyebut ia memberikan ramalan menipu.
statement.en: A later account gives it deceptive predictions.

basis_claims.quote: Nuribotoke must return to the butsudan before sunrise, and they vanish altogether during the day.

statement.id: Kisah itu menyebut ia kembali ke altar rumah sebelum fajar.
statement.en: That account says it returns to the household altar before dawn.

additional_sources.title: BYU Library Bakemono: Nuribotoke
additional_sources.basis: Institution documents pitch-black animated corpse, dangling eyeballs, emergence from open butsudan and Edo scroll black-hair appendage variant.

visual_requirements: Green-skinned hideous river hag
Long tangled hair and sharp teeth
Malevolent aquatic duckweed predator aura

basis_claims.quote: Jenny Greenteeth a.k.a. Wicked Jenny, Ginny Greenteeth and Grinteeth is a figure in English folklore. A river-hag, similar to Peg Powler and derived from the grindylow, she would pull children or the elderly into the water and drown them.

statement.id: Jenny Greenteeth (Wicked Jenny, Ginny Greenteeth, Grinteeth) sosok cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), nenek sihir sungai mirip Peg Powler, dari grindylow (Grindylow), menenggelamkan anak dan orang tua; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: Jenny Greenteeth (Wicked Jenny, Ginny Greenteeth, Grinteeth) is an English folklore river-hag like Peg Powler, from the grindylow, drowning children and the elderly.

basis_claims.quote: The name is also used to describe pondweed or duckweed, which can form a continuous mat over the surface of a small body of water, making it misleading and potentially treacherous, especially to unwary children. With this meaning the name is common around Liverpool and southwest Lancashire.

statement.id: Nama juga untuk duckweed yang menutupi kolam; umum di Liverpool dan Lancashire barat daya.
statement.en: The name is also used for duckweed covering ponds; common around Liverpool and southwest Lancashire.

basis_claims.quote: Jenny Greenteeth was often described as green-skinned, with long hair, and sharp teeth. She is called Jinny Greenteeth in Lancashire and north Staffordshire but in Cheshire and Shropshire she is called Wicked Jenny, Ginny Greenteeth or Jeannie Greenteeth.

statement.id: Berkulit hijau, berambut panjang, bergigi tajam; Jinny Greenteeth di Lancashire dan Staffordshire; Wicked Jenny, Ginny, Jeannie Greenteeth di Cheshire dan Shropshire.
statement.en: Green-skinned, long-haired, sharp-toothed; Jinny Greenteeth in Lancashire and Staffordshire; Wicked Jenny, Ginny, Jeannie Greenteeth in Cheshire and Shropshire.

yamawaro.depicted_variant: Upright one-eyed mountain humanoid, Wakan Sansai Zue short torso/long legs
visual_requirements: Exactly one central eye
Short torso and two long legs, upright humanoid
Deep Kyushu mountain habitat
Wild watchful mysterious mountain aura

basis_claims.quote: Yamawaro (山童; or yamawarau) is a yōkai (spirit) said to appear in mountains in Western Japan, starting in the Kyūshū region.

statement.id: Yamawaro adalah yōkai gunung yang diceritakan di Jepang barat dan Kyūshū.
statement.en: Yamawaro is a mountain yōkai reported in western Japan and Kyūshū.

basis_claims.quote: According to the Edo-period Wakan Sansai Zue, yamawaro lives in the depths of the mountains in Kyushu.

statement.id: Wakan Sansai Zue menempatkannya jauh di pegunungan.
statement.en: The Wakan Sansai Zue places it deep in the mountains.

basis_claims.quote: The Wakan Sansai Zue states that yamawaro has a short torso, walks upright on two long legs, and speaks in human language.

statement.id: Buku itu menggambarkannya berjalan tegak dan berbicara seperti manusia.
statement.en: That book describes upright walking and human speech.

basis_claims.quote: A yamawaro’s most distinguishing feature is the single eye in the middle of its head.

statement.id: Gambaran umum memberinya satu mata di tengah kepala.
statement.en: A common depiction gives it one central eye.

yosuzume.depicted_variant: Mountain-path night sparrow; ominous variant without asserting all regional versions are harmful
visual_requirements: Small sparrow-like bird
Ordinary coherent bird anatomy
Nocturnal mountain trail
Open chirping beak
Eerie ambiguous omen aura
yosuzume.aura: Uncanny startling nocturnal omen, ambiguous rather than monstrous

basis_claims.quote: Yosuzume (夜雀, "Night-Sparrow") are bird yōkai

statement.id: Yosuzume adalah yōkai burung yang disebut burung pipit malam.
statement.en: Yosuzume are bird yōkai known as night sparrows.

basis_claims.quote: As indicated by their name, they are a yōkai that appear in the night and chirp "chi, chi, chi" like a sparrow, and are said to pass in front of people who walk along mountain trails.

statement.id: Mereka muncul malam hari dan berkicau seperti burung pipit di jalur pegunungan.
statement.en: They appear at night and chirp like sparrows on mountain trails.

basis_claims.quote: Also, it is said that if one carelessly caught them, then one gets afflicted with nyctalopia.

statement.id: Satu kepercayaan menyebut penangkapan burung itu menyebabkan rabun senja.
statement.en: One belief says catching them causes night blindness.

basis_claims.quote: In reverse, in Wakayama Prefecture, they were not bad luck, and while possessed by a night sparrow, it was proof that a wolf was giving protection from the monsters of the mountain.

statement.id: Di Wakayama, keberadaannya dapat menandakan serigala pelindung.
statement.en: In Wakayama, their presence can indicate a protective wolf.

basis_claims.quote: By themselves they don’t do any particular harm other than startling people; however they are a sign of very bad luck and are thought to bring terrible evil to those whom they swarm around.

statement.id: Kisah lain menafsirkan keberadaan mereka sebagai pertanda sial.
statement.en: Other accounts interpret their presence as bad luck.

basis_claims.quote: Their call is mysteriously only ever heard by a single individual, even when traveling in groups.

statement.id: Satu kisah daerah menyebut hanya satu pelancong dalam kelompok yang mendengar suaranya.
statement.en: A regional account says only one traveler in a group hears their call.

basis_claims.quote: Amemasu (雨鱒（アメマス）) or Ō-amemasu (大アメマス) (rain trout) is a giant whale- or fish-like creature from Ainu folklore.

statement.id: Amemasu adalah makhluk raksasa mirip ikan atau paus dalam cerita rakyat Ainu.
statement.en: Amemasu is a giant fishlike or whalelike being in Ainu folklore.

basis_claims.quote: Some of the largest amemasu are said to live in Lake Mashū and Lake Shikotsu in Hokkaidō, with smaller ones inhabiting lakes throughout northern areas of Honshu.

statement.id: Kisah-kisah menempatkan sosok berukuran besar di danau-danau Hokkaidō.
statement.en: Accounts place large examples in lakes of Hokkaidō.

basis_claims.quote: The amemasu are known for capsizing boats, creating earthquakes, and causing other natural disasters.

statement.id: Ia dikaitkan dengan perahu terbalik dan bencana alam.
statement.en: It is associated with overturned boats and natural disasters.

basis_claims.quote: Yōkai amemasu can grow to colossal sizes, sometimes spanning an entire lake from head to tail.

statement.id: Sebagian kisah memberinya panjang yang membentang melintasi satu danau.
statement.en: Some accounts give it a length spanning an entire lake.

Broad clothing-like body expansion
Enveloping a boat at sea
Northern Kyoto coastal folklore context
Engulfing threatening sea predator aura

statement.id: Koromodako adalah yōkai gurita dalam cerita rakyat Jepang.
statement.en: Koromodako is an octopus yōkai in Japanese folklore.

basis_claims.quote: Although in the guise of a small octopus, it is said to expand and envelop boats and people.

statement.id: Ia dapat membesar dari wujud kecil dan menyelubungi perahu.
statement.en: It can expand from a small form and envelop boats.

statement.id: Legendanya dikaitkan dengan Kyoto utara.
statement.en: Its legends are associated with northern Kyoto.

basis_claims.quote: As the name indicates, koromo-dako is an octopus-like yōkai that appear small at first, but expands widely like a piece of clothing when a boat arrives, and sinks both vessel and humans in the sea.

statement.id: Ia konon menenggelamkan kapal beserta penumpangnya.
statement.en: It is said to sink vessels and their passengers.

basis_claims.quote: After feeding, the koromodako shrinks down to its tiny size, impossible to trace.

statement.id: Setelah makan, ia kembali ke wujud kecil.
statement.en: After feeding, it returns to a tiny form.

sunekosuri.depicted_variant: Dog-shaped Okayama local form with shin-rubbing behavior
visual_requirements: Small dog-shaped spirit with four legs and one tail
Rubbing traveler shins as defining behavior
Rainy Japanese alley
Harmless uncanny mischievous aura

basis_claims.quote: The sunekosuri (meaning "rub against lower legs") is a Japanese yōkai.

statement.id: Sunekosuri adalah yōkai Jepang yang namanya merujuk pada gesekan pada kaki.
statement.en: Sunekosuri is a Japanese yōkai whose name refers to rubbing against legs.

basis_claims.quote: Stories are told of it in Okayama Prefecture and is said to get in the way of people's paths as they walk.

statement.id: Cerita Okayama menggambarkannya menghalangi pejalan kaki.
statement.en: Okayama tales describe it obstructing pedestrians.

basis_claims.quote: According to folklore from Ibara in Nankaichi town within this city, sunekosuri would appear beside a shrine called Iryō-dō, and it would move through the space between the legs of pedestrians and would take the shape of a dog.

statement.id: Satu kisah setempat memberinya wujud anjing.
statement.en: One local account gives it a dog’s shape.

basis_claims.quote: They appear on rainy nights in streets and alleys where people travel.

statement.id: Ia konon muncul di jalan dan gang pada malam hujan.
statement.en: It is said to appear on rainy nights in streets and alleys.

basis_claims.quote: They rub against their shins, weave in and out of their legs, nuzzle against the knees, and otherwise make it difficult to walk.

statement.id: Gerakannya di antara kaki manusia menyulitkan orang berjalan.
statement.en: Its movements between people’s legs make walking difficult.

basis_claims.quote: They do not intentionally cause any harm to humans, although occasionally their rubbing is strong enough to make a person stumble or even knock them down.

statement.id: Ia tidak digambarkan sengaja mencelakai, meskipun dapat membuat orang tersandung.
statement.en: It is not portrayed as deliberately harmful, though it can make people stumble.

ikuchi.depicted_variant: Edo sea-serpent crossing boat and dripping oil
visual_requirements: Exceptionally long limbless sea serpent
Body crosses wooden boat and leaves dark viscous oil
Hitachi deep sea setting
Ominous immense slow sea menace
ikuchi.aura: ominous immense slow dangerous sea presence

basis_claims.quote: Ikuchi is a yōkai of the sea serpent type in Japanese legend.

statement.id: Ikuchi adalah yōkai ular laut dalam legenda Jepang.
statement.en: Ikuchi is a sea-serpent yōkai in Japanese legend.

basis_claims.quote: is an extremely long fish dwelling in the deep waters off Hitachi Province (now Ibaraki Prefecture).

statement.id: Satu kisah menempatkan makhluk itu di perairan dalam lepas Hitachi.
statement.en: An account places the creature in deep waters off Hitachi.

basis_claims.quote: It has only been spotted at night, sometimes rearing out of water and slinking over a ship, taking a long time to complete its passage, and leaving a residue of viscous oil.

statement.id: Ia melintas di atas kapal dan meninggalkan minyak kental.
statement.en: It crosses over ships and leaves viscous oil behind.

basis_claims.quote: The sheer amount of oil needs to be dumped overboard lest the ship sink.

statement.id: Pelaut dalam cerita harus membuang minyak itu agar kapal tidak tenggelam.
statement.en: Sailors in the story must remove the oil to keep the ship from sinking.

basis_claims.quote: Ikuchi are so long—many kilometers, by some accounts—that it can take hours for an entire one to slither over a boat.

statement.id: Panjangnya yang luar biasa membuat lintasannya di atas kapal berlangsung berjam-jam.
statement.en: Its extreme length makes a crossing over a ship last for hours.

selkolla.depicted_variant: Selkolla in the defining seal-headed-woman variant, standing on an Icelandic coastal path.
visual_requirements: One woman with seal head
Human woman's body fully clothed
Recognizable seal muzzle and whiskers
Menacing Icelandic spirit aura
selkolla.aura: Uncanny menacing supernatural deceiver, unsettling predatory calm rather than a friendly seal.

basis_claims.quote: Selkolla (literally 'seal-head') is a supernatural being in Icelandic folklore. She is described as a fair woman that is sometimes seen having the head of a seal. She is most prominently attested as an antagonist of Bishop Guðmundur Arason (1161–1237). Tales of Selkolla are noted for combining Christian ideas with concepts found in Scandinavian non-Christian traditions.

statement.id: Selkolla (harfiah "kepala anjing laut") adalah makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Islandia (Icelandic), perempuan cantik yang kadang terlihat berkepala anjing laut; ia terutama tercatat sebagai lawan Uskup Guðmundur Arason (1161–1237), dan kisahnya memadukan gagasan Kristen (Christian) dengan konsep tradisi Skandinavia (Scandinavian) non-Kristen.
statement.en: Selkolla ('seal-head') is a supernatural being of Icelandic folklore, a fair woman sometimes seen with a seal's head; she is chiefly attested as an antagonist of Bishop Guðmundur Arason (1161–1237), and her tales mix Christian ideas with Scandinavian non-Christian concepts.

basis_claims.quote: It is then said that a certain woman is "newly arrived in the district, sometimes with an ordinary face but sometimes with a seal's head. This devil walked about as boldly by day as by night, for which reason this midday-devil was called Selkolla in the district".

statement.id: Lalu disebutkan seorang perempuan baru tiba di daerah itu, kadang berwajah biasa, kadang berkepala anjing laut; setan ini berkeliaran berani siang maupun malam, sehingga "setan tengah hari" ini disebut Selkolla.
statement.en: Then a woman is said to have newly arrived in the district, sometimes with an ordinary face, sometimes with a seal's head; this devil walked boldly by day and night, so this midday-devil was called Selkolla.

basis_claims.quote: First, in the guise of the farmer's wife, she tries to entice him into having sex. When he realises what is actually going on, he tries to turn for home, but Selkolla bars his way

statement.id: Mula-mula, menyamar sebagai istri petani, ia mencoba merayunya; ketika petani menyadarinya dan hendak pulang, Selkolla menghalangi jalannya.
statement.en: First, disguised as the farmer's wife, she tries to seduce him; when he realises and turns for home, Selkolla bars his way.

basis_claims.quote: Selkolla er kynjavera í íslenskri þjóðtrú. Hún er falleg kona, en sést stundum með selshöfuð.

statement.id: Selkolla adalah makhluk ajaib dalam kepercayaan rakyat Islandia (íslenskri); ia perempuan cantik yang kadang terlihat berkepala anjing laut.
statement.en: Selkolla is a wondrous being of Icelandic (íslenskri) folk belief; a beautiful woman, sometimes seen with a seal's head.

ulm-sparrow.depicted_variant: The sparrow in the humorous Ulm legend carrying a nest twig toward its nest, rather than the different dove statue on the minster.
visual_requirements: One recognizable natural sparrow
Twig carried toward nest
Old Ulm architectural setting
Clever benign humorous folklore atmosphere
ulm-sparrow.aura: Bright clever benign folk-tale helper, warm and modest.

basis_claims.quote: Der Sage nach sollen die Ulmer beim Bau des Münsters einen besonders großen Balken angekarrt haben. Sie schafften es aber nicht, ihn durch das Stadttor zu bringen. Als sie kurz davor waren, das Tor einzureißen, sahen sie einen Spatzen, der einen Zweig im Schnabel trug, um diesen in sein Nest einzubauen.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, warga Ulm membawa balok sangat besar untuk membangun katedral (Münsters) tetapi tak bisa memasukkannya lewat gerbang kota; saat hendak merobohkan gerbang, mereka melihat burung gereja membawa ranting untuk sarangnya.
statement.en: Legend says the people of Ulm carted a huge beam for building the minster (Münsters) but could not get it through the city gate; about to tear the gate down, they saw a sparrow carrying a twig for its nest.

basis_claims.quote: Dieser Spatz drehte den Zweig vor dem Einbau längsseits. Da ging dann wohl auch den Ulmern ein Licht auf und sie legten den Balken der Länge nach auf ihren Karren und nicht quer, wie bisher.

statement.id: Burung gereja itu memutar rantingnya memanjang sebelum menyusunnya; warga Ulm pun tersadar dan meletakkan balok memanjang di gerobak, bukan melintang seperti sebelumnya; Ulmer Spatz adalah lambang (Wahrzeichen) Ulm.
statement.en: The sparrow turned the twig lengthwise before building it in; the Ulmers then saw the light and laid the beam lengthwise on their cart rather than across as before; the Ulmer Spatz is a landmark (Wahrzeichen) of Ulm.

basis_claims.quote: Diese humoristische Sage ist seit dem zweiten Viertel des 19. Jahrhunderts nachweisbar.

statement.id: Legenda jenaka ini dapat dilacak sejak perempat kedua abad ke-19.
statement.en: This humorous legend is traceable from the second quarter of the 19th century.

nobusuma.depicted_variant: Nobusuma flying-squirrel yōkai in recorded fire-breathing variant: natural gliding squirrel with membranes stretched between four limbs, one bushy tail, emits a SMALL clear orange flame from its mouth over an Edo woodland footpath. Restrained actual flame only supportedmagic; no glowing entirebody, no dragonwings/horns or extralimbs.
visual_requirements: Cited variant/episode readable
Coherent anatomy
No generic aura

basis_claims.quote: which some say is a transmuted bat, and others a flying squirrel.

statement.id: Kisahnya berbeda antara kelelawar yang berubah dan tupai terbang.
statement.en: Accounts differ between a transformed bat and a flying squirrel.

basis_claims.quote: As for it allegedly consuming flame (or smoke from a fire), a source explains that it engages in a sort of fire-eating and -breathing behavior after chomping the tip off a lit torch.

statement.id: Satu gambaran memberinya perilaku memakan dan menyemburkan api.
statement.en: A description gives it fire-eating and fire-breathing behavior.

Turning pillow beside futon
Two arms and legs
Eerie nocturnal mischievous aura
makuragaeshi.aura: eerie nocturnal mischief with stern guardian appearance

basis_claims.quote: The makuragaeshi (枕返し or 反枕, “pillow flip”) is a kind of Japanese spirit or yōkai.

statement.id: Makuragaeshi adalah roh atau yōkai Jepang.
statement.en: Makuragaeshi is a Japanese spirit or yōkai.

basis_claims.quote: They would come at night to one's pillow side and flip over the pillow.

statement.id: Ia konon membalik bantal orang yang tidur pada malam hari.
statement.en: It is said to turn over a sleeper’s pillow at night.

basis_claims.quote: In the Edo Period collection of yōkai pictures, the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō, they are depicted as a miniature Niō.

statement.id: Ilustrasi zaman Edo menggambarkannya sebagai penjaga Niō kecil.
statement.en: An Edo-period illustration depicts a miniature Niō guardian.

visual_requirements: Iron cooking pot head
Hand holding votive tablet
Animated household-object aura

basis_claims.quote: Narigama (鳴釜; or Narikama, Narukama) or Kamanari (釜鳴) is a Japanese yōkai depicted in Toriyama Sekien's yōkai art collection Gazu Hyakki Tsurezure Bukuro.

statement.id: Narigama adalah yōkai yang digambar oleh Toriyama Sekien.
statement.en: Narigama is a yōkai illustrated by Toriyama Sekien.

basis_claims.quote: It is depicted as a hairy figure wearing a kama (iron pot) on its head and holding an ema (votive tablet) in its hand.

statement.id: Gambarnya memakai panci besi di kepala.
statement.en: Its image wears an iron cooking pot on its head.

basis_claims.quote: It is depicted as a hairy figure wearing a kama (iron pot) on its head and holding an ema (votive tablet) in its hand.

statement.id: Sosok itu memegang papan persembahan.
statement.en: The figure holds a votive tablet.

basis_claims.quote: The terms Narigama and Kamanari themselves refer to Shinto rituals in which fortune (good or bad luck) is judged based on the sound produced when a pot is heated with fire, or to folk beliefs that view a pot making unexpected sounds as an omen of good or bad luck.

statement.id: Namanya juga merujuk pada ramalan melalui bunyi panci yang dipanaskan.
statement.en: Its name also refers to divination through the sound of a heated pot.

kuzuryu.depicted_variant: Revered Kuzuryu Daimyojin nine-headed Lake Ashi water dragon
visual_requirements: Exactly nine heads on one shared serpentine body
Wingless water dragon
Lake Ashi/Hakone context
Majestic sacred deity aura
kuzuryu.aura: majestic reverent sacred protective water deity

basis_claims.quote: Kuzuryū (九頭龍, nine-headed dragon), or Kuzuryūshin (九頭龍神, nine-headed dragon god) is a deity that appears in folklore and legends of various parts of Japan, including, for example, Hakone (Kanagawa), Nagano Prefecture and Fukui Prefecture.

statement.id: Kuzuryū adalah dewa naga berkepala sembilan dari Jepang.
statement.en: Kuzuryū is a Japanese nine-headed dragon deity.

basis_claims.quote: In many cases, the Kuzuryū is associated with water.

statement.id: Naga itu biasanya dikaitkan dengan air.
statement.en: The dragon is commonly associated with water.

basis_claims.quote: During the Nara period, a legend arose that the Nine-headed Dragon had settled in Lake Ashi in Hakone, and that it demanded a sacrifice.

statement.id: Legenda Hakone menempatkan naga penuntut kurban di Danau Ashi.
statement.en: The Hakone legend places a dragon demanding sacrifices in Lake Ashi.

basis_claims.quote: As a result of this legend, the dragon came to be worshipped as Kuzuryū Daimyōjin (九頭竜大明神, "Great God Nine-Headed Dragon).

statement.id: Legenda itu menghasilkan pemujaan sebagai Kuzuryū Daimyōjin.
statement.en: The legend leads to worship as Kuzuryū Daimyōjin.

basis_claims.quote: Like most dragons, kuzuryū have power over rain and water.

statement.id: Kisah belakangan memberi para naga kuasa atas hujan dan air.
statement.en: A later account assigns the dragons power over rain and water.

visual_requirements: Blue-white ghost fire with face
Undamaged conifer forest
No solid body

basis_claims.quote: The tsurubebi (釣瓶火, "bucket fire") is a fire yōkai that appears in the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō by Toriyama Sekien.

statement.id: Tsurubebi adalah yōkai api yang digambar oleh Toriyama Sekien.
statement.en: Tsurubebi is a fire yōkai depicted by Toriyama Sekien.

basis_claims.quote: Tsurubebi are small tree spirits which appear at night, deep in coniferous forests.

statement.id: Satu kisah menggambarkannya sebagai roh pohon malam hari di hutan konifer.
statement.en: One account portrays it as a nocturnal tree spirit in coniferous forests.

basis_claims.quote: They take the form of blueish-white orbs of fire which bob up and down in the branches, occasionally dropping to the forest floor and floating back up into the trees.

statement.id: Ia muncul sebagai api putih kebiruan yang bergerak antara cabang dan tanah.
statement.en: It appears as bluish-white fire moving between branches and the ground.

basis_claims.quote: Sometimes the vague shape of a human or bestial face can be seen in the flames.

statement.id: Wajah manusia atau hewan kadang terlihat di dalam apinya.
statement.en: A human or animal face may be visible in its flames.

basis_claims.quote: Their flames produce no heat and do not burn the trees that they live in; nor do these yokai pose any other known threat.

statement.id: Apinya digambarkan tidak menghasilkan panas atau merusak pohon.
statement.en: Its fire is described as producing no heat or damage to trees.

visual_requirements: Horse-headed clothed yokai
Humanlike sitting posture
Eerie former-owner household haunting

basis_claims.quote: is one of the 16 yōkai depicted in the Tosa Obake Zōshi, drawn during the Edo period; it appears as a skeletal, flaming horse, claimed to be the spirit of a horse that perished in a fire.

statement.id: Bakotsu adalah yōkai kuda yang digambar dalam Tosa Obake Zōshi zaman Edo.
statement.en: Bakotsu is a horse yōkai pictured in the Edo-period Tosa Obake Zōshi.

basis_claims.quote: 'horse bone') is one of the 16 yōkai depicted in the Tosa Obake Zōshi, drawn during the Edo period;

statement.id: Namanya secara harfiah berarti tulang kuda.
statement.en: Its name literally means horse bone.

basis_claims.quote: Behavior : Bakotsu are formed from horses that burned to death in fires.

statement.id: Ia konon muncul dari kuda yang mati dalam kebakaran.
statement.en: It is said to arise from a horse that dies in a fire.

basis_claims.quote: Bakotsu look like horses, however they also have several human-like characteristics–they wear clothes and sit on their haunches like a person.

statement.id: Satu kisah memberinya pakaian dan posisi duduk seperti manusia.
statement.en: One account gives it clothing and a human-like sitting posture.

basis_claims.quote: The resentful spirits of the horses, angry at being subjected to such a terrifying and painful death, transform into monsters and haunt their former owners.

statement.id: Kisah itu menggambarkannya menghantui bekas pemilik kuda.
statement.en: That account describes it haunting the horse’s former owner.

basis_claims.quote: The two appear to be sitting and talking beneath a mosquito net.

statement.id: Gulungan itu menggambarkan dua yōkai bersama di bawah kelambu.
statement.en: The scroll depicts two yōkai together beneath a mosquito net.

visual_requirements: Man-sized owllike humanoid
Pointed feather ear tufts and glowing eyes
Black claws and feathered wings

basis_claims.quote: In Cornish folklore, the Owlman (Cornish: Kowanden ), also known as the Cornish Owlman or Owlman of Mawnan, is an owl-like humanoid creature reportedly sighted in 1976 in the village of Mawnan, Cornwall, United Kingdom. The reported sightings of the creature flying above the local church tower have been interpreted by some as misidentifications of a barn owl

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Cornwall (Cornish folklore), Owlman (Cornish: Kowanden; Cornish Owlman, Owlman of Mawnan) humanoid mirip burung hantu, terlihat 1976 di Mawnan, Cornwall, Britania Raya (United Kingdom); terbang di atas menara gereja; mungkin burung hantu gudang.
statement.en: In Cornish folklore the Owlman (Cornish Kowanden; Cornish Owlman, Owlman of Mawnan) is an owl-like humanoid seen in 1976 at Mawnan, Cornwall, United Kingdom, flying over the church tower; perhaps a barn owl.

basis_claims.quote: The story originated with Tony "Doc" Shiels, who had been involved in a series of "monster-raising" exploits in 1976. Shiels claimed to have investigated a report of two young girls on holiday in Mawnan who allegedly saw a large winged creature hovering above the tower of St Mawnan and St Stephen's Church, Mawnan on 17 April 1976.

statement.id: Kisah dari Tony Doc Shiels; dua gadis melihat makhluk bersayap di atas menara gereja Mawnan, 17 April 1976. Kowanden
statement.en: The story came from Tony Doc Shiels; two girls saw a winged creature above Mawnan church tower, 17 April 1976.

basis_claims.quote: The account states that the two girls were camping when they encountered a creature described as a "big owl with pointed ears, as big as a man", with glowing eyes and black, pincer-like claws.

statement.id: 3 Juli: Sally Chapman dan Barbara Perry melihat burung hantu besar bertelinga runcing sebesar manusia, mata menyala, cakar hitam.
statement.en: 3 July: Sally Chapman and Barbara Perry saw a big owl with pointed ears, as big as a man, glowing eyes, black claws.

visual_requirements: Tiny scaly greenish humanoid
Very long arms with sharp claws
Sharp teeth and frightening aquatic predator aura

basis_claims.quote: In English folklore, Grindylow or Grundylow is a creature in the counties of Yorkshire and Lancashire. The name is thought to be connected to Grendel, a name or term used in Beowulf and in many Old English charters where it is seen in connection with meres, bogs and lakes.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore), Grindylow (Grundylow) makhluk Yorkshire dan Lancashire; nama terkait Grendel (Beowulf, Inggris Kuno/Old English); di Britania Raya.
statement.en: In English folklore the Grindylow (Grundylow) is a creature of Yorkshire and Lancashire; its name is linked to Grendel (Beowulf, Old English).

basis_claims.quote: Grindylows are supernatural creatures that appear in the folklore of England, most notably the Lancaster area. They are described as diminutive humanoids with scaly skin, a greenish complexion, sharp claws and teeth, and long, wiry arms with lengthy fingers at the end.

statement.id: Humanoid kecil bersisik, kehijauan, cakar dan gigi tajam, lengan panjang; terutama Lancaster.
statement.en: Tiny scaly greenish humanoids with sharp claws and teeth and long arms; especially Lancaster.

basis_claims.quote: They are said to dwell in ponds and marshes waiting for unsuspecting children, which they grab with their shockingly strong grip, and then drag under the surface of the waters.

statement.id: Tinggal di kolam dan rawa, menangkap anak dengan cengkeraman kuat dan menyeretnya ke air.
statement.en: They dwell in ponds and marshes, seizing children with a strong grip and dragging them under.

visual_requirements: Black skin, emerald eyes and dragonlike beard
Male fearsome-faced humanoid
Gentle grieving demeanor and ruby tears
samebito.aura: Gentle sorrowful sea exile despite fearsome visage

basis_claims.quote: is a creature that appears in "The Gratitude of the Samebito", a short story by Lafcadio Hearn.

statement.id: Samebito adalah manusia hiu dalam dongeng yang diceritakan ulang Lafcadio Hearn.
statement.en: Samebito is the shark-person in a folktale retold by Lafcadio Hearn.

basis_claims.quote: It is described as a shark-like humanoid with inky black skin, emerald green eyes, a face like a demon's, and a beard like a dragon's.

statement.id: Ia berkulit hitam, bermata zamrud, berwajah mirip iblis, dan berjanggut mirip naga.
statement.en: He has black skin, emerald eyes, a demonic face and a dragonlike beard.

basis_claims.quote: Although frightening, the creature turns out to be a gentle being who, as punishment for a petty fault, has been expelled from the sea by his former employer Ryūjin.

statement.en: Despite his frightening appearance, he is gentle and expelled from the sea by Ryūjin.
statement.id: Meskipun penampilannya menakutkan, ia lembut dan diusir dari laut oleh Ryūjin.

basis_claims.quote: When the Samebito learns that his master is on his deathbed, he begins to cry tears of blood which become precious rubies when they hit the ground.

statement.id: Air matanya yang seperti darah mengeras menjadi rubi.
statement.en: His bloodlike tears harden into rubies.

basis_claims.quote: Literally, "a Shark-Person," but in this story the Samébito is a male.

statement.id: Catatan Hearn secara tegas menyebut manusia hiu ini laki-laki.
statement.en: Hearn’s note explicitly describes this shark-person as male.

basis_claims.quote: is a yōkai in Japanese mythology.

statement.en: Kotobuki is a yōkai in Japanese mythology.

basis_claims.quote: The Kotobuki is a Japanese Chimera that has the parts of the creatures of the animals on the Chinese zodiac where it sports the head of a rat, the ears of a rabbit, the horns of an ox, the comb of a rooster, the beard of a goat, the neck of a dragon, the mane of a horse, the shoulders of a tiger, the arms of a monkey, the back of a boar, the hind legs of a dog, and the tail of a snake.

statement.id: Tubuh gabungannya memadukan ciri dua belas hewan zodiak.
statement.en: Its composite body combines features of all twelve zodiac animals.

basis_claims.quote: the head of a rat, the ears of a rabbit, the horns of an ox

statement.id: Kepalanya memadukan kepala tikus dengan telinga kelinci dan tanduk sapi.
statement.en: Its head combines a rat’s head with rabbit ears and ox horns.

basis_claims.quote: the back of a boar, the hind legs of a dog, and the tail of a snake.

statement.id: Ia memiliki punggung babi hutan, kaki belakang anjing, dan ekor ular.
statement.en: It has a boar’s back, dog hind legs and a snake tail.

basis_claims.quote: Merely possessing an image of the kotobuki was thought to be enough to protect a person from sickness and disease.

statement.id: Gambarnya dipercaya melindungi pemilik dari penyakit.
statement.en: Images were believed to protect their owners from disease.
