klagmuhme.aura: Sorrowful chilling midnight death warning, ominous rather than vicious attack

basis_claims.quote: is a female sprite from German folklore also known as Klagmutter or Klagemutter (both: wailing mother; German: [ˈklaːɡˌmʊtɐ, ˈklaːɡəˌmʊtɐ] ). She heralds imminent death through wailing and whining and is thus the German equivalent of the banshee.

statement.id: Klagmuhme atau Klagemuhme ("bibi peratap"), juga disebut Klagmutter atau Klagemutter ("ibu peratap"), adalah roh perempuan dari cerita rakyat Jerman yang mengabarkan kematian dengan ratapan dan rintihan, sehingga menjadi padanan banshee di Jerman.
statement.en: The Klagmuhme or Klagemuhme ('wailing aunt'), also called Klagmutter or Klagemutter ('wailing mother'), is a female sprite of German folklore who heralds imminent death by wailing and whining, the German equivalent of the banshee.

basis_claims.quote: The Klagmuhme often appears as an animal. So she roves howling around the concerned house in the shape of a longhaired black dog, or she sits whiningly in the corner as a white goose or in the eaves gutter as a dove.

statement.id: Klagmuhme sering tampil sebagai hewan: anjing hitam berbulu panjang yang melolong mengitari rumah bersangkutan, angsa putih yang merintih di sudut, atau merpati di talang.
statement.en: The Klagmuhme often takes animal form: a long-haired black dog howling round the house concerned, a white goose whimpering in the corner, or a dove in the eaves gutter.

basis_claims.quote: If the Klagmuhme wails in front of a house where an ill person is inside, clothing belonging to the diseased is thrown outside the door. If the Klagmuhme carries the clothing away, the diseased will undoubtedly die; if she leaves it behind, the diseased will recover. The prophesied disaster can be averted by immediately telling the Klagmuhme an alternative.

statement.id: Bila Klagmuhme meratap di depan rumah orang sakit, pakaian si sakit dilempar keluar; jika ia membawanya pergi, orang itu pasti mati, jika ditinggalkan ia sembuh; bencana yang diramalkan dapat dicegah dengan segera menyebutkan alternatif kepadanya.
statement.en: If the Klagmuhme wails before a house with a sick person, the patient's clothes are thrown outside; if she carries them away he will surely die, if she leaves them he will recover; the foretold disaster can be averted by at once telling her an alternative.

basis_claims.quote: She is usually invisible when she gets close to the houses without ever entering them and floats over them. Her whining (which sounds like "u-u-u!") can cause frightened people to fall ill with a nervous disease. Otherwise, she does nobody harm.

statement.id: Biasanya ia tak terlihat saat mendekati rumah, tanpa pernah masuk, dan melayang di atasnya; rintihannya ("u-u-u!") dapat membuat orang yang ketakutan sakit saraf, tetapi selain itu ia tidak mencelakai siapa pun; ia biasanya aktif tengah malam.
statement.en: She is usually invisible as she nears houses, never entering, floating above them; her whine ('u-u-u!') can give frightened people a nervous illness, but otherwise she harms nobody; she is usually active at midnight.

nonhuman_features: Wholly animal black-dog manifestation explicitly attributed to Klagmuhme
klagmuhme.historical_basis: Research c03 explicitly describes Klagmuhme's animal form as long-haired black dog howling around the affected house.
artistic_changes: Exact dog breed unspecified; neutral long-haired canine interpreted
Quiet empty rural house instead of visible ill person

basis_claims.quote: King Harald told a warlock to hie to Iceland in some altered shape, and to try what he could learn there to tell him: and he set out in the shape of a whale. ... where he saw all the mountains and hills full of guardian-spirits, some great, some small.

statement.en: King Harald sent a warlock to Iceland in altered shape; he went as a whale and saw all the mountains and hills full of guardian spirits, great and small.

basis_claims.quote: First on the East side by a large dragon followed by snakes, toads and lizards who blew atter, or poison, at him, then on the North side by a great bird with many smaller birds, next in the West a large bull followed by beasts and other landvættir, and finally a huge bergrisi with an iron staff in the South

statement.id: Ia diusir di sisi timur oleh naga besar yang diikuti ular, kodok, dan kadal penyembur racun, di utara oleh burung besar, di barat oleh banteng besar beserta landvættir lain, dan di selatan oleh bergrisi raksasa bertongkat besi.
statement.en: He was driven off in the east by a great dragon with poison-blowing snakes, toads and lizards, in the north by a great bird, in the west by a great bull with other landvættir, and in the south by a huge bergrisi with an iron staff.

basis_claims.quote: Les quatre Landvættir sont aujourd'hui considérés comme les protecteurs des quatre quartiers d'Islande : le dragon (Dreki) dans le Nord-Est, l'aigle ou griffon (Gammur) dans de Nord-Ouest, le taureau (Griðungur) dans le Sud-Ouest, et le géant (Bergrisi) dans le Sud-Est. Les quatre Landvættir de l'Islande sont représentés sur les Armoiries de l'Islande et sur l'envers des pièces

statement.id: Empat landvættir kini dianggap pelindung empat wilayah Islandia: naga (Dreki), elang atau griffin (Gammur), banteng (Griðungur), dan raksasa (Bergrisi); keempatnya tampil pada lambang Islandia dan sisi belakang koin króna.
statement.en: The four landvættir are now regarded as protectors of Iceland's four quarters: the dragon (Dreki), eagle or griffin (Gammur), bull (Griðungur) and giant (Bergrisi); they appear on the Icelandic arms and the reverse of króna coins.

pangu.aura: Cosmic egg opening and separation of heaven from earth

basis_claims.quote:
Pangu or Pan Gu (also sometimes spelled Peng Gu and P’an-ku)
(Chinese: 盤古; pinyin: Pángǔ ; PAN-koo) is a primordial being and creation figure in Chinese mythology and in Taoism. According to legend, Pangu separated heaven and earth, and his body later became geographic features such as mountains and flowing water.

statement.id: Pangu adalah makhluk purba dan tokoh penciptaan dalam mitologi Tiongkok dan Taoisme; menurut legenda ia memisahkan langit dan bumi.
statement.en: Pangu is a primordial being and creation figure in Chinese mythology and Taoism; according to legend he separated heaven and earth.

basis_claims.quote: In the beginning, there was nothing and the universe was in a featureless, formless primordial state. This primordial state coalesced into a cosmic egg over the course of about 18,000 years. Within it, the perfectly opposed principles of yin and yang became balanced and Pangu emerged (or woke up) from the egg. Pangu inside the cosmic egg symbolizes Taiji.

statement.id: Dalam kisah telur kosmis, Pangu muncul setelah yin dan yang mencapai keseimbangan.
statement.en: In the cosmic-egg tale, Pangu emerges once yin and yang reach balance.

basis_claims.quote: Pangu inside the cosmic egg symbolizes Taiji. Pangu is usually depicted as a primitive, hairy giant with horns on his head.

statement.id: Pangu lazim digambarkan sebagai raksasa berbulu dengan tanduk di kepala.
statement.en: Depictions commonly present Pangu as a hairy giant bearing horns.

basis_claims.quote: P'an Ku is pictured as a man of dwarfish stature clothed in bearskin, or merely in leaves or with an apron of leaves. He has two horns on his head. In his right hand he holds a hammer and in his left a chisel (sometimes these are reversed)
basis_claims.locator: Chapter III, "The Fashioner of the Universe"

statement.id: Menurut Werner, P'an Ku digambarkan sebagai pria bertubuh kerdil berpakaian kulit beruang atau daun, bertanduk dua, memegang palu di tangan kanan dan pahat di tangan kiri (kadang terbalik).
statement.en: According to Werner, P'an Ku is pictured as a dwarfish man clothed in bearskin or leaves, with two horns, holding a hammer in his right hand and a chisel in his left (sometimes reversed).

basis_claims.quote: His task occupied eighteen thousand years, during which he formed the sun, moon, and stars, the heavens and the earth, himself increasing in stature day by day, being daily six feet taller than the day before, until, his labours ended, he died that his works might live.
basis_claims.locator: Chapter III, "The Fashioner of the Universe"

statement.id: Menurut Werner, tugas P'an Ku memakan delapan belas ribu tahun; ia membentuk matahari, bulan, bintang, langit, dan bumi sambil bertambah tinggi enam kaki setiap hari, lalu wafat agar karyanya hidup.
statement.en: According to Werner, P'an Ku's task occupied eighteen thousand years, during which he formed the sun, moon, stars, heavens and earth, growing six feet taller each day until he died so that his works might live.

statement.en: The myling (also utburd in Norwegian, útburður in Icelandic, ihtiriekko and liekkiö in Finnish) is said to chase lone wanderers at night, jump on their backs and demand to be carried to the graveyard; it grows heavier as the graveyard nears, and if the victim fails to reach it, kills them in rage.

basis_claims.quote: In legends, Rübezahl appears as a capricious giant, gnome, or mountain spirit. With good people he is friendly, teaching them medicine and giving them presents. statement.id: Dalam legenda Rübezahl tampil sebagai raksasa, gnom, atau roh gunung yang berubah-ubah; ramah kepada orang baik, mengajari pengobatan dan memberi hadiah, tetapi membalas keras orang yang mengejeknya, dan kadang berperan sebagai penipu.
statement.en: In legend Rübezahl appears as a capricious giant, gnome or mountain spirit; friendly to good people, teaching medicine and giving presents, but taking severe revenge on those who deride him, and sometimes a trickster.

basis_claims.quote: Rübezahl is the fantastic lord of weather of the mountains and is similar to the Wild Hunt. Unexpectedly or playfully, he sends lightning and thunder, fog, rain and snow from the mountain above, even while the sun is shining.

statement.id: Rübezahl adalah penguasa cuaca pegunungan, mirip Perburuan Liar, yang tiba-tiba mengirim petir, guntur, kabut, hujan, dan salju walau matahari bersinar.
statement.en: Rübezahl is the lord of weather of the mountains, similar to the Wild Hunt, sending lightning, thunder, fog, rain and snow even while the sun shines.

basis_claims.quote: Représenté pour la première fois en 1561 sur une carte du géographe Martin Helwig, il n'est pas antérieur au XVe siècle. Sa légende naquit probablement parmi les mineurs immigrants dans la région.

statement.id: Rübezahl pertama kali digambarkan pada 1561 di peta ahli geografi Martin Helwig, tidak lebih tua dari abad ke-15, dan legendanya mungkin lahir di kalangan penambang pendatang.
statement.en: Rübezahl was first depicted in 1561 on a map by the geographer Martin Helwig, is no older than the 15th century, and his legend probably arose among immigrant miners.

basis_claims.quote: Insbesondere zeigt er sich als Mönch in aschgrauer Kutte (vergleichbar Wodan im Wolkenmantel), aber auch als Bergmann, Junker, Handwerker und in ähnlicher Gestalt und Verkleidung, aber auch in Tiergestalt oder als Gegenstand (Baumstumpf, Stein, Wolke).

statement.id: Ia menampakkan diri terutama sebagai biarawan berjubah kelabu abu, tetapi juga sebagai penambang, bangsawan muda, tukang, dalam wujud hewan, atau sebagai benda (tunggul pohon, batu, awan).
statement.en: He appears especially as a monk in an ash-grey habit, but also as a miner, squire or craftsman, in animal form, or as an object (tree stump, stone, cloud).

basis_claims.quote: Rübezahl is seen to be the guardian of the Giant Mountains. ... Historically, his character has kept on expanding; from a bad demon causing storms and heavy snow, he evolved into a guardian of the poor people living in his mountains.

statement.id: Rübezahl dipandang sebagai penjaga Pegunungan Raksasa; dari setan jahat pembawa badai dan salju lebat, ia berkembang menjadi pelindung orang miskin di pegunungannya.
statement.en: Rübezahl is seen as guardian of the Giant Mountains; from a bad demon causing storms and heavy snow he evolved into a guardian of the poor in his mountains.

basis_claims.quote: Another proposed etymology is Riebezagel, from a combination of the personal name Riebe and the Middle High German zagel, meaning "tail", from his pictorial representation as a tailed demon.

statement.id: Etimologi lain yang diajukan adalah Riebezagel, gabungan nama diri Riebe dan kata Jerman Hulu Pertengahan zagel, "ekor", dari penggambarannya sebagai setan berekor.
statement.en: Another proposed etymology is Riebezagel, combining the personal name Riebe with Middle High German zagel, 'tail', from his depiction as a tailed demon.

nonhuman_features: One eagle head bearing one pair of branching deer antlers
Lion-like torso with two forelimbs and two goat hindlegs
Goat hooves and one bifurcated tail with two terminal branches
Whole upright heraldic hybrid beast, no human face
rubezahl.historical_basis: Actual public-domain 1561 Helwig map held at Badische Landesbibliothek was individually inspected, including zoomed Rübenzal figure. Regional Krkonoše heritage publication explicitly describes eagle head, deer antlers, lion body, goat legs and twofold tail.
rubezahl.artistic_changes: Painterly forest mountain lighting and richer natural animal textures; faithful historic hybrid silhouette and bodily components retained.

additional_sources.title: Badische Landesbibliothek: Helwig 1561 Silesia map
additional_sources.purpose: Primary original map and IIIF crop individually inspected; beast near Rübenzal label.

additional_sources.title: Primary map Rübenzal detail
additional_sources.purpose: Direct zoom of original 1561 hybrid figure used as visual anatomy reference.

additional_sources.title: Krkonoše official regional heritage publication
additional_sources.purpose: Lists named historic hybrid components, not generic demon anatomy.

elder-mother.depicted_variant: Elder Mother / Flearemem transformed into an elder tree in Rollright-Stones legend
visual_requirements: One living elder tree, woody trunk/branches with compound leaf clusters
No ordinary human woman, human face or hybrid limbs
Mysterious guarded grove and stone-circle context
Uncanny watchful tree-guardian/witch transformation aura
elder-mother.aura: Ancient uncanny guarded woodland presence, watchful tree spirit with ominous witch-legend undertone

basis_claims.quote: The Elder Mother is an elder-guarding being in English and Scandinavian folklore known by a variety of names, such as the Danish Hyldemoer ("Elder-Mother") and the Lincolnshire names Old Lady and Old Girl.

statement.id: Elder Mother adalah makhluk penjaga pohon elder dalam cerita rakyat Inggris (English) dan Skandinavia (Scandinavian) dengan banyak nama, seperti Hyldemoer dari Denmark (Danish) dan Old Lady atau Old Girl di Lincolnshire.
statement.en: The Elder Mother is an elder-guarding being in English and Scandinavian folklore with many names, such as the Danish Hyldemoer and the Lincolnshire Old Lady and Old Girl.

basis_claims.quote: The Elder Mother is thought to be the guardian of the elder trees, and it was said, until recent times in various parts of England and Scandinavia that to take wood from the elder tree one would have to ask the Elder Mother first, or else ill luck would befall the woodsman.

statement.id: Elder Mother dianggap penjaga pohon elder; hingga belum lama ini di berbagai bagian Inggris (England) dan Skandinavia (Scandinavia) dikatakan bahwa untuk mengambil kayu elder orang harus meminta izinnya dulu, atau penebang akan tertimpa sial.
statement.en: The Elder Mother is held to guard elder trees; until recently in parts of England and Scandinavia it was said one must first ask her before taking elder wood, or ill luck would befall the woodsman.

basis_claims.quote: And thus the king and his knights were turned to stone and the witch turned herself into an elder tree.

statement.id: Demikianlah raja dan para ksatrianya diubah menjadi batu, dan penyihir itu mengubah dirinya menjadi pohon elder.
statement.en: Thus the king and his knights were turned to stone and the witch turned herself into an elder tree.

basis_claims.quote: Yn ien sa'n ferhaal feroaret de Flearmem sa'n kening en syn mannen yn 'e Rollright Stones, dy't op 'e grins fan 'e Ingelske greefskippen Oxfordshire en Warwickshire steane, wylst se harsels yn in flearebeam feroaret.

statement.id: Dalam satu kisah, Flearemem mengubah seorang raja dan anak buahnya menjadi Batu Rollright (Rollright Stones) di perbatasan Oxfordshire dan Warwickshire, sementara ia sendiri berubah menjadi pohon elder.
statement.en: In one such tale the Flearemem turns a king and his men into the Rollright Stones on the Oxfordshire–Warwickshire border, while turning herself into an elder tree.

nonhuman_features: Wholly botanical elder-tree transformation explicitly attributed to Elder Mother
elder-mother.historical_basis: Research c05/c08 says Flearemem/Elder Mother changes herself into elder tree while king/men become Rollright Stones. Depict actual tree transformation; no invented tree face or branch hands.
artistic_changes: Specific old elder branching habit and leaf/flower texture interpreted botanically
Distant stone silhouettes establish Rollright legend scene; they are inert background

vamana.depicted_variant: One respectful monumental depiction of Vamana in the TRIVIKRAMA growth episode: a modestly clothed youthful human Brahmin grows to COSMIC SCALE, one foot spanning earth and next stride reaching heaven. Ordinary human body, two arms and two legs, no additional limbs. One hand holds a plain umbrella, the other a kamandalu water vessel; fully clothed modest sacred robes. Small world landscape below and immense cloud/star dome establish the documented three-world strides. Majestic benevolent light, no text, no aggression or distorted body. Do not blend with blue four-armed Vishnu or infant nudity.

visual_requirements.description: One respectful monumental depiction of Vamana in the TRIVIKRAMA growth episode: a modestly clothed youthful human Brahmin grows to COSMIC SCALE, one foot spanning earth and next stride reaching heaven. Ordinary human body, two arms and two legs, no additional limbs. One hand holds a plain umbrella, the other a kamandalu water vessel; fully clothed modest sacred robes. Small world landscape below and immense cloud/star dome establish the documented three-world strides. Majestic benevolent light, no text, no aggression or distorted body. Do not blend with blue four-armed Vishnu or infant nudity.
Cosmic-scale expansion and heaven/earth-spanning stride; basis: documented growth and three strides reclaiming worlds

basis_claims.quote: is an avatar of the Hindu deity Vishnu. He is the fifth avatar of Vishnu and the first Dashavatara in the Treta Yuga, after Narasimha. First mentioned in the Vedas, Vamana is most commonly associated in the Hindu epics and Puranas with the story of taking back the three worlds (collectively referred to as the Trailokya) from the daitya-king Mahabali by taking three steps

statement.id: Vamana adalah awatara kelima dewa Hindu Vishnu (Wisnu), Dashavatara pertama di Treta Yuga sesudah Narasimha, yang dalam Weda (Vedas) dan Purana merebut tiga dunia (Trailokya) dari Mahabali dengan tiga langkah (three steps).
statement.en: Vamana is the fifth avatar of the Hindu deity Vishnu, the first Dashavatara of the Treta Yuga after Narasimha, who in the Vedas and Puranas takes back the three worlds (Trailokya) from Mahabali with three steps.

basis_claims.quote: Wamana dilukiskan sebagai brahmana dengan raga anak kecil yang membawa kamandalu dan payung. Wamana kadang-kadang dikenal juga dengan sebutan Upendra

statement.id: Wamana dilukiskan sebagai brahmana berraga anak kecil membawa kamandalu dan payung, juga disebut Upendra.
statement.en: Wamana is shown as a brahmin (brahmana) in a child's body with a kamandalu and umbrella (payung), also called Upendra.

basis_claims.quote: brahmana kecil itu meminta tanah seluas tiga jengkal yang diukur dengan langkah kakinya. Raja Bali pun takabur dan melupakan nasihat Sukracarya, dan menyuruh brahmana kecil itu melangkah. Pada waktu itu juga, brahmana tersebut membesar dan terus membesar. Dengan ukurannya yang sangat besar, ia mampu melangkah di surga dan bumi sekaligus.

statement.id: Brahmana kecil meminta tanah tiga langkah; Raja Bali mengabulkan, lalu brahmana itu membesar hingga melangkah di surga dan bumi sekaligus.
statement.en: The little brahmin asked for land of three strides; King Bali (Raja Bali) granted it, and the brahmin grew until he strode over heaven (surga) and earth (bumi) at once.

basis_claims.quote: Pada langkah yang pertama, ia menginjak swarga. Pada langkah yang kedua, ia menginjak bumi. Pada langkah yang ketiga, karena tidak ada lahan untuknya berpijak, maka Bali menyerahkan kepalanya.

statement.id: Langkah pertama menginjak swarga, kedua bumi, dan untuk langkah ketiga Bali menyerahkan kepalanya.
statement.en: His first step trod swarga, the second the earth (bumi), and for the third Bali offered his head (kepalanya).

basis_claims.quote: 'Trivikrama' त्रिविक्रम 'three steps' or 'three strides' (tri 'three' + vikrama 'step' or 'stride'). This epithet refers to the three steps or strides of Vishnu in the Rigveda.

statement.id: Julukan Trivikrama berarti tiga langkah (three steps), merujuk tiga langkah Wisnu (Vishnu) dalam Rigveda.
statement.en: The epithet Trivikrama means three steps, referring to Vishnu's three strides in the Rigveda.

artistic_changes: Low-angle framing, painterly materials and environmental color are artistic rendering.
Effects are limited to the cited domains, deeds, attributes or iconography; natural light and scale supply presence where no elemental ability is documented.

presentation_revision.rationale: Big names (major gods, archangels, demon princes, primordial monsters, famous literary beings) must look imposing and powerful: an epic, awe-inspiring or terrifying presence that matches their standing in the tradition.

kuntilanak.depicted_variant: Malay folklore Kuntilanak with a hollow back, selected independently of neck-hole account
visual_requirements: One adult spirit with large visibly empty structural cavity in upper back
Modest long white robe, long black hair kept away from cavity
One head and two arms; whole figure within frame
Cold watchful nocturnal haunting aura

basis_claims.quote: Umumnya, kuntilanak digambarkan sebagai wanita cantik berambut panjang dan berbaju panjang warna putih.

statement.id: Umumnya kuntilanak digambarkan berwujud wanita cantik dengan rambut panjang dan busana gaun panjang berwarna putih.
statement.en: Kuntilanak is commonly depicted as an attractive woman with long hair in a long white dress.

basis_claims.quote: Dalam cerita rakyat Melayu, sosok kuntilanak digambarkan dalam bentuk wanita cantik dengan punggung berlubang.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Melayu, kuntilanak digambarkan berwujud wanita cantik dengan punggung berlubang.
statement.en: In Malay folklore, kuntilanak is depicted as an attractive woman with a hole in her back.

basis_claims.quote: Kuntilanak digambarkan senang meneror penduduk kampung untuk menuntut balas.

statement.id: Kuntilanak digambarkan senang meneror penduduk kampung di pedesaan untuk menuntut balas.
statement.en: Kuntilanak is described as terrorizing village inhabitants to seek retribution.

basis_claims.quote: Kuntilanak konon juga menyukai pohon tertentu sebagai tempat "bersemayam", misalnya waru yang tumbuh condong ke samping (populer disebut "waru doyong").

statement.id: Kuntilanak menyukai pohon tertentu sebagai tempat bersemayam, seperti pohon waru condong atau Waru doyong.
statement.en: Kuntilanak favors certain trees to haunt, particularly leaning Waru trees.

nonhuman_features: Large hollow cavity structurally within upper back
kuntilanak.historical_basis: Reviewed kuntilanak-c05 explicitly documents hollow-back form in Malay folklore; c04 long black hair and white dress, c06 vengeance, c07 leaning waru tree. Selected back-cavity variant without conflating neck-hole accounts.
artistic_changes: Pose, lighting, garment opening and composition expose documented hollow back; no new anatomical traits.

banshee.depicted_variant: Female Banshee keening in grey cloak over green dress
visual_requirements: Female Banshee keening in grey cloak over green dress
Coherent anatomy and documented mythic scene
banshee.aura: Presence through source-backed form and physical scene; no generic glow, ribbons or magical mist.

basis_claims.quote: A banshee (/ˈbænʃiː/ BAN-shee; Modern Irish bean sí  [bʲanˠ ˈʃiː] , from Old Irish: ben síde  [bʲen ˈʃiːðʲe] , "woman of the fairy mound" or "fairy woman") is a female spirit in Irish folklore who heralds the death of a family member

statement.id: Banshee adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia yang menandai kematian anggota keluarga.
statement.en: A banshee is a female spirit in Irish folklore who heralds the death of a family member.

basis_claims.quote: Sometimes she has long streaming hair, which she may be seen combing, with some legends specifying she can only keen while combing her hair.

statement.id: Banshee kadang terlihat memiliki rambut panjang terurai yang sedang disisir.
statement.en: She is sometimes seen with long streaming hair that she combs.

basis_claims.quote: She wears a grey cloak over a green dress, and her eyes are red from continual weeping.

statement.id: Banshee digambarkan mengenakan jubah abu-abu di atas gaun hijau dengan mata merah karena terus menangis.
statement.en: She wears a grey cloak over a green dress with red eyes from weeping.

artistic_changes: Painterly square composition
Clothing, weather and exact setting details are editorial unless identified in claims

presentation_revision.rationale: Replaces ordinary animal presentation with Female Banshee keening in grey cloak over green dress

wewe-gombel.depicted_variant: Javanese Wewe Gombel with documented elongated breasts and claws, modest opaque treatment
visual_requirements: Long sharp recurved finger claws visible on both hands
Two distinctly elongated pendulous breasts covered by opaque cloth
wewe-gombel.aura: Stern protective yet uncanny elderly forest spirit

basis_claims.quote: Wewe Gombel atau juga disebut Nenek Gombel dalam tradisi Jawa yang berarti roh jahat atau hantu yang suka menculik anak-anak, tetapi tidak mencelakainya.

statement.id: Wewe Gombel atau Nenek Gombel dalam tradisi Jawa adalah hantu yang suka menculik anak-anak tanpa mencelakainya.
statement.en: Wewe Gombel or Nenek Gombel in Javanese tradition is a ghost that kidnaps children without harming them.

basis_claims.quote: Di Semarang dan Jawa Tengah berkembang mitos adanya hantu dengan sebutan Wewe Gombel. Di daerah lain dikenal dengan nama Kolong Wewe.

statement.id: Mitos hantu Wewe Gombel berkembang di Semarang dan Jawa Tengah, serta dikenal dengan nama Kolong Wewe di daerah lain.
statement.en: The myth of Wewe Gombel developed in Semarang and Central Java, known as Kolong Wewe in other areas.

basis_claims.quote: Mitos yang hidup di masyarakat, perwujudan Wewe Gombel adalah perempuan yang bisa berubah wujud menjadi siapa saja, dengan ukuran payudara yang luar biasa besarnya.

statement.id: Wewe Gombel digambarkan memiliki ukuran payudara yang luar biasa besar dan dapat berubah wujud menjadi siapa saja.
statement.en: Wewe Gombel is depicted with exceptionally large breasts and can shapeshift into anyone.

basis_claims.quote: Wewe Gombel itu menculik anak-anak karena membela mereka, kalau orang tuanya sudah menyesal, Wewe Gombel akan menunjukkan tempat disembunyikannya

statement.id: Wewe Gombel menculik anak-anak untuk membela mereka dan akan menunjukkan tempat sembunyinya setelah orang tua menyesal.
statement.en: Wewe Gombel kidnaps children to defend them and reveals their hiding place once parents repent.

basis_claims.quote: involving a mother and her son living in extreme poverty, with a looming threat posed by the being Wewe Gombel, a ghost from Javanese mythology that has a penchant for kidnapping unloved children. With elongated breasts and claws

statement.id: Wewe Gombel digambarkan sebagai hantu mitologi Jawa berpayudara panjang dan bercakar yang menculik anak-anak.
statement.en: Wewe Gombel is portrayed as a Javanese mythological ghost with elongated breasts and claws who kidnaps unloved children.

nonhuman_features: Long sharp recurved finger claws visible on both hands
Two distinctly elongated pendulous breasts covered by opaque cloth
wewe-gombel.historical_basis: Reviewed c05 records exceptionally large breasts and c13 explicitly documents elongated breasts and claws. c06 supports sheltering neglected children without harming them, informing non-attacking protective aura.
wewe-gombel.artistic_changes: Opaque black draping modestly covers elongated anatomy; dusk banyan pose and cloth pattern are interpretive.

almaz-mythical-beast.depicted_variant: Male hairy hideous Caucasian Almaz with axe embedded in chest
visual_requirements: Entire densely shaggy hair-covered bodily surface
One axe embedded non-graphically in the chest rather than carried in the hands

basis_claims.quote: The Almaz (Adyghe: Almesti, Chechen and Ingush: Almaz or Hun-sag; ), roughly translated as various "feral forest-man" or "stone spirit", is a mythical beast that is considered to be an evil forest creature with magical powers residing in its hair that exists in Chechen, Ingush and Circassian folk beliefs.

statement.id: Almaz adalah makhluk hutan dalam kepercayaan rakyat Chechen, Ingush, dan Circassian, dengan kekuatan gaib di rambutnya.
statement.en: Almaz is a forest creature in Chechen, Ingush and Circassian folk belief, with magical power in its hair.

basis_claims.quote: The male almaz is said to be hairy and hideous, and have an axe embedded in its chest

statement.id: Laki-laki almaz digambarkan berbulu, mengerikan, dan memiliki kapak tertanam di dadanya.
statement.en: Male almaz are described as hairy and hideous with an axe embedded in the chest.

basis_claims.quote: The almaz is said to have magical powers residing in its hair, but if the hair is removed or even grabbed, it may be rendered helpless.

statement.id: Menghilangkan atau memegang rambutnya dapat membuat almaz tidak berdaya.
statement.en: Removing or grabbing its hair can render an almaz helpless.

nonhuman_features: Entire densely shaggy hair-covered bodily surface
One axe embedded non-graphically in the chest rather than carried in the hands
almaz-mythical-beast.historical_basis: Reviewed almaz-mythical-beast-c02 explicitly records hairy hideous males with an axe embedded in the chest, selected instead of female golden-haired humanlike variant c03.
almaz-mythical-beast.artistic_changes: Non-graphic embedding, modest waistcloth, forest pose and tactile fur are interpretive treatments of sourced male variant.

busaw.depicted_variant: Busaw in its corpse-stealing night form with pointed teeth, hooked nails and long tongue
visual_requirements: Conspicuous pointed teeth, one long tongue, hooked fingernails
One coherent humanoid ghoul with two arms and two legs
No horns, wings, tail, or unsupported hybrid features
Tropical tree and cemetery setting
busaw.aura: Hungry sneaking corpse-thief menace beneath a large tropical tree

basis_claims.quote: Busaw is a legendary creature that resembles humans in appearance and behavior, raising farm animals and planting root crops. However, its favorite food is humans, resulting in scattered human skeletons on the grounds of its dwelling place.

statement.id: Busaw adalah makhluk legenda yang menyerupai manusia dalam rupa dan perilaku, beternak dan menanam umbi, tetapi makanan kesukaannya manusia sehingga kerangka manusia berserakan di sekitar tempat tinggalnya.
statement.en: The busaw is a legendary creature resembling humans, raising animals and root crops, but its favourite food is humans, leaving skeletons around its home.

basis_claims.quote: The Busaw was a ghoul and corpse thief. An evil spirit who looked and behaved like ordinary human beings by day, it listened for sounds of death in the evenings, and dwelled in large trees near cemeteries. It had pointed teeth, hooked nails and a long tongue.

statement.id: Busaw adalah roh jahat pemakan mayat dan pencuri jenazah yang siang hari tampak seperti manusia biasa, malam hari mendengarkan tanda kematian, tinggal di pohon besar dekat kuburan, bergigi runcing, berkuku bengkok, dan berlidah panjang; ia mengganti jenazah dengan batang pisang, mengubahnya menjadi babi, dan memakannya.
statement.en: The busaw was an evil ghoul and corpse thief, human-seeming by day, listening for death at night, living in large trees near cemeteries, with pointed teeth, hooked nails and a long tongue; it replaced corpses with banana trunks, turned them into pigs and ate them.

nonhuman_features: Very long protruding tongue
Sharply pointed tooth rows
Long strongly hooked nails on coherent hands
busaw.historical_basis: Verified claim busaw-c02 records human-seeming day appearance but pointed teeth, hooked nails and long tongue for the corpse-thieving ghoul; it resides in large trees near cemeteries and substitutes banana trunks for corpses.
artistic_changes: Exact lengths of tongue and hooked nails are painterly interpretations of the attested long/hooked descriptions, rather than measured folkloric dimensions. Gaunt crouch, hair, plain cloth, lighting and cemetery details are aesthetic choices.

harionago.depicted_variant: Shikoku roadside Harionago with prehensile barbed-hook hair
visual_requirements: Long prehensile black hair extending in active separate locks
Large sharp hooked barbs physically at multiple hair tips

basis_claims.quote: a yokai in Japanese folklore that preys on young men.

statement.id: Harionago adalah yōkai Jepang yang konon memangsa pria muda.
statement.en: Harionago is a Japanese yōkai said to prey on young men.

basis_claims.quote: Harionago appears along roads on the island of Shikoku as an attractive young woman with long black hair.

statement.id: Ia konon muncul di jalanan Shikoku.
statement.en: She is said to appear on roads in Shikoku.

basis_claims.quote: The strands of her hair are prehensile and tipped with sharp barbed hooks.

statement.id: Kisah-kisah memberinya rambut panjang berujung kait.
statement.en: Stories give her long hair tipped with hooks.

basis_claims.quote: When a man approaches her on a pathway, she laughs and, if he laughs in return, she attacks the man with her barbed hair.

statement.id: Satu cerita menyebut ia menyerang pria yang membalas tawanya.
statement.en: A tale says she attacks a man who laughs back at her.

nonhuman_features: Long prehensile black hair extending in active separate locks
Large sharp hooked barbs physically at multiple hair tips
harionago.historical_basis: Reviewed harionago-c03 explicitly describes prehensile hair strands with sharp barbed hooks; c02 records Shikoku road appearance and c04 laughing roadside attack.
harionago.artistic_changes: Kimono pattern, forest scene and composition of barbed locks are painterly interpretations of documented hook-tipped prehensile hair.

yama-uba.depicted_variant: Kuwazu nyobo ('Wife Who Doesn't Eat') second-mouth yamauba folklore variant
visual_requirements: One humanlike adult head with normal facial mouth AND distinct real rear scalp mouth
Rear scalp mouth exposed through parted hair, two arms and two legs, whole frame
Modest fully covered figure, deceptive predatory mountain-ogress aura
yama-uba.aura: Deceptive wary predatory mountain ogress, not generic benevolent old lady

basis_claims.quote: Yamamba (山むば) is a Japanese yōkai also known as yamauba (山うば)

statement.id: Yama-uba atau yamamba adalah yōkai Jepang.
statement.en: Yama-uba, also known as yamamba, is a Japanese yōkai.

basis_claims.quote: They occasionally offer a place to sleep for the night to travelers in the form of an old woman or beautiful young woman.

statement.id: Dalam beberapa cerita ia menawarkan tempat bermalam sebagai perempuan tua atau muda.
statement.en: In some tales she offers lodging as an old or young woman.

basis_claims.quote: After their guests fall asleep, they transform into their true form and eat their guests.

statement.id: Setelah tamu tertidur, yama-uba dalam kisah menampakkan wujudnya dan memakan tamu.
statement.en: In some stories yama-uba transforms and eats sleeping guests.

nonhuman_features: Separate second anatomical mouth on back of head with teeth and tongue
yama-uba.historical_basis: Noriko T. Reider's original academic study Yamauba and Oni-Women in Japanese Folktales (Asian Ethnology 78/2, 2019), pp.407–409, analyzes Kuwazu nyobo: rear second mouth is revealed by wife whom tale identifies as yamauba. Text counts eighteen yamauba variants alongside oni/oni-baba variants. Japanese Demon Lore also explicitly identifies second-mouth wife as yamauba. Selects this documented regional story type; does not conflate all yamauba with all futakuchi-onna.
artistic_changes: Rear three-quarter staging and clothing/hut details interpreted
Teeth shape, tongue and visible aperture are illustration details within source-attested second mouth

additional_sources.title: Yamauba and Oni-Women in Japanese Folktales
additional_sources.author: Noriko T. Reider
additional_sources.basis: pp.407–409 Kuwazu nyobo second-mouth yamauba variants; primary research with tale corpus

dakini.depicted_variant: Simhamukha, the blue-black three-eyed lion-faced Tibetan wisdom Dakini; modest educational treatment
visual_requirements: One nonhuman lion face with muzzle and fangs
Exactly three red eyes including forehead eye
Blue-black body with two arms and two legs

basis_claims.quote: A dakini is a type of goddess in Hinduism and Buddhism.

statement.id: Dakini adalah jenis dewi dalam Hindu dan Buddha.
statement.en: A dakini is a type of goddess in Hinduism and Buddhism.

basis_claims.quote: Meanwhile, in Nepalese and Tibetan Buddhism, dakini (or wisdom dakini) can refer to both what can be best described as fierce-looking female embodiments of enlightened energy,

statement.id: Dalam Buddha Nepal dan Tibet, dakini kebijaksanaan dipandang sebagai perwujudan perempuan dari energi tercerahkan.
statement.en: In Nepalese and Tibetan Buddhism wisdom dakinis are regarded as female embodiments of enlightened energy.

basis_claims.quote: In the Nyingma Tradition of Tibetan Buddhism, a Dakini is a term generally used to describe a female deity or enlightened being.

statement.id: HAR menjelaskan dakini dalam Nyingma sebagai dewi perempuan atau makhluk tercerahkan.
statement.en: HAR explains dakini in Nyingma as a female deity or enlightened being.

Exactly three red eyes including forehead eye
Blue-black body with two arms and two legs
dakini.historical_basis: Additional institutional sources explicitly name Simhamukha as lion-faced wisdom Dakini. HAR quotes historical ritual visualization specifying blue-black body, one face, two hands and three red eyes; selected as one Dakini subvariant, not generalized to all dakinis.
dakini.artistic_changes: Opaque maroon/saffron drape replaces scant lower garment for modesty; skullcup left empty, graphic severed-head necklace omitted, symbolic pedestal and landscape interpreted. Anatomy unchanged.

additional_sources.title: Rubin Museum: Fierce Lion-faced Goddess, Simhamukha
additional_sources.purpose: Museum identifies lion-faced protective wisdom deity, dancing stance and knife/skullcup ritual implements.

ysbaddaden.depicted_variant: Ysbaddaden Penkawr's supernaturally heavy drooping eyebrows in Lady Charlotte Guest's Culhwch and Olwen translation
visual_requirements: One giant seated figure, one head, two arms and two legs
Immense paired fleshy eyebrow folds droop over eyes and require two fork supports
Whole seated figure and feet visible, commanding malicious giant aura
ysbaddaden.aura: Menacing obstinate giant patriarch in nearly inaccessible Welsh castle

basis_claims.quote: Ysbaddaden Bencawr ; "Ysbaddaden, Chief of Giants" (from roots meaning "hawthorn" or "infertile" - or perhaps implying both meanings), is the primary antagonist of the Welsh romance Culhwch and Olwen. A vicious giant residing in a nigh unreachable castle, he is the father of Olwen and uncle of Goreu fab Custennin.

statement.id: Ysbaddaden Bencawr, Kepala Para Raksasa (hawthorn/mandul), antagonis Culhwch and Olwen (Wales, Welsh), raksasa kejam, ayah Olwen, paman Goreu fab Custennin; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: Ysbaddaden Bencawr, Chief of Giants, is the antagonist of the Welsh Culhwch and Olwen, a vicious giant, father of Olwen and uncle of Goreu fab Custennin.

basis_claims.quote: Ysbaddaden hat Augenlider, die so schwer sind, dass sie ein Diener mit der Gabel hochheben muss, wenn er jemanden betrachten will (vergleiche dazu Balor).

statement.id: Kelopak mata (Augenlider) berat diangkat pelayan dengan garpu (Gabel); bandingkan Balor.
statement.en: His heavy eyelids (Augenlider) are lifted by a servant with a fork (Gabel); compare Balor.

nonhuman_features: Massive unnatural bodily eyebrow ridges extending down over both eyes, requiring forked supports
ysbaddaden.historical_basis: Lady Charlotte Guest, The Mabinogion, Kilhwch and Olwen: Yspaddaden calls for forks beneath his two eyebrows that have fallen over his eyes. The primary translation says eyebrows, while research c06's secondary German description says eyelids; this rendition follows the primary wording and emphasizes extraordinary physical weight, with fork supports to show the defining morphology.
artistic_changes: Fork supports rest on bench rather than being held by attendants to keep one character composition
Exact brown robe, architecture and degree of eyebrow enlargement interpreted to show source's extraordinary feature

additional_sources.title: The Mabinogion: Chapter 4, Kilhwch and Olwen
additional_sources.publisher: Kellscraft transcription of Lady Charlotte Guest translation
additional_sources.basis: Two eyebrows fallen over eyes must be raised with forks

bean-nighe.depicted_variant: Scottish Bean-nighe Washer at the Ford in recorded red-webbed-feet variant
visual_requirements: Two clearly red nonhuman webbed feet with connecting toe membranes
bean-nighe.aura: Lonely sorrowful washer and portent of death

basis_claims.quote: is a female spirit in Scottish folklore, regarded as an omen of death and a messenger from the Otherworld. She is a type of ban-sìth (Irish: bean sídhe , anglicized as "banshee") that haunts desolate streams and washes the clothing of those who are about to die. Les Lavandières is the French word under which these "night washerwomen" are perhaps best known.

statement.id: Bean-nighe (Gaelik Skotlandia, Scottish Gaelic: perempuan pencuci) roh perempuan cerita rakyat Skotlandia (Scottish folklore), pertanda kematian, utusan Dunia Lain (Otherworld); sejenis ban-sìth (Irish bean sídhe, banshee, Banshee); Les Lavandières (French, Prancis); nigheag, nigheag na h-ath, nigheag bheag a bhroin; di Britania Raya.
statement.en: The bean-nighe (Scottish Gaelic washerwoman) is a female spirit of Scottish folklore, an omen of death from the Otherworld; a type of ban-sìth (Irish bean sídhe, banshee); Les Lavandières in French.

basis_claims.quote: is seen in lonely places beside a stream or pool, washing the blood from the linen and grave-clothes of those who are about to die. Her characteristics vary depending on the locality, and differing traditions ascribe to her the powers of imparting knowledge or the granting of wishes if she is approached with caution.

statement.id: Terlihat di tepi sungai sepi mencuci darah dari kain kubur; dapat memberi pengetahuan atau mengabulkan permintaan; Washer at the Ford.
statement.en: Seen by lonely streams washing blood from grave-clothes; can impart knowledge or grant wishes; the Washer at the Ford.

nonhuman_features: Two clearly red nonhuman webbed feet with connecting toe membranes
bean-nighe.historical_basis: Online-verified current Bean-nighe article records red webbed feet and cites Briggs 1976 pp.16,19; chosen as a single physical variant. Campbell primary text separately supports washer identity and atmosphere.
bean-nighe.artistic_changes: Toe-ray number and membrane contour are unspecified by source and rendered artistically; cloth color and seated dry-stone pose make sourced webbed feet visible without mixing other variants.

additional_sources.title: Bean-nighe: Legends, physical variants
additional_sources.locator: Legends paragraph citing Katharine Briggs (1976), pp.16,19
additional_sources.purpose: Explicit red webbed feet bodily variant independently rechecked online; does not merge one-nostril or big-front-tooth alternatives.

additional_sources.title: John Gregorson Campbell (1900), Superstitions of the Highlands and Islands of Scotland
additional_sources.locator: The Bean Nighe, or Washing Woman
additional_sources.purpose: Primary folklore collection confirms stream/linen/washing-stone identity and mournful death-omen role. This primary passage is not cited for red feet.

manannan-mac-lir.depicted_variant: Manannan sea king aboard Wave-sweeper with Fragarach
visual_requirements: Manannan sea king aboard Wave-sweeper with Fragarach
Coherent anatomy and documented mythic scene
manannan-mac-lir.aura: Presence through source-backed form and physical scene; no generic glow, ribbons or magical mist.

basis_claims.quote: Manannán or Manann , also known as Manannán mac Lir ('son of the Sea'), is a sea god, warrior and king of the otherworld in Gaelic (Irish, Manx and Scottish) mythology who is one of the Tuatha Dé Danann .

statement.id: Manannán (Manann, Manannán mac Lir, son of the Sea) adalah dewa laut, pejuang, dan raja dunia lain mitologi Gaelik (Gaelic: Irish, Manx, Scottish), salah satu Tuatha Dé Danann.
statement.en: Manannán (Manann, Manannán mac Lir, son of the Sea) is a sea god, warrior and otherworld king of Gaelic (Irish, Manx, Scottish) myth, one of the Tuatha Dé Danann.

basis_claims.quote: He is said to own a self-navigating boat named Sguaba Tuinne ('Wave-sweeper'), a horse Aonbharr which can course over water as well as land and a deadly strength-sapping sword named Fragarach

statement.id: Ia memiliki perahu Sguaba Tuinne (Wave-sweeper, Penyapu Ombak), kuda Aonbharr yang berlari di air dan darat, dan pedang Fragarach.
statement.en: He owns the boat Sguaba Tuinne (Wave-sweeper), the horse Aonbharr that runs over water and land, and the sword Fragarach.

artistic_changes: Painterly square composition
Clothing, weather and exact setting details are editorial unless identified in claims

presentation_revision.rationale: Replaces ordinary animal presentation with Manannan sea king aboard Wave-sweeper with Fragarach

christmas-elf.depicted_variant: Modern Anglo-American pointed-ear Santa-helper folklore variant
visual_requirements: One short adult toy-maker elf with naturally bodily large pointed ears clearly visible
One head, two arms and two legs, full frame
Cheerful industrious benevolent workshop aura; no film-specific rodent/tail morphology
christmas-elf.aura: Cheerful kindly industrious magical Christmas helper

basis_claims.quote: In English-speaking cultures, Christmas elves are diminutive elves that live with Santa Claus at the North Pole and act as his helpers. Christmas elves are usually depicted as green- or red-clad, with large, pointy ears and wearing pointy hats.

statement.id: Dalam budaya berbahasa Inggris (English-speaking), Christmas elves tinggal bersama Santa Claus di North Pole dan membantunya; berbaju hijau atau merah, bertelinga dan bertopi runcing.
statement.en: In English-speaking cultures Christmas elves live with Santa Claus at the North Pole as helpers, clad in green or red, with pointy ears and hats.

basis_claims.quote: They are most often depicted as humanoids, but sometimes as furry mammals with tails. Santa's elves are often said to make the toys in Santa's workshop and take care of his reindeer, among other tasks.

statement.id: Mereka humanoid atau kadang mamalia berbulu; elf Santa membuat mainan di bengkel Santa dan merawat rusa kutubnya.
statement.en: They are humanoid or sometimes furry mammals; Santa's elves make toys in Santa's workshop and tend his reindeer.

basis_claims.quote: The image of elves in the workshop was popularized by Godey's Lady's Book, with a front cover illustration for its 1873 Christmas issue showing Santa surrounded by toys and elves

statement.id: Gambaran elf di bengkel dipopulerkan Godey's Lady's Book lewat sampul edisi Natal (Christmas) 1873.
statement.en: The image of elves in the workshop was popularized by Godey's Lady's Book on its 1873 Christmas cover.

nonhuman_features: Two elongated pointed bodily ears
christmas-elf.historical_basis: Current reviewed Christmas-elf c01 explicitly documents green/red clothing, pointed ears and pointed hats; c02 workshop toy-making, c05 1873 workshop illustration popularization. Uses modern folk/popular iconography documented in research, not claiming pointed-ear anatomy in all ancient elves. Smithsonian's 1940/1948 Jump Jump elf collection directly documents pointed ears in early popular elf imagery; LoC Folklife study confirms North-Pole elf toy helpers in Father Christmas tradition.
artistic_changes: Anonymous toy-maker character, clothing texture and workshop details interpreted within current described variant
Avoids copyrighted specific film designs and furry/tail version

additional_sources.title: Jump Jump Marionette
additional_sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
additional_sources.basis: Collection description of 1940/1948 popular elf with pointed ears; supporting modern elf iconography rather than identifying this anonymous character as Jump Jump

additional_sources.title: Christmas Cousins: Father Christmas and Santa Claus
additional_sources.publisher: Library of Congress American Folklife Center
additional_sources.basis: North-Pole elves making/obtaining toys in twentieth-century Christmas tradition

gagoze.depicted_variant: Toriyama Sekien's Gazu Hyakki Yagyo (1776) crawling monk-robed oni
visual_requirements: One hornless grotesque monk-robed oni crawling on two arms and two legs
Elongated bent claw fingers, sharp teeth and distorted oni jaw clearly visible
Entire four-limb figure inside frame, nocturnal menacing temple-stalker aura
gagoze.aura: Menacing furtive nocturnal Gangō-ji temple demon

basis_claims.quote: Gagoze (元興寺), also gagoji, guwagoze, gangō, and gangōji no oni (元興寺の鬼, the oni of gangōji) is a yōkai said to have appeared at Gangō-ji in the Nara Prefecture around the Asuka period.

statement.id: Gagoze adalah yōkai yang konon menghantui Gangō-ji di Nara.
statement.en: Gagoze is a yōkai said to haunt Gangō-ji in Nara.

basis_claims.quote: In classical yōkai drawings such as the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō by Toriyama Sekien, it is depicted as an oni with the appearance of a monk.

statement.id: Ilustrasi lama menggambarkannya sebagai oni mirip biksu.
statement.en: Old illustrations portray it as an oni resembling a monk.

basis_claims.quote: He appears as a hideous demon dressed in monks robes, crawling about on all fours.

statement.id: Gambaran lain menyebut ia merangkak dengan empat anggota tubuh.
statement.en: Another description has it crawl on all fours.

nonhuman_features: Elongated bony claw hands and feet with hooked nails
Grotesque oni jaw and prominent sharp canine teeth
gagoze.historical_basis: Individually inspected Sekien's 1776 Gagoze plate (Commons scan of primary historical illustration): temple-eave crawling robed oni with distorted open-jawed face and very long claw fingers. Current research c03 identifies monk-like oni, c04 four-limb crawling. Retains source morphology without adding generic horns/wings.
artistic_changes: Painterly color, moonlit temple location and exact claw lengths interpreted from monochrome plate
Both hind feet made visible for four-limb review; no invented additional appendages
