statement.en: It takes an old woman’s form and makes bean-like sounds.

basis_claims.quote: Kawagoe City, Saitama Prefecture It is said that at the abandoned temple in Shimo-Kosaka-mura, the sound of azuki beans can be heard on a rainy evening.

statement.id: Cerita setempat menempatkan bunyinya di kuil terbengkalai pada petang hujan.
statement.en: A local story places the sound at an abandoned temple on rainy evenings.

nonhuman_features: Yokai identity conveyed by documented old-woman form at temple with bean-sound evocation; no anatomical deformation is claimed
azukibabaa.historical_basis: Miyagi local tale describes an old woman's shape and bean-like sounds at an abandoned temple in rainy evenings; no fixed physical deformation supplied.
artistic_changes: Bean bowl is explicitly an editorial evocation of noises; exact robe, face and lighting are artistic.

di-sma-undar-jordi.depicted_variant: Hidden little Gotland farm guardian glimpsed through a paper hole
visual_requirements: Small humanlike underground figure
Seen through hole in blank paper
Root-lined farm dwelling

basis_claims.quote: or simply di sma, are legendary vættir-like creatures found in folklore from the island of Gotland, Sweden.

statement.id: Di sma undar jordi (Gutnish untuk "yang kecil di bawah tanah", Swedia: de små under jorden), atau singkatnya di sma, adalah makhluk legenda mirip vættir dalam cerita rakyat pulau Gotland, Swedia.
statement.en: Di sma undar jordi (Gutnish for 'the small ones underground', Swedish: de små under jorden), or just di sma, are legendary vættir-like beings in the folklore of the island of Gotland, Sweden.

basis_claims.quote: Di sma are said to take care of farms and the people and animals that live there, as long as one does not anger them. The most classical example of doing so is to mindlessly scald them when disposing hot water outdoors.

statement.id: Di sma konon merawat pertanian beserta manusia dan hewannya selama tidak dibuat marah; contoh paling klasik membuat mereka marah adalah menyiram mereka dengan air panas yang dibuang ke luar tanpa berpikir.
statement.en: Di sma reportedly look after farms and their people and animals unless angered; the classic way to anger them is to scald them carelessly when throwing out hot water.

basis_claims.quote: According to Gotlandic tales, di sma can only be seen by looking through a hole in a sheet of paper.

statement.id: Menurut kisah Gotland, di sma hanya dapat dilihat melalui lubang di selembar kertas.
statement.en: Gotland tales say di sma can only be seen through a hole in a sheet of paper.

basis_claims.quote: Di sma undar jordi (även stavat di sma undar jårdi) är en gotländsk variant på vättar. Enligt folktron är de levande väsen som bor i närheten av människorna och deras gårdar. Man bör inte hälla vatten på dem utan förvarning.

statement.id: Di sma undar jordi (juga dieja di sma undar jårdi) adalah varian Gotland dari vättar; menurut kepercayaan rakyat mereka makhluk hidup yang tinggal dekat manusia dan pertanian mereka, dan tidak boleh disiram air tanpa peringatan.
statement.en: Di sma undar jordi (also spelt di sma undar jårdi) are a Gotland variant of the vättar; folk belief makes them living beings dwelling near people and their farms, who must not have water poured on them without warning.

nonhuman_features: Little underground hidden people visible through a paper hole; no anatomical deformation claimed
di-sma-undar-jordi.historical_basis: Gotland folklore supplies small underground farm beings and a paper-hole visibility motif, with no fixed physical details.
artistic_changes: Exact male appearance, neutral rustic clothing, doorway architecture and lamplight are artistic choices.

witte-wiwer.depicted_variant: Mecklenburg subterranean white woman returning copper brewing vessel
visual_requirements: Humanlike white-clad woman
Old oak roots and underground doorway
Copper brewing vessel

basis_claims.quote: The witte Wiwer, witte Wîwer, witte Wiewer or witte Wiver ( pronounced [ˈvɪtə ˈviːvɐ] ; all meaning 'white women' in Low German; Standard German: weiße Weiber

statement.id: Witte Wiwer, witte Wîwer, witte Wiewer, atau witte Wiver berarti perempuan putih (white women) dalam bahasa Jerman Rendah (Low German); bahasa Jerman baku (Standard German): weiße Weiber.
statement.en: The witte Wiwer, witte Wîwer, witte Wiewer or witte Wiver all mean 'white women' in Low German; Standard German: weiße Weiber.

basis_claims.quote: The witte Wiwer of Mecklenburg dwell in the earth, under shrubs, in small hills, in forest clearings, or beneath the roots of old trees.

statement.id: Witte Wiwer di Mecklenburg tinggal di tanah, di bawah semak, di bukit kecil, di tanah lapang hutan, atau di bawah akar pohon tua.
statement.en: The witte Wiwer of Mecklenburg dwell in the earth, under shrubs, in small hills, forest clearings or beneath old tree roots.

basis_claims.quote: The witte Wiwer might ask to borrow the brewing copper every new moon during twilight hour, taking it away unseen if obliged. Three evenings later, they will return it the very same hour filled with some cans of the beer brewed by them as payment.

statement.id: Witte Wiwer meminjam kuali bir saat bulan baru, lalu tiga malam kemudian mengembalikannya berisi bir buatan mereka sebagai bayaran.
statement.en: The witte Wiwer borrow the brewing copper at new moon and three evenings later return it filled with their own beer as payment.

nonhuman_features: Documented white subterranean woman with brewing repayment motif; no anatomical deformation claimed
witte-wiwer.historical_basis: Low German folklore describes white women beneath roots and their borrowed brewing copper returned with beer.
artistic_changes: Hair, age, exact dress and amber beer depiction are artistic, not canonical anatomy.

korpokkur.depicted_variant: Ainu little fisher sheltered by butterbur roof
visual_requirements: Tiny adult humanlike fisher
Butterbur leaf as dwelling roof
Stream and fish basket context

basis_claims.quote: are a race of little people in folklore of the Ainu people of the northern Japanese islands.

statement.id: Korpokkur adalah kaum kecil dalam folklor Ainu.
statement.en: Korpokkur are little people in Ainu folklore.

basis_claims.quote: They were short of stature, agile, and skilled at fishing. They lived in pits with roofs made from butterbur leaves.

statement.id: Cerita menyebut mereka kecil, pandai memancing, dan tinggal di bawah atap daun butterbur.
statement.en: A tale describes small fishers in pits roofed with butterbur leaves.

basis_claims.quote: The little people hated to be seen, however, so they would stealthily make their deliveries under the cover of night.

statement.id: Mereka enggan terlihat dan memberi barang pada malam hari.
statement.en: They avoid being seen and deliver goods at night.

basis_claims.quote: Long ago, the korpokkur were on good terms with the Ainu, and would send them deer, fish, and other game and exchange goods with them.

statement.id: Mereka bertukar hasil buruan dan ikan dengan orang Ainu dalam cerita.
statement.en: The tale describes exchanges of game and fish with the Ainu.

nonhuman_features: Documented little people beneath butterbur roofs; no anatomical deformation claimed
korpokkur.historical_basis: Ainu tale attests small fishing people with butterbur-roofed pits, shy nocturnal exchanges with Ainu.
artistic_changes: Individual face, woven dress, fishery tools and moonlit landscape treatment are artistic.

vidyadhara.depicted_variant: Hindu epic wingless airborne flower-scattering celestial being
visual_requirements: Humanlike celestial being levitating without wings
Scattering flowers with both hands
Reverent joyful divine air setting

basis_claims.quote: are a group of supernatural beings in Indian religions who possess magical powers.

statement.id: Vidyadhara adalah golongan makhluk gaib agama India yang memiliki kekuatan sihir.
statement.en: Vidyadharas are a class of Indian religious supernatural beings possessing magical powers.

basis_claims.quote: In Hinduism, they also attend Shiva, who lives in the Himalayas. They are considered Upadevas, or demi-gods.

statement.id: Dalam Hindu mereka mengiringi Shiva dan digolongkan sebagai setengah dewa.
statement.en: In Hinduism they attend Shiva and are considered demigods.

basis_claims.quote: Vidyādharas are described as essentially spirits of the air. ... strewing flowers watching a combat, rejoicing with music and laughter,

statement.id: Epos Hindu menggambarkan mereka sebagai roh udara yang menabur bunga dan bergembira dengan musik.
statement.en: Hindu epics depict them as air spirits scattering flowers and rejoicing with music.

basis_claims.quote: occupying with the Vidyádharas the middle air or region between the earth and the sun.

statement.id: Catatan terjemahan Ramayana Griffith menempatkan Vidyadhara bersama Siddha di udara antara bumi dan matahari.
statement.en: Griffith's Ramayana translation note places Vidyadharas with Siddhas in the air between earth and sun.

nonhuman_features: Documented wingless air-spirit existence and flower scattering; no anatomical deformation claimed
vidyadhara.historical_basis: Hindu epic sources describe semidivine magical air spirits scattering flowers between earth and sun.
artistic_changes: Female appearance, Indian garment, elaborate jewelry and floral head ornament, pose and sunlit clouds are artistic choices.

munjya.depicted_variant: Konkan unmarried boy ghost with sacred thread in peepal tree
visual_requirements: Humanlike boy apparition
Peepal branches and heart-shaped leaves
Thin diagonal sacred thread

basis_claims.quote: According to folklore in Maharashtra and the Konkan coast, Munjya is believed to be the ghosts of boys who died after this ceremony but before marriage, inhabiting peepal trees.

statement.id: Munjya adalah hantu anak laki-laki yang menurut cerita rakyat Maharashtra dan pesisir Konkan meninggal setelah upacara benang suci tetapi sebelum menikah.
statement.en: Munjya are ghosts of boys who, in Maharashtra and Konkan folklore, died after the sacred-thread ceremony but before marriage.

basis_claims.quote: Munjya is believed to be the ghosts of boys who died after this ceremony but before marriage, inhabiting peepal trees.

statement.id: Mereka dipercaya menghuni pohon peepal.
statement.en: They are believed to inhabit peepal trees.

basis_claims.quote: Munjya's are described as restless bachelor ghosts who roam trees at night, possessing cleverness and multilingual abilities.

statement.id: Sebagian cerita menggambarkan hantu bujang yang gelisah, cerdik, dan menguasai beberapa bahasa.
statement.en: Some tales describe restless bachelor ghosts with cleverness and multilingual abilities.

basis_claims.quote: While most Munjya's are not harmful, they may retaliate against those who defile their tree homes, potentially pelting offenders with stones or causing accidents.

statement.id: Meskipun umumnya tidak berbahaya, mereka dapat membalas orang yang mengotori pohon tempat tinggalnya.
statement.en: Although usually harmless, they may retaliate against people who defile their tree homes.

nonhuman_features: Documented boy ghost tied to sacred-thread ceremony and peepal dwelling; no anatomical deformation claimed
munjya.historical_basis: Konkan and Maharashtra folklore describes boys dying after sacred-thread ceremony but before marriage, dwelling in peepal trees, often clever and usually harmless.
artistic_changes: Exact boy's face, dhoti, pale treatment, moonlight and coastal landscape are artistic. Cloth drapes shoulder while thread lies over upper torso, rather than entirely over chest cloth.

visual_requirements: Ordinary stern man in ragged fur clothing
Lowered switch and pocket with sweets/cakes/nuts
Solitary snowy cottage visitor
belsnickel.aura: Ambivalent stern and benign Christmas visitor

basis_claims.quote: Belsnickel (also known as Belschnickel, Belznickle, Belznickel, Pelznikel, Pelznickel, Bell Sniggle) is a crotchety, fur-clad Christmas gift-bringer figure in the folklore of the Palatinate region of southwestern Germany along the Rhine, the Saarland, and the Odenwald area of Baden-Württemberg. The figure is also preserved in Pennsylvania Dutch communities and Brazilian-German communities.

statement.id: Belsnickel (juga Belschnickel, Belznickel, Pelznickel, dan lain-lain) adalah sosok pembawa hadiah Natal yang pemarah dan berbaju bulu dalam cerita rakyat Pfalz di barat daya Jerman di sepanjang Rhein, Saarland, dan Odenwald di Baden-Württemberg, dan juga dipertahankan dalam komunitas Pennsylvania Dutch serta Jerman-Brasil.
statement.en: Belsnickel (also Belschnickel, Belznickel, Pelznickel and others) is a crotchety, fur-clad Christmas gift-bringer in the folklore of the Palatinate of south-western Germany along the Rhine, the Saarland and the Odenwald of Baden-Württemberg, also preserved among the Pennsylvania Dutch and German-Brazilians.

basis_claims.quote: Belsnickel is related to other companions of Saint Nicholas in the folklore of German-speaking Europe. He may have been based on an older German myth, Knecht Ruprecht ... Unlike those figures, Belsnickel does not accompany Saint Nicholas but instead visits alone and combines both the threatening and the benign aspects

statement.id: Belsnickel berkerabat dengan pendamping Santo Nikolaus lain dalam cerita rakyat Eropa berbahasa Jerman dan mungkin bersumber dari mitos Knecht Ruprecht; namun ia tidak mendampingi Nikolaus, melainkan datang sendiri dan memadukan sisi mengancam dan sisi baik.
statement.en: Belsnickel is related to other companions of Saint Nicholas in German-speaking folklore and may be based on the Knecht Ruprecht myth; but he visits alone rather than with Nicholas, combining threatening and benign aspects.

basis_claims.quote: Belsnickel is a man wearing fur. He is typically very ragged and disheveled. He wears torn, tattered, and dirty clothes, and he carries a switch in his hand with which to beat naughty children, but also pockets full of cakes, candies, and nuts for good children.

statement.id: Belsnickel adalah lelaki berbaju bulu yang compang-camping dan kumal, membawa ranting untuk memukul anak nakal sekaligus saku penuh kue, permen, dan kacang untuk anak baik.
statement.en: Belsnickel is a fur-wearing man, ragged and dishevelled, carrying a switch to beat naughty children and pockets full of cakes, sweets and nuts for good ones.

basis_claims.quote: The traditional Belsnickel showed up at houses 1–2 weeks before Christmas ... He would rap on the door or window with his stick and often the children would have to answer a question for him or sing some type of song. In exchange he would toss candies onto the floor. If the children jumped too quick for the treats, they may end up getting struck with Belsnickel's switch.

statement.id: Belsnickel tradisional datang ke rumah-rumah satu atau dua minggu sebelum Natal, mengetuk pintu atau jendela dengan tongkat, meminta anak menjawab pertanyaan atau bernyanyi, lalu melempar permen ke lantai; anak yang terlalu cepat menyambar bisa terkena rantingnya.
statement.en: The traditional Belsnickel came to houses one or two weeks before Christmas, rapped on door or window with his stick, had children answer a question or sing, then tossed sweets on the floor; those who jumped too fast might be struck with his switch.

nonhuman_features: Traditional fur-clad solitary folkloric gift-bringer and disciplinary switch motif; no anatomical deformation claimed
belsnickel.historical_basis: Palatinate tradition identifies ragged fur-wearing man arriving alone with switch and pockets of cakes, sweets and nuts.
artistic_changes: Exact face, fur cap, bundle of thin switch twigs, rural doorway and snow are artistic choices.

egil-brother-of-volund.depicted_variant: Human legendary master archer at northern keep
visual_requirements: Adult human archer
Wooden bow and quiver
Keep evoking documented defense motif

basis_claims.quote: Egil is a legendary hero of the Völundarkviða and the Thidreks saga. The name is from Proto-Germanic *Agilaz, and the same legend is reflected in Old English Ægil [ˈæɡil] of the Franks Casket and Alamannic Aigil of the Pforzen buckle.

statement.id: Egil adalah pahlawan legendaris Völundarkviða dan Thidreks saga; namanya dari Proto-Jermanik *Agilaz, dan legenda yang sama tercermin pada Ægil dalam bahasa Inggris Kuno di Peti Franks dan Aigil dalam bahasa Alemannik di gesper Pforzen.
statement.en: Egil is a legendary hero of the Völundarkviða and Thidreks saga; his name comes from Proto-Germanic *Agilaz, and the same legend appears in Old English Ægil on the Franks Casket and Alamannic Aigil on the Pforzen buckle.

basis_claims.quote: The Proto-Germanic form of the legend may only be guessed at, but it appears likely that Egil was a renowned archer who defended a keep together with his wife Alruna, against numerous attackers. ... The Franks Casket shows the scene of Aegil and his wife enclosed in the keep, with Aegil shooting arrows against attacking troops.

statement.id: Bentuk Proto-Jermanik legenda ini hanya bisa ditebak, tetapi tampaknya Egil adalah pemanah termasyhur yang bersama istrinya Alruna mempertahankan benteng dari banyak penyerang; Peti Franks menampilkan Aegil dan istrinya di dalam benteng, Aegil memanahi pasukan penyerang.
statement.en: The Proto-Germanic legend can only be guessed at, but Egil seems to have been a renowned archer who with his wife Alruna defended a keep against many attackers; the Franks Casket shows Aegil and his wife in the keep, Aegil shooting at attacking troops.

basis_claims.quote: In the Völundarkviða, Egil is a son of a Finn king, his elder brother being Slagfiðr, his younger one Völund. The three brothers marry valkyries they encounter in swans' form ... while Egil marries Ölrún, a daughter of the Roman Emperor (Kiár of Valland).

statement.id: Dalam Völundarkviða, Egil adalah putra raja Finn dengan kakak Slagfiðr dan adik Völund; ketiganya menikahi valkyrie yang mereka temui dalam rupa angsa, dan Egil menikahi Ölrún, putri Kaisar Romawi (Kiár dari Valland).
statement.en: In the Völundarkviða Egil is a Finnish king's son, Slagfiðr his elder and Völund his younger brother; the three marry valkyries met in swan form, Egil marrying Ölrún, daughter of the Roman Emperor (Kiár of Valland).

basis_claims.quote: In the Thidreks saga, Egil acts as a masterly archer, once he is forced by king Nidung to shoot an apple from the head of his son. He readies two arrows, but succeeds with the first one.

statement.id: Dalam Thidreks saga, Egil adalah pemanah ulung yang pernah dipaksa Raja Nidung memanah apel dari kepala putranya; ia menyiapkan dua anak panah tetapi berhasil dengan yang pertama.
statement.en: In the Thidreks saga Egil is a master archer once forced by King Nidung to shoot an apple from his son's head; he readies two arrows but succeeds with the first.

nonhuman_features: No nonhuman anatomy claimed: source describes legendary hero and master archer, not a creature with deformed body
egil-brother-of-volund.historical_basis: Völundarkviða and Thidreks saga identify Egil as legendary archer and Volund's brother; keep-defense visual motif documented by Franks Casket discussion.
artistic_changes: Exact face, beard, blue tunic decoration, cloak, boots, bow construction and landscape are artistic historical treatment.

gnome-king-kyrie.depicted_variant: Tiny nocturnal kabouter ruler at Hoogeloon tumulus
visual_requirements: Single small humanlike kabouter king
Nighttime mound dwelling
Dignified secretive watchful ruler

basis_claims.quote: is, according to local folklore, the leader of the legendary gnomes (kabouters) who lived in the Campine region of the province of North Brabant, the Netherlands. These gnomes had their base in the village of Hoogeloon. ... According to tradition the gnome king Kyrië lived on the Kerkakkers in the Kabouterberg ("gnome mountain"), also known as Duivelsberg ("devil's mountain"), a tumulus

statement.id: Menurut cerita rakyat setempat, Raja Kurcaci Kyrië adalah pemimpin kabouter legendaris di wilayah Kempen, Brabant Utara, Belanda, para kabouter berpangkalan di desa Hoogeloon, dan Kyrië tinggal di Kerkakkers di Kabouterberg ("gunung kurcaci") atau Duivelsberg ("gunung setan"), sebuah tumulus.
statement.en: By local folklore, Gnome King Kyrië led the legendary kabouters of the Campine, North Brabant, the Netherlands; based in Hoogeloon, they travelled into neighbouring lands, and Kyrië lived on the Kerkakkers in the Kabouterberg ('gnome mountain') or Duivelsberg ('devil's mountain'), a tumulus.

basis_claims.quote: The gnomes of the Campine were helpful creatures who helped mostly farmers and households in the Campine and also in the neighboring lands of the Peel and the Meierij. They came by night and did not want to be seen by people. If people did see them, they were punished by the gnomes. One story tells of an inquisitive farmer who spied on the gnomes and later became blind in one eye as a punishment.

statement.id: Kabouter Kempen adalah makhluk penolong yang terutama membantu petani dan rumah tangga di Kempen, Peel, dan Meierij; mereka datang di malam hari dan tak ingin dilihat, dan orang yang melihat mereka dihukum, seperti petani penasaran yang buta sebelah matanya.
statement.en: The Campine gnomes were helpful beings aiding farmers and households in the Campine, the Peel and the Meierij; they came at night, did not want to be seen, and punished those who saw them, like a curious farmer blinded in one eye.

nonhuman_features: Documented kabouter kingship and nocturnal mound dwelling; small humanlike form chosen, no anatomical deformation claimed
gnome-king-kyrie.historical_basis: Local Campine folklore names Kyrië leader of helpful nocturnal kabouters dwelling at Kabouterberg tumulus near Hoogeloon; does not supply fixed individual morphology.
artistic_changes: Elderly bearded male appearance, miniature staging, simple circlet as kingship symbol, clothes and doorway are artistic choices, not claimed historical costume.

changeling.depicted_variant: Irish fairy child substitute with documented old-man beard
visual_requirements: Child-sized fictional fairy substitute
Old-man beard
Clever knowing expression in cottage
changeling.aura: Quiet uncanny mature intelligence in small fairy form

basis_claims.quote: A changeling, also historically referred to as an auf or oaf, is a human-like creature found throughout much of European folklore. According to folklore, a changeling was a substitute left by a supernatural being when kidnapping a human being.

statement.id: Changeling (auf atau oaf) adalah makhluk mirip manusia dalam cerita rakyat Eropa (European folklore), pengganti yang ditinggalkan makhluk gaib saat menculik manusia. Dulu disebut dalam bahasa Inggris (English) dan dikenal di Eropa (Europe).
statement.en: A changeling (auf or oaf) is a human-like creature of European folklore, a substitute left by a supernatural being when kidnapping a human.

basis_claims.quote: Although sometimes it was a "stock" (a piece of wood made magically to resemble the kidnapped human), more often the changeling was a supernatural being made magically to look like the kidnapped human.

statement.id: Kadang changeling sepotong kayu (stock) yang disihir, lebih sering makhluk gaib yang disihir menyerupai korban.
statement.en: Sometimes the changeling was a stock of wood, more often a supernatural being magically made to look like the victim.

basis_claims.quote: In Irish legend, a fairy child may appear sickly and will not grow in size like a normal child, and may have notable physical characteristics such as a beard or long teeth. They may also display intelligence far beyond their apparent years and possess uncanny insight.

statement.id: Dalam legenda Irlandia (Irish), anak peri tampak sakit, tak tumbuh, berjanggut atau bergigi panjang, dan cerdas melampaui usianya.
statement.en: In Irish legend a fairy child looks sickly, does not grow, may have a beard or long teeth, and is clever beyond its years.

nonhuman_features: Source-attested old-man beard on child-sized fairy substitute
changeling.historical_basis: Irish legend specifically permits a fairy substitute with beard and cleverness beyond its apparent years; selected beard feature without illness or long teeth.
artistic_changes: Exact youthful face, beard length, rural nightshirt, chair and candlelit cottage are artistic choices.

huldufolk.depicted_variant: Humanlike Nordic hidden person with subtle convex philtrum treatment
visual_requirements: Humanlike hidden person
Rocky mound dwelling
Quiet secretive supernatural neighbor
huldufolk.aura: Still secretive nature neighbor appearing at dusk

basis_claims.quote: In Nordic folklore, including the Northern Isles, hidden-folk (Faroese and Icelandic: huldufólk ; Norwegian: huldrefolk ),

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Nordik (Nordic folklore), termasuk Northern Isles, hidden-folk: Faroe dan Islandia (Faroese and Icelandic) huldufólk, Norwegia (Norwegian) huldrefolk; mencakup elf, wight, brownie (nisse), troll; di Islandia dan Kepulauan Faroe.
statement.en: In Nordic folklore, including the Northern Isles, hidden-folk: Faroese and Icelandic huldufólk, Norwegian huldrefolk; covering elves, wights, brownies (nisse), trolls.

basis_claims.quote: They are supernatural beings that live in nature. They look and behave similarly to humans, but live in a parallel world. They can make themselves visible at will.

statement.id: Makhluk gaib di alam, mirip manusia, hidup di dunia sejajar, bisa menampakkan diri sesuka hati.
statement.en: Supernatural beings of nature, humanlike, in a parallel world, visible at will.

basis_claims.quote: Konrad von Maurer cites a 19th-century Icelandic source claiming that the only visible difference between normal people and outwardly human-appearing huldufólk is, the latter have a convex rather than concave philtrum

statement.id: Konrad von Maurer mengutip sumber Islandia (Icelandic) abad ke-19: beda satu-satunya philtrum mereka cembung.
statement.en: Konrad von Maurer cites a 19th-century Icelandic source: their philtrum is convex.

basis_claims.quote: Their dwellings are in mounds, and they are also called Elves." Some Icelandic folk tales caution against throwing stones, as it may hit the hidden people.

statement.id: Dalam dongeng Faroe (Faroese) mereka tinggal di gundukan (disebut juga Elves); dongeng Islandia (Icelandic) melarang melempar batu.
statement.en: In Faroese tales they dwell in mounds (also called Elves); Icelandic tales warn against throwing stones.

basis_claims.quote: terme islandais signifiant littéralement en français « peuple caché », est composé des créatures des légendes et croyances du folklore islandais. Il s'agit d'elfes, de trolls et de personnes invisibles qui vivent préférentiellement dans les montagnes et les rochers où ils construisent leurs villes, les Álagablettur.

statement.id: Huldufólk berarti orang tersembunyi (peuple caché), makhluk folklore Islandia (islandais): elf, troll, orang tak kasat mata di gunung dan batu, kota mereka Álagablettur; juga di Kepulauan Faroe.
statement.en: Huldufólk means hidden people (peuple caché), beings of Icelandic (islandais) folklore: elves, trolls and invisible people in mountains and rocks, their towns the Álagablettur.

nonhuman_features: Humanlike hidden person; subtle convex philtrum requested from reported nineteenth-century variant, no other anatomical deformation claimed
huldufolk.historical_basis: Nordic accounts describe humanlike hidden nature people of rocks or mounds; one nineteenth-century Icelandic source reports a convex philtrum. Face detail is subtle, not diagnostic at normal display scale.
artistic_changes: Individual female face, exact rustic clothing, rocky coastal location and mound doorway are artistic choices; combines general Nordic hidden-folk setting motifs without claiming one exact local account.

kabouter.depicted_variant: Dutch miniature bearded household helper in red pointed cap
visual_requirements: Tiny humanlike man beside large stable bucket
Long full beard
Tall red pointed cloth hat

basis_claims.quote: is a gnome-like creature in Dutch folklore. The Dutch Kabouter is akin to the Irish leprechaun, Scandinavian tomte or nisse , the English hob, the Scottish brownie and the German Klabauter or kobold.

statement.id: Kabouter adalah makhluk mirip gnom dalam cerita rakyat Belanda, sekerabat dengan leprechaun Irlandia, tomte atau nisse Skandinavia, hob Inggris, brownie Skotlandia, dan Klabauter atau kobold Jerman.
statement.en: The kabouter is a gnome-like creature of Dutch folklore, akin to the Irish leprechaun, Scandinavian tomte or nisse, English hob, Scottish brownie and German Klabauter or kobold.

basis_claims.quote: In the folklore of the Low Countries, kabouters are tiny people, about 10–15 cm tall, who live in or near houses and stables, or in hills, in forests or on heaths. Many stories refer to vast kabouter kingdoms

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Negeri-Negeri Rendah, kabouter adalah orang mungil setinggi sekitar 10–15 cm yang tinggal di dalam atau dekat rumah dan kandang, atau di bukit, hutan, dan padang; banyak kisah menyebut kerajaan kabouter yang luas.
statement.en: In Low Countries folklore kabouters are tiny people about 10–15 cm tall living in or near houses and stables, or in hills, forests or heaths; many tales mention vast kabouter kingdoms.

basis_claims.quote: Kabouters can be regarded as spirits who help in the home by doing tasks at night and care for the animals like milking them. ... The males have long, full beards and they all wear tall, pointed hats, generally of a red or green colour. Kabouters are shy of humans and in stories often punish people for spying on them.

statement.id: Kabouter dapat dipandang sebagai roh yang membantu di rumah dengan bekerja di malam hari dan merawat ternak seperti memerah susu; yang jantan berjanggut panjang lebat dan semuanya memakai topi tinggi runcing berwarna merah atau hijau; mereka pemalu dan sering menghukum orang yang mengintip.
statement.en: Kabouters can be seen as spirits who help at home by working at night and tending animals such as milking; males have long full beards, all wear tall pointed red or green hats, and they are shy and often punish people who spy on them.

basis_claims.quote: Blinding was a common punishment for spying on the gnomes, but they could also make life more difficult by souring the milk, blackening the grain, making objects disappear, or scaring the livestock. Leaving milk and bread out for kabouters was a way to improve relationships with them. ... they exist under a number of different local names such as alvermanneke or auwelke .

statement.id: Kebutaan adalah hukuman umum bagi pengintip, tetapi mereka juga bisa mengasamkan susu, menghitamkan biji-bijian, melenyapkan barang, atau menakuti ternak; meninggalkan susu dan roti dapat memperbaiki hubungan dengan mereka, dan mereka punya berbagai nama lokal seperti alvermanneke atau auwelke.
statement.en: Blinding was a common punishment for spying, but they could also sour milk, blacken grain, make objects vanish or scare livestock; leaving out milk and bread improved relations, and they have various local names such as alvermanneke or auwelke.

nonhuman_features: Attested tiny scale about 10-15 cm, long male beard and tall pointed cloth hat; no anatomical deformation claimed
kabouter.historical_basis: Low Countries kabouter folklore supplies 10-15 cm little people, male beards, red or green pointed hats and nighttime domestic/animal care.
artistic_changes: Exact face, brown work clothes, milk bowl and lantern are artistic choices; scale is conveyed by stable bucket rather than measurement.

heinzelmannchen.depicted_variant: Cologne tiny nocturnal tailor helper in pointed cap
visual_requirements: Small humanlike household artisan
Pointed cloth cap
Nighttime workshop sewing

basis_claims.quote: are helpful household spirits or kobolds associated with the city of Cologne in Germany, akin to brownies of Scotland.

statement.id: Heinzelmännchen adalah roh rumah tangga penolong atau kobold yang dikaitkan dengan kota Köln di Jerman, mirip brownie dari Skotlandia.
statement.en: The Heinzelmännchen are helpful household spirits or kobolds associated with Cologne in Germany, akin to the brownies of Scotland.

basis_claims.quote: The little house gnomes are said to have done all the work of the citizens of Cologne during the night, so that the inhabitants of Cologne could be very lazy during the day. ... this went on until a tailor's wife got so curious to see the gnomes that she scattered peas onto the floor of the workshop to make the gnomes slip and fall. This infuriated the gnomes, who disappeared and never returned.

statement.id: Gnom-gnom rumah kecil itu konon mengerjakan semua pekerjaan warga Köln di malam hari sehingga penduduk bisa bermalas-malasan di siang hari, sampai istri seorang penjahit yang ingin melihat mereka menaburkan kacang polong di lantai bengkel agar mereka terpeleset; mereka murka, menghilang, dan tak pernah kembali.
statement.en: The little house gnomes are said to have done all of Cologne's work at night so the citizens could be lazy by day, until a tailor's wife, curious to see them, scattered peas on the workshop floor to make them slip; infuriated, they vanished and never returned.

basis_claims.quote: Die Heinzelmännchen waren der Sage nach Kölner Hausgeister. Sie verrichteten nachts, wenn die Bürger schliefen, deren Arbeit. ... Neben ihrer geringen Größe zeigen auch typische Attribute, wie die Zipfelmütze und ihr Fleiß, dass die Heinzelmännchen zur Gruppe der Kobolde, Wichtel und Zwerge gehören.

statement.id: Menurut sage, Heinzelmännchen adalah roh rumah Köln yang mengerjakan pekerjaan warga di malam hari saat mereka tidur; ukuran kecil, topi runcing, dan kerajinannya menunjukkan mereka segolongan dengan kobold, Wichtel, dan kurcaci.
statement.en: By legend the Heinzelmännchen were Cologne house spirits who did the citizens' work at night while they slept; their small size, pointed cap and diligence mark them as kin of kobolds, Wichtel and dwarfs.

basis_claims.quote: Populär geworden ist sie in der Gedichtfassung (Ballade) von 1836 des Malers und Dichters August Kopisch (1799–1853), mit der er die ursprünglich rheinländische Sage aus dem Siebengebirge nach Köln transportierte

statement.id: Kisah ini menjadi populer lewat versi puisi (balada) tahun 1836 karya pelukis dan penyair August Kopisch, yang memindahkan sage asal Siebengebirge di Rheinland ke Köln.
statement.en: The tale became popular through the 1836 ballad by the painter and poet August Kopisch, who moved the originally Rhineland legend from the Siebengebirge to Cologne.

nonhuman_features: Source-attested small house-spirit scale and pointed cap; no anatomical deformation claimed
heinzelmannchen.historical_basis: Cologne legend describes helpful small house spirits working at night, with pointed cap, including tailor workshop narrative.
artistic_changes: Youthful adult artisan appearance, red cap color, exact work clothes, needle, spool and Gothic city window are artistic scene details.

nis-puk.depicted_variant: Helpful Schleswig household/barn guardian receiving butter porridge
visual_requirements: Small unobtrusive humanlike barn spirit
Barn attic setting
Porridge bowl with butter

basis_claims.quote: The Nis Puk (sometimes also Niß Puk ( German: [ˈnɪs pʊk] )) is a legendary creature, a kind of Kobold, from Danish-, Low German- and North Frisian-speaking areas of Northern Germany and Southern Denmark, among them Schleswig, today divided into the German Southern Schleswig and Danish Northern Schleswig. It is also known in Denmark itself as nis pug , as a variant of nisse.

statement.id: Nis Puk (juga Niß Puk) adalah makhluk legenda sejenis kobold dari wilayah berbahasa Denmark, Jerman Rendah, dan Frisia Utara di Jerman utara dan Denmark selatan, termasuk Schleswig; di Denmark ia juga disebut nis pug, varian nisse.
statement.en: Nis Puk (also Niß Puk) is a legendary kobold-like creature from Danish-, Low German- and North Frisian-speaking northern Germany and southern Denmark, including Schleswig; in Denmark it is also nis pug, a variant of the nisse.

basis_claims.quote: Depending on the place, it can either appear as a domestic spirit or take on the role of a being generally called Drak or Kobold in Danish and German mythology, an infernal spirit making its owner wealthy by bringing them stolen goods.

statement.id: Tergantung tempatnya, ia bisa tampil sebagai roh rumah tangga atau berperan sebagai makhluk yang disebut Drak atau kobold dalam mitologi Denmark dan Jerman, roh dari neraka yang membuat pemiliknya kaya dengan membawakan barang curian.
statement.en: Depending on place, it may appear as a domestic spirit or take the role of what Danish and German mythology call a Drak or kobold, an infernal spirit enriching its owner with stolen goods.

basis_claims.quote: Der Nis Puk soll auf Haus, Hof und Tiere achtgeben ... Der Nis Puk soll auf dem Dachboden oder in einer Scheune leben. Angeblich können ihn Erwachsene nicht mehr sehen. Einmal im Jahr, zu Weihnachten, muss dem Nis Puk eine Schüssel Grütze (mit Butter) gebracht werden. Geschieht das nicht, wandert der Nis Puk in ein anderes Dorf.

statement.id: Nis Puk menjaga rumah, halaman, dan ternak; ia tinggal di loteng atau lumbung, tak terlihat oleh orang dewasa, dan setahun sekali saat Natal harus diberi semangkuk bubur bermentega, bila tidak ia pindah ke desa lain.
statement.en: Nis Puk looks after house, yard and animals; he lives in the attic or barn, unseen by adults, and once a year at Christmas must get a bowl of porridge with butter, or he moves to another village.

basis_claims.quote: Figuren forbinder den dansk-skånsk-norske nisse med den engelske puk ... Han tager sig af huset og dyrene, hvis beboerne er villige til at behandle deres egne børn og dyr godt. ... Huset ville så være udsat for forfald og ulykker. ... Et ordsprog fra øen Sild siger på sildfrisisk Hi glüüret üs en pük (≈Han stirrer som en Nis Puk). Figuren fandt indgang i flere af Boy Lornsens børnebøger.

statement.id: Figur ini memadukan nisse Denmark-Skåne-Norwegia dengan puk Inggris; ia menjaga rumah dan hewan bila penghuni bersedia memperlakukan anak dan hewan mereka dengan baik; tanpa bubur rumah itu terancam kerusakan dan malapetaka; pepatah Sylt berbunyi "Hi glüüret üs en pük" (ia menatap seperti Nis Puk), dan ia muncul dalam buku-buku anak Boy Lornsen.
statement.en: The figure combines the Danish-Scanian-Norwegian nisse with the English puk; he looks after house and animals if the occupants treat their own children and animals well; without porridge the house faces decay and misfortune; a Sylt saying runs 'Hi glüüret üs en pük' (he stares like a Nis Puk), and he features in Boy Lornsen's children's books.

nonhuman_features: Documented household kobold/nisse identity, unseen barn residence and butter-porridge relationship; no anatomical deformation claimed
nis-puk.historical_basis: Schleswig Nis Puk helpful variant looks after home and animals, lives in attic/barn and expects Christmas butter porridge. Source does not prescribe fixed individual anatomy.
artistic_changes: Small bearded humanlike man, soft brown cloth cap, rustic clothes, exact scale and barn lighting are artistic appearance choices.

leanan-sidhe.depicted_variant: Female Irish Aos Si dangerous inspirational lover
visual_requirements: Beautiful adult humanlike fairy woman
Modest rustic clothing
Alluring restless uncanny moonlit presence
leanan-sidhe.aura: Inviting but restless life-consuming supernatural muse

basis_claims.quote: is a figure from Celtic mythology. She is depicted as a beautiful woman of the Aos Sí ("people of the fairy mounds") who takes a human lover. Lovers of the leannán sídhe are said to live brief, though highly inspired, lives.

statement.id: Leannán sídhe (Irlandia/Irish, kekasih peri; Scottish Gaelic leannan sìth; Manx lhiannan shee) sosok mitologi Kelt (Celtic), perempuan Aos Sí yang mengambil kekasih manusia; di Irlandia. (Skotlandia)
statement.en: The leannán sídhe (Irish, fairy lover; Scottish Gaelic leannan sìth; Manx lhiannan shee) is a Celtic figure, an Aos Sí woman taking a human lover.

basis_claims.quote: A version of the myth was popularized during the Celtic Revival in the late 19th-century. The leannán sídhe is mentioned by Jane Wilde, writing as "Speranza", in her 1887 Ancient Legends, Mystic Charms and Superstitions of Ireland.

statement.id: Dipopulerkan saat Kebangkitan Kelt (Celtic Revival); Jane Wilde (Speranza), Ancient Legends, Mystic Charms and Superstitions of Ireland (1887).
statement.en: Popularised in the Celtic Revival; Jane Wilde (Speranza), Ancient Legends, Mystic Charms and Superstitions of Ireland (1887).

basis_claims.quote: W. B. Yeats popularized his own 'newly-ancient' version of the leannán sídhe, emphasizing the spirit's almost vampiric tendencies. As he imagined it, the leannán sídhe is depicted as a beautiful muse who offers inspiration to an artist in exchange for their love and devotion; although the supernatural affair leads to madness and eventual death for the artist

statement.id: W. B. Yeats: muse cantik yang hampir vampirik, memberi ilham demi cinta, berujung kegilaan dan kematian.
statement.en: W. B. Yeats: a near-vampiric beautiful muse giving inspiration for love, ending in madness and death.

basis_claims.quote: Die Feen brauchen das Leben ihrer Liebhaber auf und lassen sie auch nach dem Tod nicht entkommen.

statement.id: Para peri (Feen) menghabiskan nyawa kekasihnya dan tak membiarkan mereka lolos setelah mati.
statement.en: The fairies (Feen) use up their lovers' lives and do not let them escape even after death.

basis_claims.quote: The Gaelic poets die young, for she is restless, and will not let them remain long on earth—this malignant phantom.

statement.id: Penyair Gaelik (Gaelic) mati muda karena ia gelisah (menurut W. B. Yeats).
statement.en: Gaelic poets die young, for she is restless (per W. B. Yeats).

nonhuman_features: Source-described female Aos Si fairy lover with dangerous inspiration; no anatomical deformation claimed
leanan-sidhe.historical_basis: Celtic Revival accounts of beautiful fairy lover/muse connect her inspirational allure with lovers' curtailed lives; near-vampiric mood does not justify vampire anatomy.
artistic_changes: Exact face, dark hair, modest Irish rustic dress, mound and moonlit landscape are artistic setting choices. No fangs inferred.

naale-ba.depicted_variant: Karnataka female ghost seeking husband and knocking at night
visual_requirements: Single humanlike female ghost
Hand raised to closed house door
Nocturnal ominous searching aura

basis_claims.quote: is a popular folk legend which features prominently in areas across Karnataka, India. ... It is believed that a malevolent spirit or witch roams around at night

statement.id: Naale Ba adalah legenda roh jahat yang berkeliaran malam hari di Karnataka, India.
statement.en: Naale Ba is a legend of a malevolent spirit roaming at night in Karnataka, India.

basis_claims.quote: In some variations, people believed that a demon roams around, knocks on doors and calls out names of people imitating the voice of their kin.

statement.id: Dalam satu versi ia mengetuk pintu dan meniru suara kerabat saat memanggil penghuni.
statement.en: In one version it knocks on doors and imitates relatives when calling residents.

basis_claims.quote: There are also variations of the story where the spirit is believed to be a female ghost in search of her husband. She is known to take away the man of the house,

statement.id: Versi lain menyebut hantu perempuan yang mencari suaminya dan membawa pergi lelaki penghuni rumah.
statement.en: Another version describes a female ghost seeking her husband and taking away a male resident.

nonhuman_features: Documented female ghost and door-knocking nocturnal behavior; no anatomical deformation claimed
naale-ba.historical_basis: Karnataka versions describe spirit knocking and imitating relatives; selected female ghost seeking husband, with no source-defined monstrous anatomy.
artistic_changes: Exact woman's face, long hair, simple sari, moonlight and rural door architecture are artistic. No protective writing rendered.

fasolt.depicted_variant: Medieval Eckenlied giant knight with very long braided hair
visual_requirements: Giant humanlike knight
Very long thick plaits below waist
Plain medieval mail and stormy mountain pass

basis_claims.quote: Fasolt, Fasold or Vasolt is a giant or knight who appears in the following works: The Middle High German heroic poem Eckenlied (c. 1230). The Old Norse compendium of German legends known as the Thidrekssaga (c. 1250).

statement.id: Fasolt (Fasold, Vasolt) adalah raksasa atau kesatria yang muncul dalam puisi heroik Jerman Tinggi Pertengahan (Middle High German) Eckenlied (sekitar 1230) dan kumpulan legenda Jerman berbahasa Nordik Kuno (Old Norse) Thidrekssaga (sekitar 1250).
statement.en: Fasolt (Fasold, Vasolt) is a giant or knight appearing in the Middle High German heroic poem Eckenlied (c. 1230) and the Old Norse compendium of German legends, the Thidrekssaga (c. 1250).

basis_claims.quote: The name Fasolt likely derives from a root similar to Old High German faso, thread, and most likely refers to the long braided hair he is described as having in the Eckenlied. He may have originally been a storm demon, as evidenced by a 17th-century prayer to witches at the mountain Jochgrimm outside of Bozen to cause "ffasolt" to send storms far away.

statement.id: Nama Fasolt kemungkinan dari akar yang mirip kata Jerman Tinggi Kuno (Old High German) faso, "benang", merujuk rambut panjangnya yang dikepang dalam Eckenlied; ia mungkin semula setan badai, dibuktikan doa abad ke-17 kepada penyihir di gunung Jochgrimm dekat Bozen agar "ffasolt" menjauhkan badai.
statement.en: The name Fasolt likely stems from a root like Old High German faso, 'thread', referring to his long braided hair in the Eckenlied; he may first have been a storm demon, as a 17th-century prayer to witches on Mount Jochgrimm near Bozen asks 'ffasolt' to send storms away.

nonhuman_features: Attested giant scale and conspicuous very long braided hair; no additional anatomical deformation claimed
fasolt.historical_basis: Eckenlied/Thidreks tradition presents Fasolt as giant or knight; Eckenlied long braided hair and possible storm association supply selected motifs, separate from Wagner plot.
artistic_changes: Exact face, two-plait arrangement, mail, boots, giant-to-gateway scale and mountain landscape are artistic choices.

vittra-folklore.depicted_variant: Northern Swedish humanlooking female herding wight
visual_requirements: Ordinary humanlike rural woman
Summer pasture/cattle shed
Single distant cow supporting herding context

basis_claims.quote: A vittra (plural: vittror) is a type of wight (a term for supernatural beings) from northern Sweden. They were associated with herding, either cattle or reindeer; they were believed to live normally among humans and only revealed a supernatural nature if their livestock were mistreated.

statement.id: Vittra (jamak vittror) adalah sejenis wight (makhluk gaib) dari Swedia (Sweden) utara, dikaitkan dengan penggembalaan sapi atau rusa kutub; mereka dipercaya hidup biasa di antara manusia dan hanya menampakkan sifat gaib bila ternaknya diperlakukan buruk.
statement.en: A vittra (plural vittror) is a kind of wight (supernatural being) from northern Sweden, associated with herding cattle or reindeer; they were believed to live normally among humans, revealing their supernatural nature only if their livestock were mistreated.

basis_claims.quote: Like the hulder and the skogsrå, the vittra is also associated with longing and desire. The vittra appears as a beautiful, female wight who seduces men in the forest.

statement.id: Seperti hulder dan skogsrå, vittra dikaitkan dengan kerinduan dan hasrat, tampil sebagai wight perempuan cantik yang menggoda lelaki di hutan.
statement.en: Like the hulder and skogsrå, the vittra is linked with longing and desire, appearing as a beautiful female wight who seduces men in the forest.

basis_claims.quote: De håller till på fäbodvallen under vinterhalvåret då människorna inte är där. Vittra sägs hålla egen boskap, som kallas vitterkor, och dessa kor ansågs som särskilt förtrollade.

statement.id: Vittra tinggal di padang penggembalaan (fäbodvallen) pada musim dingin ketika manusia tak ada, dan memelihara ternak sendiri yang disebut vitterkor, sapi yang dianggap sangat bertuah.
statement.en: The vittra stay on the summer pasture (fäbodvallen) in winter when people are absent, and keep their own cattle called vitterkor, considered especially enchanted.

basis_claims.quote: Vittra ser ut, lever och klär sig som människor, och de är till skillnad från många andra väsen i folktron dödliga.

statement.id: Vittra tampak, hidup, dan berpakaian seperti manusia, dan berbeda dari banyak makhluk lain dalam kepercayaan rakyat, mereka bisa mati.
statement.en: The vittra look, live and dress like people and, unlike many other folk-belief beings, are mortal.

nonhuman_features: Source explicitly human-looking mortal supernatural herding being; no anatomical deformation claimed
vittra-folklore.historical_basis: Northern Swedish vittra lore describes people who look, live and dress like ordinary humans, associated with summer pastures and cattle; selected beautiful female wight manifestation.
artistic_changes: Individual face, red skirt, linen blouse and shawl, cattle-shed architecture and ordinary cow depiction are artistic choices.

wight.depicted_variant: Living German Wichtel small humanlike domestic helper
visual_requirements: Small humanlike living helper
Cave/house corner habitat
Quiet daily-work bucket motif
wight.aura: Friendly modest industrious subterranean house spirit

basis_claims.quote: "Wight" is further cognate with Scots: wicht , German: Wicht , Dutch: Wicht , Gothic: 𐍅𐌰𐌹𐌷𐍄𐍃 and Old Norse: vættr , the ancestor of Swedish: vätte , Danish: vætte and Icelandic: vættur .

statement.id: Wight sekerabat dengan Wicht (German, Jerman), vættr (Old Norse, Nordik Kuno), vätte (Swedish, Swedia), vætte (Danish, Denmark).
statement.en: Wight is cognate with German Wicht, Old Norse vættr, Swedish vätte and Danish vætte.

basis_claims.quote: Als Wichtel werden in Märchen, Sagen und Erzählungen Wesen bezeichnet, die von der Gestalt und Art her menschenähnlich sind, aber deutlich kleiner und in eigenen Gemeinschaften lebend. Sie tauchen meist in Gruppen auf, leben unterirdisch, in Höhlen oder in versteckten Ecken in den Häusern der Menschen.

statement.id: Wichtel dalam dongeng (Märchen) dan legenda (Sagen) mirip manusia (menschenähnlich) tetapi kecil, hidup berkelompok di bawah tanah (unterirdisch), gua (Höhlen), atau sudut rumah (Häusern).
statement.en: Wichtel in tales (Märchen) and legends (Sagen) look human (menschenähnlich) but small, living in groups underground (unterirdisch), in caves (Höhlen) or corners of houses (Häusern).

basis_claims.quote: Wichtel oder Wichtelmännchen ist ein Diminutiv von Wicht, einem Begriff, der im Altdeutschen allgemein für lebendes Wesen, Geschöpf stand.

statement.id: Wichtel adalah bentuk kecil (Diminutiv) dari Wicht, yang dalam bahasa Jerman lama (Altdeutschen) berarti makhluk hidup (lebendes Wesen, Geschöpf).
statement.en: Wichtel is a diminutive (Diminutiv) of Wicht, which in old German (Altdeutschen) meant a living being (lebendes Wesen, Geschöpf).

basis_claims.quote: Im Allgemeinen sind sie den Menschen gegenüber freundlich und helfen ihnen, meist unaufgefordert, bei der täglichen Arbeit. Bisweilen bitten sie ihrerseits die Menschen um Hilfe, manchmal tauschen sie ein menschliches Kind gegen ein eigenes aus.

statement.id: Wichtel ramah (freundlich), membantu pekerjaan sehari-hari (täglichen Arbeit), dan kadang menukar anak manusia (menschliches Kind).
statement.en: Wichtel are friendly (freundlich), help with daily work (täglichen Arbeit), and sometimes swap a human child (menschliches Kind).

nonhuman_features: Attested small humanlike Wichtel and underground/house habitat; no anatomical deformation claimed
wight.historical_basis: Wight is broad linguistic category; image selects German Wichtel described as small humanlike cave or house beings helping daily work, without importing modern undead fantasy.
artistic_changes: Exact face, beard, soft cap, brown clothing, bucket and doorway are artistic details.

durinn.depicted_variant: Human-appearing Norse dwarf smith associated with Tyrfing
visual_requirements: Human-appearing craftsperson without invented anatomy
Forge, tongs and straight sword
Ancient skilled smith atmosphere

basis_claims.quote: is a dwarf according to stanza 10 of the poem Völuspá from the Poetic Edda, and repeated in Gylfaginning from the Prose Edda. He was the second created after the first and foremost dwarf Mótsognir.

statement.id: Durinn (atau Durin) adalah kurcaci menurut bait ke-10 puisi Völuspá dari Edda Puisi, diulang dalam Gylfaginning dari Edda Prosa; ia yang kedua diciptakan setelah kurcaci pertama dan terkemuka, Mótsognir.
statement.en: Durinn (or Durin) is a dwarf according to stanza 10 of the Völuspá in the Poetic Edda, repeated in the Gylfaginning of the Prose Edda; he was the second created after the first and foremost dwarf, Mótsognir.

basis_claims.quote: He is also attested in Hervarar saga, where he forged the magic sword Tyrfing with the help of the dwarf Dvalin. In variant texts of the saga Durinn is known as Dulinn.

statement.id: Ia juga tercatat dalam Hervarar saga, menempa pedang ajaib Tyrfing dibantu kurcaci Dvalin; dalam varian teks saga itu ia disebut Dulinn.
statement.en: He is also attested in Hervarar saga, forging the magic sword Tyrfing with the dwarf Dvalin; in variant texts of the saga he is called Dulinn.

basis_claims.quote: Durin, auch Durinn (altnordisch), war der zweite Zwerg, der von den Göttern in der nordischen Mythologie erschaffen wurde.

statement.id: Durin, juga Durinn (Nordik Kuno), adalah kurcaci kedua yang diciptakan para dewa dalam mitologi Nordik.
statement.en: Durin, also Durinn (Old Norse), was the second dwarf created by the gods in Norse mythology.

basis_claims.quote: Durin (el durmiente) y Mótsognir (de feroz rugido) se formaron de forma espontánea cuando Odín y sus hermanos Vili y Ve crearon el mundo a partir del cuerpo del gigante cósmico Ymir. ... Los dioses les concedieron la inteligencia y una apariencia humana.

statement.id: Durin dan Mótsognir terbentuk dengan sendirinya ketika Odin serta saudaranya Vili dan Ve menciptakan dunia dari tubuh raksasa kosmis Ymir; para dewa lalu memberi mereka akal dan rupa manusia.
statement.en: Durin and Mótsognir formed spontaneously when Odin and his brothers Vili and Ve made the world from the body of the cosmic giant Ymir; the gods then gave them intelligence and human appearance.

nonhuman_features: Source-attested created Norse dwarf with granted human appearance and Tyrfing forging association; no anatomical deformation claimed
durinn.historical_basis: Edda names Durinn a created dwarf; source describes gods granting human appearance; Hervarar saga makes Durinn and Dvalin Tyrfing's smiths. Single selected figure does not claim he forged it alone.
artistic_changes: Exact adult bearded face, normal proportions, leather apron, cavern forge, tongs and heat-glowing sword are artistic details; sword glow is heat rather than claimed magic effect.

visual_requirements: Handsome ordinary adult male water spirit
Coherent fiddle and bow playing
Waterfall setting

basis_claims.quote: Fossegrim, also known simply as the grim (Norwegian) or Strömkarlen (Swedish), is a water spirit or troll in Scandinavian folklore. He is often depicted as a handsome, nude man playing the fiddle in

statement.id: Fossegrim, juga disebut grim (Norwegia) atau Strömkarlen (Swedia), adalah roh air atau troll dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia yang sering digambarkan sebagai lelaki tampan tanpa busana yang bermain biola.
statement.en: Fossegrim, also the grim (Norwegian) or Strömkarlen (Swedish), is a water spirit or troll of Scandinavian folklore, often shown as a handsome naked man playing the fiddle.

basis_claims.quote: Fossegrim is described as an exceptionally talented fiddler: the sounds of forest, wind and water play over his fiddle strings. Fossegrims can be induced to teach the skill. The Swedish strömkarl's lay is said to have eleven variations, the final one being reserved for the night spirits

statement.id: Fossegrim digambarkan sebagai pemain biola yang luar biasa berbakat, yang senarnya memainkan bunyi hutan, angin, dan air; ia dapat dibujuk mengajarkan keahliannya, dan lagu strömkarl Swedia konon punya sebelas variasi, yang terakhir disimpan untuk roh malam.
statement.en: Fossegrim is described as an exceptionally talented fiddler whose strings carry the sounds of forest, wind and water; he can be induced to teach, and the Swedish strömkarl's lay has eleven variations, the last reserved for the night spirits.

basis_claims.quote: Fossegrim è stato associato allo spirito del mulino (kvernknurr) ed è imparentato con lo spirito dell'acqua (nokken) ed è talvolta chiamato anche näcken in Svezia. È associato ai corsi d'acqua (il nome svedese "Strömkarlen" significa "L'uomo del corso d'acqua") e in particolare ai corsi d'acqua a cascata (foss in norvegese)

statement.id: Fossegrim dikaitkan dengan roh penggilingan (kvernknurr), berkerabat dengan roh air (nokken), dan di Swedia kadang disebut näcken; ia terkait aliran air (nama Swedia Strömkarlen berarti "lelaki aliran air"), terutama yang berair terjun (foss dalam bahasa Norwegia).
statement.en: Fossegrim is linked with the mill spirit (kvernknurr), related to the water spirit (nokken) and sometimes called näcken in Sweden; he is tied to watercourses (Swedish Strömkarlen means 'the man of the stream'), especially those with waterfalls (Norwegian foss).

nonhuman_features: Documented handsome human-form water spirit and supernatural fiddling association; no anatomical deformation claimed
fossegrim.historical_basis: Scandinavian folklore presents handsome often-naked man playing fiddle and associated with waterfalls/watercourses. Simple waist cloth is an artistic modesty adaptation, not asserted folklore costume.
artistic_changes: Exact youthful face, long wet hair, linen waist cloth, seated pose, fiddle construction and waterfall scene are artistic choices. Stream's geographical flow direction cannot be inferred from picture.

askafroa.depicted_variant: Humanlike female guardian and soul of living ash tree
visual_requirements: Female being near intact ash tree
Compound pinnate ash leaves
Stern dangerous guardian aura and water at roots

basis_claims.quote: The Askafroa (Swedish: wife of the ash tree ), also known as the Danish Askefrue is a type of legendary creature in Scandinavian folklore, similar to the Greek Hamadryads. The Askafroa is the guardian (tutelary deity) of the ash tree. The Askafroa was thought to be a malicious creature that did much damage, and to appease her, it was necessary to make a sacrifice to her on Ash Wednesday.

statement.id: Askafroa (bahasa Swedia, "istri pohon ash"), dalam bahasa Denmark Askefrue, adalah makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Skandinavia yang mirip hamadryad Yunani, penjaga pohon ash; ia dianggap makhluk jahat yang banyak merusak, sehingga perlu diberi persembahan pada Rabu Abu.
statement.en: The Askafroa (Swedish 'wife of the ash tree'), Danish Askefrue, is a legendary creature of Scandinavian folklore like the Greek hamadryads, guardian of the ash tree; thought malicious and destructive, she had to be appeased with a sacrifice on Ash Wednesday.

basis_claims.quote: The Askafroa lives in ash trees in the Scania region of Sweden, and is said to be a very dangerous creature. She is the soul of the tree and if it is cut down, she will exert revenge.

statement.id: Askafroa tinggal di pohon ash di wilayah Skåne, Swedia, dan disebut sangat berbahaya; ia jiwa pohon itu dan akan membalas dendam bila pohonnya ditebang.
statement.en: The Askafroa lives in ash trees in Skåne, Sweden, and is said to be very dangerous; she is the tree's soul and will take revenge if it is cut down.

basis_claims.quote: The Swedish scholar Hyltén-Cavallius recorded in his ethnographic work Wärend och Wirdarne a belief of a female creature living in the ash tree, in Ljunit Hundred. The elders sacrificed to the Askafroa on the morning of Ash Wednesday. Before the sun had risen, they poured water over the roots of the ash tree.

statement.id: Sarjana Swedia Hyltén-Cavallius mencatat dalam karya etnografinya Wärend och Wirdarne kepercayaan di Ljunit Hundred tentang makhluk perempuan di pohon ash; para tetua berkorban kepadanya pada pagi Rabu Abu dengan menuang air ke akar pohon sebelum matahari terbit.
statement.en: The Swedish scholar Hyltén-Cavallius recorded in his ethnographic work Wärend och Wirdarne a belief in Ljunit Hundred in a female being in the ash tree; the elders sacrificed to her on Ash Wednesday morning, pouring water over the roots before sunrise.

basis_claims.quote: While doing this, they said: "Nu offrar jag, så gör du oss ingen skada", meaning "Now I sacrifice [to you], so that you do us no harm". Hyltén-Cavallius further writes that they believed that if anyone broke branches or twigs from the ash tree, they would become ill.

statement.id: Sambil melakukannya mereka berkata "Nu offrar jag, så gör du oss ingen skada", artinya "Kini aku berkorban [kepadamu], agar kau tidak mencelakai kami"; mereka juga percaya siapa pun yang mematahkan dahan atau ranting pohon ash akan jatuh sakit.
statement.en: While doing so they said 'Nu offrar jag, så gör du oss ingen skada', meaning 'Now I sacrifice [to you], so that you do us no harm'; they also believed anyone breaking branches or twigs from the ash would fall ill.

nonhuman_features: Documented female tree-dwelling guardian/soul of ash tree; no anatomical deformation claimed
askafroa.historical_basis: Skåne folklore attests female ash-tree guardian, harmful if offended, with Ash Wednesday water poured at roots before sunrise. Source gives no fixed physical morphology.
artistic_changes: Discreet adult humanlike woman, dark rustic dress, hair and face are artistic form choices; root pool evokes water offering without depicting rite. Rendered horizon shows sunrise glow rather than strictly pre-sunrise, a scene lighting choice.

goryo.depicted_variant: Human-shaped enshrined Japanese court spirit, inspired by Prince Sawara calamity account
visual_requirements: One human-shaped resentful court spirit
Heian court clothing and Kyoto shrine context
Calamity atmosphere without invented monstrous anatomy
goryo.aura: Solemn unsettling shrine apparition under storm clouds

basis_claims.quote: In a narrower sense, it refers to a noble or accomplished person who lost a political power struggle or died prematurely from an epidemic or other disease, becoming an onryō that brings pestilence or famine and is later enshrined as a kami in Shinto shrines.

statement.id: Dalam arti khusus, goryō adalah arwah tokoh yang wafat tragis, lalu dipercaya menyebabkan bencana dan dipuja sebagai kami.
statement.en: More narrowly, a goryō is the spirit of a person who died tragically, was blamed for calamity and later enshrined as a kami.

basis_claims.quote: Goryō Shinko (御霊信仰, Belief in goryō) refers to the belief that the onryō of people who have died unfortunate deaths cause hauntings and disasters, and the belief that they are enshrined as kami to appease them.

statement.id: Kepercayaan goryō mencakup upaya menenangkan roh pendendam dengan memujanya sebagai kami.
statement.en: Goryō belief includes appeasing resentful spirits by enshrining them as kami.

basis_claims.quote: After his death, a plague epidemic broke out in Kyoto, which people feared was caused by his spirit.

statement.id: Wabah di Kyoto setelah kematian Pangeran Sawara ditakuti sebagai ulah rohnya.
statement.en: A plague in Kyoto after Prince Sawara’s death was feared to be caused by his spirit.

basis_claims.quote: they were linked to calamities and thus feared.

statement.id: Ensiklopedia Shinto mencatat bahwa goryō ditakuti karena dikaitkan dengan malapetaka.
statement.en: The Encyclopedia of Shinto says goryō were feared because they were linked to calamity.

nonhuman_features: Tragically dead spirit placated through enshrinement, linked to calamity; no anatomical deformation claimed
goryo.historical_basis: Goryō are spirits of tragically dead people linked to calamity and later enshrined as kami. Prince Sawara is one documented instance; human appearance in period court dress is an illustrative choice rather than a source-prescribed anatomy.
artistic_changes: Exact human facial appearance, costume, landscape or architecture, spectral rendering, scale placement and illumination are artistic choices; no additional anatomical claim introduced.

nephilim.depicted_variant: One immensely strong HUMANLIKE GIANT in modest rough ancient clothing standing over tiny rocky hills and distant human-scale settlement. Choose Hebrew-Bible giant interpretation, no wings/horns/halo added from disputed angel-parent interpretation. One normal human head, two arms, two legs; powerful muscles and extraordinary size create awe and threat through perspective. Monumental low angle, clouds at shoulders, natural sunset behind storm clouds; no lightning powers, glowing magic or modern superhero designs.

visual_requirements.description: One immensely strong HUMANLIKE GIANT in modest rough ancient clothing standing over tiny rocky hills and distant human-scale settlement. Choose Hebrew-Bible giant interpretation, no wings/horns/halo added from disputed angel-parent interpretation. One normal human head, two arms, two legs; powerful muscles and extraordinary size create awe and threat through perspective. Monumental low angle, clouds at shoulders, natural sunset behind storm clouds; no lightning powers, glowing magic or modern superhero designs.
Extraordinary giant scale; basis: documented size/strength and biblical giants interpretation

basis_claims.quote: are enigmatic figures mentioned in several passages of the Hebrew Bible and later Jewish and Christian literature.

statement.id: Nephilim adalah tokoh misterius dalam Alkitab Ibrani dan sastra Yahudi serta Kristen berikutnya.
statement.en: Nephilim are enigmatic figures in the Hebrew Bible and later Jewish and Christian literature.

basis_claims.quote: They are traditionally associated with extraordinary size, strength, or status

statement.id: Nephilim secara tradisional dikaitkan dengan ukuran, kekuatan, atau kedudukan luar biasa.
statement.en: Nephilim are traditionally associated with extraordinary size, strength, or status.

basis_claims.quote: There were giants in the earth in those days;

statement.id: Kejadian 6:4 dalam terjemahan KJV menyebut raksasa berada di bumi pada masa itu.
statement.en: Genesis 6:4 in the KJV describes giants on the earth in those days.

artistic_changes: Low-angle framing, painterly materials and environmental color are artistic rendering.
Effects are limited to the cited domains, deeds, attributes or iconography; natural light and scale supply presence where no elemental ability is documented.

presentation_revision.rationale: Big names (major gods, archangels, demon princes, primordial monsters, famous literary beings) must look imposing and powerful: an epic, awe-inspiring or terrifying presence that matches their standing in the tradition.

qareen.depicted_variant: Human spiritual companion and matching double, distinct from Qarinah
visual_requirements: Human and matching spiritual double visibly distinct
Matching normal face and clothing
Intimate unsettling companion atmosphere

basis_claims.quote: is a spiritual double of a human, either part of the human themself or a complementary creature in a parallel realm.

statement.id: Qareen adalah kembaran spiritual manusia, bagian diri atau makhluk pendamping di alam sejajar.
statement.en: Qareen is a human’s spiritual double, understood as part of the person or a complementary creature in a parallel realm.

basis_claims.quote: they are more often associated with malevolent spirits tempting into sin.

statement.id: Qareen lebih sering dihubungkan dengan roh jahat yang menggoda ke dalam dosa.
statement.en: Qareen is more often associated with malevolent spirits tempting people into sin.

basis_claims.quote: The Qareen as an accompanying spirit should not be confused with the Qarinah, a female "childbed demon" in Middle Eastern traditions.

statement.id: Qareen sebagai roh pendamping dibedakan dari Qarinah, iblis perempuan yang berkaitan dengan persalinan.
statement.en: Qareen as an accompanying spirit is distinguished from Qarinah, a female childbed demon.

nonhuman_features: Spiritual companion/double matching its human's appearance and associated with temptation; no anatomical deformation claimed
qareen.historical_basis: Qareen is documented as a person's spiritual double or complementary companion. Double imagery is interpretive visualization of this identity, not a claim that Qur'anic verses prescribe visible anatomy; no Qarinah childbed demon imagery imported.
artistic_changes: Exact human facial appearance, costume, landscape or architecture, spectral rendering, scale placement and illumination are artistic choices; no additional anatomical claim introduced.

bergsra.depicted_variant: Female woman-in-white mountain-spirit manifestation from Sven Andersson 1691 account
visual_requirements: One woman in white inside Nordic mountain
Ore seams and inviting mountain entrance
Human appearance without forest-spirit tail or hollow back
bergsra.aura: Enigmatic invitation into an otherworldly ore-rich mountain

basis_claims.quote: The bergsrå could be either masculine or feminine. It lived in the mountain with a court of relatives and sometimes surrounded by trolls. It was a common phenomenon in the mythology about the bergsrå to trick people into their dwellings in the mountain and to become bergtagen

statement.id: Bergsrå bisa laki-laki atau perempuan, tinggal di gunung bersama istana kerabat dan kadang dikelilingi troll; ia lazim memperdaya orang masuk ke kediamannya di gunung sehingga mereka menjadi bergtagen ("diambil ke dalam gunung").
statement.en: The bergsrå could be male or female, living in the mountain with a court of relatives and sometimes trolls; it commonly tricked people into its mountain home so they became bergtagen ('taken into the mountain').

basis_claims.quote: Bergsrået, eller bergatrollet eller bergakungen, var i nordisk folktro ett övernaturligt väsen, som bor i berget och råder över dess malm. Bergsrået förvänder ofta synen på dem som råkat upptäcka malmfyndigheter, så att de senare inte kan hitta dem. I många berättelser omges bergsrået av sin familj och ett hov av troll.

statement.id: Bergsrået (bergatrollet, bergakungen) dalam kepercayaan rakyat Nordik (nordisk) adalah makhluk gaib yang tinggal di gunung dan menguasai bijihnya; ia sering mengacaukan penglihatan orang yang menemukan endapan bijih sehingga tak bisa menemukannya lagi, dan dalam banyak cerita dikelilingi keluarga dan istana troll.
statement.en: Bergsrået (bergatrollet, bergakungen) in Nordic (nordisk) folk belief is a supernatural being living in the mountain and ruling its ore; it often twists the sight of those who find ore deposits so they cannot find them again, and in many tales is surrounded by family and a court of trolls.

basis_claims.quote: Drängen hade förklarat att han en gång somnat i skogen vid ett berg då han letat efter en bortsprungen get och då tagits in i berget av en kvinna i vitt. Kvinnan hade gett honom mat och dryck och sedan haft samlag med honom.

statement.id: Buruh tani itu mengaku pernah tertidur di hutan dekat gunung saat mencari kambing yang lepas, lalu dibawa ke dalam gunung oleh perempuan berbaju putih yang memberinya makan dan minum, lalu bersetubuh dengannya.
statement.en: The farmhand said he had once fallen asleep in the forest by a mountain while seeking a stray goat and was taken into the mountain by a woman in white, who gave him food and drink and then lay with him.

nonhuman_features: Mountain sovereign who lures people inside and rules ore, appearing as woman in white; no anatomical deformation claimed
bergsra.historical_basis: Selects female Bergsrå manifestation recorded in Sven Andersson's 1691 account, a woman in white who takes a person inside a mountain. Ore sovereignty is documented; no Skogsrå hollow back, animal tail or modern troll anatomy is imported.
artistic_changes: Exact face, white robe folds/belt/brooch, cavern geometry, mineral appearance and golden illumination are artistic visualization of documented woman-in-white and mountain ore context.

acheri.depicted_variant: Kumaon Himalayan girl spirit with dusk descent and dangerous shadow
visual_requirements: One girl-shaped Himalayan spirit
Kumaon mountain ridge at dusk
Uncanny shadow without invented anatomy or visible victim
acheri.aura: Quiet mountain dusk with ominous long spirit shadow

basis_claims.quote: An Acheri is a spirit of a young girl in the folklore of the southern Himalayas, specifically regions around Kumaon.

statement.id: Acheri adalah roh gadis dalam cerita rakyat wilayah Kumaon di Himalaya selatan.
statement.en: An Acheri is a girl spirit in Kumaon folklore in the southern Himalayas.

basis_claims.quote: It is said that they dwell during the day in the mountains or hilltops, and at dusk they descend to hold revel. It is often unwise to visit the places where the revels, regardless of if the Acheri are present or not. They are also said to bring disease to children (and sometimes others) who come in contact with their shadow (Cháyá).

statement.id: Ia tinggal di gunung pada siang hari dan turun bersuka ria saat senja.
statement.en: She dwells in the mountains by day and descends to revel at dusk.

basis_claims.quote: They are also said to bring disease to children (and sometimes others) who come in contact with their shadow (Cháyá).

statement.id: Bayangannya dipercaya menularkan penyakit kepada anak-anak.
statement.en: Her shadow is believed to inflict disease on children.

basis_claims.quote:
Along the lower Himalaya the Acheri are ghosts of little 
children, who live on the tops of mountains and descend at 
night to hold their revels in more convenient places.

statement.id: Crooke mencatat keyakinan bahwa Acheri tinggal di puncak gunung dan turun pada malam hari untuk bersuka ria.
statement.en: Crooke records the belief that Acheris live on mountaintops and descend at night to revel.

nonhuman_features: Girl spirit of mountaintops descending at dusk, with disease-bearing shadow; no anatomical deformation claimed
acheri.historical_basis: Kumaon Acheri is a girl spirit living on mountain peaks and descending at night to revel, whose shadow is believed to cause illness. Retains girl-shaped human anatomy without invented horror traits; no inaccurate red-clothing protection shown.
artistic_changes: Specific faces, clothing, environment geometry, shadow or golden-animal rendering and lighting are artistic choices rather than additional historical claims.

additional_sources.author: William Crooke

gandalf-mythology.depicted_variant: Gandálfr as Eddic dvergr of the Völuspá dwarf tally, without Tolkien wizard attributes
visual_requirements: One compact human-shaped Norse dwarf
Old Norse dress rather than Tolkien wizard costume
No speculative individual attributes or anatomy

basis_claims.quote: is a Dvergr (Norse dwarf) in Norse mythology, appearing in the so-called 'Tally of the Dwarves' within the poem Völuspá from the Poetic Edda, as well as in the Prose Edda.

statement.id: Gandalf (Nordik Kuno: Gandálfr) adalah dvergr (kurcaci Nordik) dalam mitologi Nordik yang muncul dalam "Daftar Para Kurcaci" di puisi Völuspá dari Edda Puisi serta dalam Edda Prosa.
statement.en: Gandalf (Old Norse Gandálfr) is a dvergr (Norse dwarf) in Norse mythology appearing in the 'Tally of the Dwarves' in the Völuspá of the Poetic Edda and in the Prose Edda.

basis_claims.quote: En la mitología nórdica, Gandalf es un enano que aparece en el poema Völuspá de la Edda poética.

gandalf-mythology.historical_basis: Gandálfr is attested as a dvergr in Völuspá and Prose Edda, with little individual morphology specified. This restrained dwarf portrait avoids importing Tolkien's wizard persona or inventing distinctive monstrous attributes.

dainn-norse-dwarf.depicted_variant: Dáinn in dwarf co-creator role beside Freyja's golden boar Hildisvíni
visual_requirements: One compact human-shaped Norse dwarf
One golden boar Hildisvíni to identify crafting association
No unsupported elf ears or unrelated Tolkien dwarf styling

basis_claims.quote: "Dead") or Dain is a character in Norse mythology. Mostly the tales relate to him being a dwarf and in others as king of elves.

statement.id: Dáinn ("Yang Mati") atau Dain adalah tokoh mitologi Nordik; kebanyakan kisah menyebutnya kurcaci, sebagian raja para elf.
statement.en: Dáinn ('Dead') or Dain is a character of Norse mythology; most tales make him a dwarf, others a king of elves.

basis_claims.quote: In the Hyndluljóð (7) he is said to have made Freyja's boar Hildisvíni, along with another dwarf, his brother Nabbi. Dáinn is referred to as a dwarf in the dwarf-þula of the Völuspá (11) and in a stanza by Sigvatr Þórðarson. But in the Hávamál (153) he is said to be an elf who carved the runes:

statement.id: Dalam Hyndluljóð (7) ia disebut membuat babi Hildisvíni milik Freyja bersama kurcaci lain, saudaranya Nabbi; ia disebut kurcaci dalam daftar kurcaci Völuspá (11) dan dalam bait Sigvatr Þórðarson, tetapi dalam Hávamál ia elf yang mengukir rune.
statement.en: In the Hyndluljóð (7) he made Freyja's boar Hildisvíni with another dwarf, his brother Nabbi; he is a dwarf in the Völuspá's dwarf-þula (11) and in a stanza by Sigvatr Þórðarson, but in the Hávamál an elf who carved the runes.

basis_claims.quote: Dain, auch Dainn (altnordisch Dáinn „gestorben“), ist ein Zwerg der nordischen Mythologie, der den goldenen Eber Hildisvini der Göttin Freyja schuf. Im Gegensatz zu anderen Zwergen wird Dain vergleichsweise häufig in den alten Texten erwähnt.

statement.id: Dain atau Dainn (Nordik Kuno Dáinn, "yang mati") adalah kurcaci mitologi Nordik yang membuat babi hutan emas Hildisvini milik dewi Freyja; berbeda dari kurcaci lain, ia cukup sering disebut dalam teks lama.
statement.en: Dain or Dainn (Old Norse Dáinn, 'dead') is a dwarf of Norse mythology who made the goddess Freyja's golden boar Hildisvini; unlike other dwarfs he is mentioned fairly often in the old texts.

nonhuman_features: Norse dwarf co-creator of Freyja's golden boar; no anatomical deformation claimed
dainn-norse-dwarf.historical_basis: Selects Dáinn's dwarf role rather than the alternative elf-king identity. His participation in making Freyja's golden boar is source-supported; alone beside the boar does not claim he made it without Nabbi.
artistic_changes: Specific faces, clothing, environment geometry, shadow or golden-animal rendering and lighting are artistic choices rather than additional historical claims.

bran-the-blessed.depicted_variant: Living human-shaped Welsh giant king wading the Irish Sea toward Ireland
