statement.en: Firedrakes (fire-drake, fyrdraca) of English folklore: dragon-sightings from shooting stars and will-o'-the-wisps; fireballs in the sky; Shakespeare.

basis_claims.quote: A fiery meteor. ... Flying Dragons, or as Englishmen call them, fire-Drakes, be caused in this manor.
basis_claims.locator: Fire-drake, sense 2 (citation of W. Fulke, Meteors)

statement.id: Kamus yang sama mencantumkan arti fire-drake sebagai meteor berapi, dengan kutipan W. Fulke, Meteors, tentang naga terbang yang oleh orang Inggris disebut fire-drake.
statement.en: The same dictionary lists a sense of fire-drake as a fiery meteor, citing W. Fulke, Meteors, on flying dragons that Englishmen call fire-drakes.

galeru.depicted_variant: Galeru the rainbow serpent, revered life-saving sustainer of northeastern Kimberley

visual_requirements.description: ONE enormous limbless RAINBOW SERPENT, exactly ONE snake head/TWO natural snake eyes/ONE long continuous coiling body/ONE tail; natural snake jaw and scales with restrained red/yellow/green/blue rainbow bands. NO horns/arms/legs/wings/crown or film designs. Body fills frame, no additional serpents
Life-saving sustainer and fertility embodied as the living serpent itself; no invented weather/lightning/creation effects
northeastern Kimberley rocky ground, no sacred human motifs or invented rituals

galeru.aura: Life-saving sustainer and fertility embodied as the living serpent itself; no invented weather/lightning/creation effects [galeru-c07]

basis_claims.quote: Dans la mythologie des Aborigènes d'Australie, Galeru (ou Galaru) est un serpent arc-en-ciel

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Aborigin Australia, Galeru atau Galaru adalah seekor ular pelangi.
statement.en: In Australian Aboriginal mythology, Galeru or Galaru is a rainbow serpent.

basis_claims.quote: Galeru (or Galoru, Kaleru) by the Wandjina (Kimberley Region)

statement.id: Dalam daftar nama Ular Pelangi, Galeru (atau Galoru, Kaleru) dikaitkan dengan Wandjina di wilayah Kimberley.
statement.en: In the list of names for the Rainbow Serpent, Galeru (or Galoru, Kaleru) is attributed to the Wandjina of the Kimberley Region.

basis_claims.quote: According to Phyllis M. Kaberry, in northeastern Kimberley, the Rainbow Snake known as Galeru (Kaleru) is also a life saver and sustainer, the embodiment of fertility

statement.id: Menurut Berndt yang merujuk Kaberry, di Kimberley timur laut Ular Pelangi bernama Galeru (Kaleru) adalah penyelamat dan penopang hidup, perwujudan kesuburan.
statement.en: According to Berndt citing Kaberry, in northeastern Kimberley the Rainbow Snake known as Galeru (Kaleru) is a life saver and sustainer, the embodiment of fertility.

gazeka.depicted_variant: Papuan Devil-Pig Gazeka from Ogi’s reported sighting, not Graves’s fictional comic beast

visual_requirements.description: ONE strange pig/tapirlike quadruped, approximately3.5feet tall and5feet long, ONE head/TWO eyes/FOUR CLOVEN-FEET legs, LONG SNOUT and ONE long horse-like hairy tail. Very dark patterned hide. NO horns/tusks/extra limbs, no elephant trunk or cartoon Gazeka design
Mount Albert Edward Papua New Guinea, grazing ground amid shadowed mountain vegetation

gazeka.aura: No documented supernaturalpower; reported frightened witness c06, menace through strange proportions and close looming framing only [gazeka-c02, gazeka-c05]

basis_claims.quote: Gazeka, Gazeka de Monckton,  o más popularmente «cerdo diablo papú», es un críptido, un animal imaginario. Se dice que fue visto en Papúa Nueva Guinea a principios del siglo xx, y su aspecto sería parecido a un tapir o un perezoso gigante, con un hocico largo, parecido al rictus de un trompetista, descendiente de algún marsupial extinto perteneciente a la familia Palorchestidae.

statement.id: Laporan menggambarkan moncong panjang dan rupa menyerupai tapir atau kungkang besar.
statement.en: Reports describe a long snout and a tapir- or giant-sloth-like appearance.

basis_claims.quote: And in 1906, two such beasts were finally encountered, albeit in a wholly unplanned manner. ... During the spring of that year, explorer Captain Charles A.W. Monckton was leading a major expedition to PNG's Mount Albert Edward. ... while seeking Oina, Ogi came upon two extraordinary creatures grazing nearby.

statement.id: Pada 1906, selama ekspedisi Kapten Charles A.W. Monckton ke Gunung Albert Edward di PNG, prajurit bernama Ogi, yang terpisah dari rekannya Oina, menjumpai dua makhluk luar biasa yang sedang merumput.
statement.en: In 1906, during Captain Charles A.W. Monckton's expedition to Mount Albert Edward in PNG, a private named Ogi, separated from his companion Oina, came upon two extraordinary creatures grazing nearby.

basis_claims.quote: Although vaguely pig-like, each of these animals was approximately 3.5 ft tall, and 5 ft long, with a very dark, patterned hide, cloven feet, a long snout, and a horse-like (hairy?) tail.

statement.id: Meski samar-samar mirip babi, tiap hewan itu kira-kira setinggi 3,5 kaki dan sepanjang 5 kaki, berkulit sangat gelap bercorak, berkuku belah, berhidung panjang, dan berekor seperti kuda (berbulu?).
statement.en: Though vaguely pig-like, each animal was about 3.5 ft tall and 5 ft long, with a very dark patterned hide, cloven feet, a long snout, and a horse-like (hairy?) tail.

hiyang-athouba.depicted_variant: Hiyang Athouba as the transformed wife with rough hair, big eyes and enormous teeth

visual_requirements.description: ONE humanlike adult female undead being, ONE head/TWO enormous ROUND EYES/TWO arms/TWO legs, rough UNCOMBED HAIR and dishevelled fullyOPAQUE long clothes. Enormous TEETH visible in open mouth, no animalhead/horns/claws. Intact dry skin without wounds, body contorted but no exposed brokenbones or gore
In folktale pursues husband then throws stones when unable to touch liana; physical airborne stone and footdust only, no magical rays
outside her village house beside hanging liana, deep night

hiyang-athouba.aura: In folktale pursues husband then throws stones when unable to touch liana; physical airborne stone and footdust only, no magical rays [hiyang-athouba-c10]

basis_claims.quote: The transformed being is often said to appear in the likeness of the deceased person.

statement.id: Makhluk itu dikatakan menyerupai orang yang meninggal.
statement.en: The being is said to resemble the deceased.

basis_claims.quote: The woman became seriously ill and died. No one knew she was dead. Her dead body lied in the house. A cat jumped over body and she turned into Hiyanthau.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat ini, seorang perempuan jatuh sakit parah dan meninggal tanpa ada yang tahu; mayatnya tergeletak di rumah, seekor kucing melompati tubuhnya, dan ia berubah menjadi Hiyanthau.
statement.en: In this folktale a woman became seriously ill and died without anyone knowing; her dead body lay in the house, a cat jumped over the body, and she turned into Hiyanthau.

basis_claims.quote: 'It is open. Just come in,' replied Hiyanthau in the form of the wife. The husband pushed the door open and came in. The wife was in dishevelled cloths. Her hair was rough as it had not been combed for days.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat ini, ketika sang suami pulang dan memanggil, Hiyanthau menjawab dalam wujud istrinya dan menyuruhnya masuk; ia berpakaian kusut dan berambut kasar karena berhari-hari tidak disisir.
statement.en: In this folktale, when the husband returned and called, Hiyanthau replied in the form of the wife and told him to come in; she wore dishevelled clothes and her hair was rough as it had not been combed for days.

basis_claims.quote: Then he noticed the broken body of his wife and trembled in fear. The wife looked at him with big round eyes and showed him her enormous teeth.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat ini, sang suami melihat tubuh istrinya yang rusak dan gemetar ketakutan; sang istri menatapnya dengan mata bulat besar dan memperlihatkan giginya yang sangat besar.
statement.en: In this folktale the husband noticed his wife's broken body and trembled in fear; the wife looked at him with big round eyes and showed him her enormous teeth.

basis_claims.quote: So ran and climbed up a liana. Hiyanthau came after him. She could not the touch the liana so she threw stone at him. Then sat down and waited for him to come down.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat ini, sang suami memanjat sulur liana; Hiyanthau mengejarnya tetapi tidak dapat menyentuh liana itu sehingga ia melempar batu lalu duduk menunggu sang suami turun.
statement.en: In this folktale the husband climbed up a liana; Hiyanthau came after him but could not touch the liana, so she threw stones at him and then sat down and waited for him to come down.

hua-she.depicted_variant: Huà-shé from original text: human-faced dholebody, birdwings and snake-like gait

visual_requirements.description: ONE beast with HUMANFACE on ONE head/TWO eyes, DHOLElike russet canine body, FOUR normal canine legs, ONE tail and exactly TWO BIRD feather WINGS. No serpent tail/body replacement; snake-like sinuous gait achieved by bending quadruped body. Fully furred opaque body, no human torso or nudity
Sighting foretells a great flood; rising turbulent river and flooded nearby town express flood context, no beams or claimed command over water
Yang River joining Yi River beneath bare rocky Mount Yang with no grass/trees, tiny distant flood-threatened town

hua-she.aura: Sighting foretells a great flood; rising turbulent river and flooded nearby town express flood context, no beams or claimed command over water [hua-she-c01, hua-she-c06]

basis_claims.quote: 化蛇（かだ）は、中国に伝わる妖怪である。 これが見られた土地には洪水がもたらされる。

statement.id: Huà-shé adalah makhluk gaib Tiongkok yang dikaitkan dengan banjir.
statement.en: Huà-shé is a Chinese supernatural creature associated with floods.

basis_claims.quote: 『山海経』の「中山経」によると、陽水の伊水への合流点（現在の河南省嵩県と推測されている）の水中にすむ。人面で豺のような胴体と鳥の翼を持ち、蛇のように進み、叫ぶような声で啼くという。

statement.id: Shan Hai Jing memberinya wajah manusia, tubuh mirip jakal, dan sayap burung di pertemuan sungai.
statement.en: The Shan Hai Jing gives it a human face, a jackal-like body and bird wings in a river confluence.

basis_claims.quote: 人面で豺のような胴体と鳥の翼を持ち、蛇のように進み、叫ぶような声で啼くという。

statement.id: Ia bergerak seperti ular dan bersuara seperti teriakan.
statement.en: It moves like a snake and makes a cry like a shout.

basis_claims.quote: 又西三百里，曰陽山，多石，無草木。陽水出焉，而北流注于伊水。其中多化蛇

statement.id: Bab Zhongshan Jing (中山經) dalam Shanhaijing (山海經) menyebut Gunung Yang (陽山) yang berbatu dan tanpa tumbuhan; Sungai Yang (陽水) mengalir ke utara menuju Sungai Yi (伊水), dan di dalamnya banyak huà-shé (化蛇).
statement.en: The Zhongshan Jing (中山經) chapter of the Shanhaijing (山海經) mentions Mount Yang (陽山), rocky and bare of plants; the Yang River (陽水) flows north into the Yi River (伊水), and in it are many huà-shé (化蛇).

basis_claims.quote: 其中多化蛇，其狀如人面而豺身，鳥翼而蛇行，其音如叱呼，見則其邑大水。

statement.id: Teks aslinya: rupanya berwajah manusia dan bertubuh serigala hutan (豺身), bersayap burung dan bergerak seperti ular, suaranya seperti bentakan, dan bila ia terlihat, kotanya dilanda banjir besar (大水).
statement.en: The original text: it has a human face and a dhole-like body (豺身), bird wings and a snake-like gait, its voice is like a shout, and when it is seen its town suffers a great flood (大水).

huri-kamuy.depicted_variant: Huri Kamuy as enormous red bird casting the documented immense shadow

visual_requirements.description: ONE enormous BIRD with ONE head/TWO eyes/TWO huge feather WINGS/TWO birdlegs/ONE feather tail. Deep RED bird feathers, simple natural broad hooked birdbeak. No horns/teeth/extraheads or fantasyarmor. Tiny trees and coastline below establish vast scale
Its overhead shadow darkens the area for days in Kunnui place-name legend; physical huge birdshadow on land only, no fire/wind powers borrowed from ancestors
Kunnui landscape under birdshadow, tiny coastal trees below

huri-kamuy.aura: Its overhead shadow darkens the area for days in Kunnui place-name legend; physical huge birdshadow on land only, no fire/wind powers borrowed from ancestors [huri-kamuy-c08]

basis_claims.quote: A huri or furi is a giant bird in Ainu folklore.

statement.en: Ainu stories describe Huri as an enormous bird.
statement.id: Kisah Ainu menggambarkan Huri sebagai burung sangat besar.

basis_claims.quote: Its name suggests a red or reddish bird, and by some lore said to have a single wing measuring 28 kilometres (17 mi).

statement.id: Namanya mengarah pada burung merah, dan sebagian kisah menggambarkan sayap sangat besar.
statement.en: Its name suggests a red bird, and some accounts describe an enormous wing.

basis_claims.quote: そして、この国縫/訓縫（クンネ、「暗い、黒い」の意）の地名の由来になったためだとも伝わる。すなわち、フリカムイが上空にを飛んで影がさしかかり、被害地は何日も暗くなったためだ。

statement.id: Konon nama tempat Kunnui (国縫, dari kunne, "gelap, hitam") berasal dari huri kamuy (フリカムイ), karena saat ia terbang di atas, bayangannya membuat daerah itu gelap berhari-hari.
statement.en: The place name Kunnui (国縫, from kunne, "dark, black") is said to come from the huri kamuy (フリカムイ), because when it flew overhead its shadow left the area dark for days.

igopogo.depicted_variant: Igopogo in Eberhart’s gray sealbody/dogface/dorsalfins/fishtail variant

visual_requirements.description: ONE enormous GRAY SEALlike long animal, ONE head/TWO PROMINENT eyes, DOGlike FACE with GAPING natural mouth, long smooth gray body with restrained DORSAL FINS and ONE FISHlike TAIL. Natural small paired sealflippers only, no long landlegs, horns or dragonspikes. Length12–70feet documented, use roughly12meter body
Reported creature leaves wake and mudtrail; heavy physical wake and tail splashes only, no supernatural powers
cold Lake Simcoe Ontario, far dark shoreline and small reeds for scale

igopogo.aura: Reported creature leaves wake and mudtrail; heavy physical wake and tail splashes only, no supernatural powers [igopogo-c05]

basis_claims.quote: In Canadian folklore, the Igopogo is a legendary creature said to dwell in Lake Simcoe, Ontario.

statement.id: Igopogo adalah makhluk legendaris dalam cerita rakyat Kanada yang menghuni Danau Simcoe, Ontario.
statement.en: The Igopogo is a legendary creature in Canadian folklore dwelling in Lake Simcoe, Ontario.

basis_claims.quote: While tending sheep, Soules reportedly saw a long creature leaving a wake in the water and a trail in the mud.

statement.id: Saat menggembala domba, Soules dilaporkan melihat makhluk panjang yang meninggalkan riak di air dan jejak di lumpur.
statement.en: While tending sheep, Soules reportedly saw a long creature leaving a wake in the water and a trail in the mud.

basis_claims.quote: Descriptions of the Igopogo vary. Writer George M. Eberhart describes the Igopogo as a gray, seal-like animal stretching 12–70 feet (3.7–21.3 m) in length with a dog- or horse-like face, prominent eyes, a gaping mouth, dorsal fins, and a fishlike tail

statement.id: Gambaran Igopogo beragam. George M. Eberhart menggambarkannya sebagai hewan abu-abu mirip anjing laut sepanjang 12–70 kaki (3,7–21,3 m) dengan wajah seperti anjing atau kuda, mata menonjol, mulut menganga, sirip punggung, dan ekor seperti ikan.
statement.en: Descriptions of the Igopogo vary. George M. Eberhart describes it as a gray, seal-like animal 12–70 feet (3.7–21.3 m) long with a dog- or horse-like face, prominent eyes, a gaping mouth, dorsal fins, and a fishlike tail.

basis_claims.quote: Residents of Beaverton, on the eastern shore, call it Beaverton Bessie, while others refer to it as Kempenfelt Kelly, after Kempenfelt Bay, which has the lake's deepest water and claims the most sightings.

statement.id: Warga Beaverton di tepi timur menyebutnya Beaverton Bessie, sedangkan yang lain menyebutnya Kempenfelt Kelly, dari Kempenfelt Bay, bagian danau yang paling dalam dan paling banyak dilaporkan penampakannya.
statement.en: Residents of Beaverton on the eastern shore call it Beaverton Bessie, while others call it Kempenfelt Kelly, after Kempenfelt Bay, which has the lake's deepest water and the most sightings.

jarita.depicted_variant: the Sarngika mother bird sheltering four young during the Khandava fire

visual_requirements.description: ONE natural mother bird with one head/two eyes, one beak, TWO wings/TWO bird legs, ordinary brown feathers; EXACTLY FOUR smaller nestling birds beneath her wings, no humanoid bird hybrid, jewellery or giant anatomy.
No invented magic from Jarita. Forest fire surrounds the shelter but does not touch mother or young; documented protection moment, no injuries or death.
Khandava forest burning behind a tree-root shelter at ground level.

jarita.aura: SPREAD both wings into a fierce protective canopy over four young, chest thrust against incoming heat, open beak calling, gaze determined; wide wings fill most frame. Grounded in jarita-c01, jarita-c02, jarita-c12, jarita-c04, jarita-c10, jarita-c13.

basis_claims.quote: Jarita (Sanskrit: जरित, IAST Jaritā) was a certain female bird of the species called Sarngika, whose story is told in the Mahabharata.

statement.id: Jarita adalah burung betina Sarngika yang kisahnya terdapat dalam Mahabharata.
statement.en: Jarita is a female Sarngika bird whose story appears in the Mahabharata.

basis_claims.quote: The saint Mandapala, who returned from the shades because he had no son, assumed the form of a male bird, and by her had four sons.

statement.id: Mandapala mengambil bentuk burung jantan dan memiliki empat anak dengannya.
statement.en: Mandapala takes the form of a male bird and has four sons with her.

basis_claims.quote: In the conflagration of the Khandava Forest she showed great devotion to the protection of her children

statement.id: Ia berusaha melindungi anak-anaknya ketika Hutan Khandava terbakar.
statement.en: She strives to protect her young when the Khandava Forest burns.

basis_claims.quote: It was, therefore, O monarch, that he blazed not forth, while consuming the forest of Khandava, for the destruction of Mandapala's children.

statement.id: Menurut teks ini, karena itulah ia tidak berkobar untuk membinasakan anak-anak Mandapala ketika melahap hutan Khandava.
statement.en: In this text, for that reason he did not blaze forth to destroy Mandapala's children while consuming the forest of Khandava.

basis_claims.quote: I do not, even by reflection, see any way of escape for you. I shall even cover you with my wings and die with you.

statement.id: Dalam ratapannya Jarita mengatakan ia tidak melihat jalan keluar bagi anak-anaknya dan akan menutupi mereka dengan sayapnya serta mati bersama mereka.
statement.en: In her lament Jarita says she sees no way of escape for the infants and will cover them with her wings and die with them.

basis_claims.quote: Hearing what the infants said. Jarita replied, 'There is a hole here in the ground near to this tree, belonging to a mouse.

statement.id: Jarita mengusulkan agar anak-anaknya masuk ke lubang tikus di dekat pohon itu untuk menghindari api.
statement.en: Jarita proposes that the infants enter a mouse's hole in the ground near the tree to escape the fire.

jinmenju.depicted_variant: the mountain-valley tree bearing human-head-like smiling flowers

visual_requirements.description: ONE living gnarly tree, with several LARGE FLOWERS resembling human heads, face petals joined to flower calyces and stalks, not severed bloody heads. Human-faced FLOWERS ONLY, not fruit or talking bark face.
Flowers silently smile and drop petals; flowers laughing too much wither and fall. No laser, ghost energy or predatory power.
A dark mountain valley, rough rocks and tree roots behind the dominant branches.

jinmenju.aura: LEAN branches toward close viewer; the foremost human-headed flower fills foreground, silently smiling uncanny broad smile while neighboring laughing flowers SHED PETALS and one flower falls. Grounded in jinmenju-c02, jinmenju-c05, jinmenju-c06, jinmenju-c07.

basis_claims.quote: It is commonly depicted as a tree bearing flowers that resemble human heads.

statement.id: Ia umumnya digambarkan sebagai pohon yang berbunga menyerupai kepala manusia.
statement.en: It is commonly depicted as a tree bearing flowers that resemble human heads.

basis_claims.quote: The Konjaku Hyakki Shūi depicts it as a tree blooming with flowers that resemble human heads

statement.id: Konjaku Hyakki Shūi menggambarkannya sebagai pohon yang berbunga seperti kepala manusia.
statement.en: The Konjaku Hyakki Shūi depicts it as a tree blooming with flowers that resemble human heads.

basis_claims.quote: In mountain valleys, its flowers just like human heads, without a word, they merely just smile away, smile away until its petals fall just like that

statement.id: Teks penjelas dalam Konjaku Hyakki Shūi: di lembah pegunungan bunganya seperti kepala manusia, tanpa kata hanya tersenyum terus-menerus sampai kelopaknya gugur begitu saja.
statement.en: In the explanatory text, in mountain valleys its flowers are just like human heads, and without a word they merely smile on and on until their petals fall just like that.

basis_claims.quote: According to the Sancai Tuhui, Dashiguo is a land one thousand li southwest, with flowers like human heads, and upon asking it questions, its flowers would laugh, but it wouldn't understand human language. If they laughed too much, the flowers would wither and fall.

statement.id: Menurut Sancai Tuhui, Dashiguo adalah negeri sejauh seribu li ke barat daya dengan bunga seperti kepala manusia; bila pohonnya ditanyai, bunganya tertawa tetapi tidak memahami bahasa manusia, dan bila terlalu banyak tertawa bunganya layu dan jatuh.
statement.en: According to the Sancai Tuhui, Dashiguo is a land one thousand li to the southwest with flowers like human heads; if the tree is questioned its flowers laugh but do not understand human language, and if they laugh too much the flowers wither and fall.

kasha-folklore.depicted_variant: the large bipedal corpse-stealing monster cat

visual_requirements.description: ONE large BIPEDAL feline, human-sized or taller, one head/two natural cat eyes/two ears, TWO arms ending clawed feline paws and TWO hind legs, one long tail. No second tail or demon horns.

Documented hellish FLAMES accompany monster cat physically; flames lick rainy air around creature but no energy ribbons. Corpse theft represented by closed shrouded bundle, absolutely no visible body/wounds.
Night storm over plain Japanese funeral building and roof.

kasha-folklore.aura: LEAP down from roof toward the close viewer, clutching a completely closed opaque cloth-wrapped coffin-length bundle in both clawed forepaws, hindlegs extending behind. Feline face confrontational with natural open teeth. Grounded in kasha-folklore-c07, kasha-folklore-c09, kasha-folklore-c13, kasha-folklore-c10, kasha-folklore-c08.

basis_claims.quote: Kasha are a type of bake-neko, or monster cat. They are large, bipedal felines as large as or larger than a human. They are often accompanied by hellish flames or lightning.

statement.id: Kasha adalah sejenis bake-neko (kucing monster): kucing besar berkaki dua sebesar manusia atau lebih besar, yang sering disertai api neraka atau kilat.
statement.en: Kasha are a type of bake-neko, or monster cat: large bipedal felines as large as or larger than a human, often accompanied by hellish flames or lightning.

basis_claims.quote: They like to appear during rainy or stormy weather, and most often during the night.

statement.id: Kasha suka muncul saat hujan atau badai, dan paling sering pada malam hari.
statement.en: Kasha like to appear in rainy or stormy weather, and most often at night.

basis_claims.quote: Kasha, being bake-neko, often live among humans, disguised as ordinary house cats or strays. However, they reveal their true forms during funeral services, when they leap down from rooftops to snatch corpses out of their coffins.

statement.id: Kasha sering hidup di antara manusia dengan menyamar sebagai kucing rumah atau kucing liar biasa, lalu menampakkan wujud aslinya saat upacara pemakaman: melompat dari atap untuk merebut jenazah dari peti.
statement.en: Kasha often live among humans disguised as ordinary house cats or strays, and reveal their true forms at funerals, leaping down from rooftops to snatch corpses out of their coffins.

basis_claims.quote: Kasha are occasionally employed as messengers or servants of hell, in which case they are tasked with collecting the corpses of wicked humans spiriting them off to hell for punishment. Other times, they steal corpses for their own uses — either to animate as puppets or to eat.

statement.id: Kasha kadang dipekerjakan sebagai utusan atau pelayan neraka untuk mengumpulkan jenazah orang jahat dan membawanya ke neraka sebagai hukuman; pada kesempatan lain mereka mencuri jenazah untuk dijadikan boneka atau dimakan.
statement.en: Kasha are occasionally employed as messengers or servants of hell, collecting the corpses of wicked humans and carrying them off to hell for punishment; at other times they steal corpses for their own use, to animate as puppets or to eat.

basis_claims.quote: Kasha were once ordinary house cats. Like other animals, as they age in years and their tails grow longer, cats begin to develop magical powers. Some turn into bake-neko, more powerful cats turn into neko-mata, and beyond that some turn into kasha.

statement.id: Kasha dahulu kucing rumah biasa; seiring usia dan makin panjang ekornya, kucing mulai memiliki kekuatan gaib: sebagian menjadi bake-neko, kucing yang lebih kuat menjadi neko-mata, dan di atas itu sebagian menjadi kasha.
statement.en: Kasha were once ordinary house cats; as cats age and their tails lengthen they develop magical powers, some becoming bake-neko, more powerful ones neko-mata, and beyond that some becoming kasha.

khyah-legendary-creature.depicted_variant: the dark hairy apelike household Newar spirit

visual_requirements.description: ONE short FAT HAIRY APELIKE HUMANOID, one head/two eyes/two arms/two legs, black coarse hair covers body, plain opaque coarse waist cloth; no horns/wings or theatrical cowl/costume conflated with creature.
No documented magical effects; dark household spirit movement and hair anatomy convey awe, no predatory harms added.
Attic dark wooden rafters and stored plain sacks/crates.

khyah-legendary-creature.aura: SCRAMBLE out of attic darkness toward viewer, large knuckled hand gripping close wooden beam, squat body crouching forward and intent uncanny stare. Grounded in khyah-legendary-creature-c01, khyah-legendary-creature-c04, khyah-legendary-creature-c13, khyah-legendary-creature-c02.

basis_claims.quote: Khyāh (Newar: 𑐏𑑂𑐫𑐵𑑅; alternative spellings Khyā or Khyāk) is a mythical humanoid creature in Newari folklore. It is depicted as a fat, hairy and short ape-like creature.

statement.id: Khyah adalah makhluk humanoid dalam cerita rakyat Newar, digambarkan pendek, gemuk, berbulu, dan mirip kera.
statement.en: Khyah are humanoid creatures of Newar folklore, portrayed as short, fat, hairy and apelike.

basis_claims.quote: Khyahs appear in children's stories popular in Newar society. A friendly Khyah fills the home with goodness while bad ones bring trouble. A white Khyah is believed to bring good luck while a black one can create problems. Encountering a Khyah can make one ill. Khyahs are said to tickle their victims to death.

statement.id: Khyah yang bersahabat membawa kebaikan, sedangkan yang jahat membawa masalah.
statement.en: Friendly khyah bring goodness, while bad ones bring trouble.

basis_claims.quote: Household Khyahs usually dwell in the attic and dark storerooms. They are said to fear electric lighting.

statement.id: Khyah rumah tinggal di loteng dan ruang penyimpanan gelap.
statement.en: Household khyah dwell in attics and dark storerooms.

basis_claims.quote: Khyahs always dwell in the dark as they are afraid of the light. There are two types of Khyahs; white and black. The white ones are the good ones

statement.id: Menurut penulis ini, Khyah selalu tinggal di tempat gelap karena takut cahaya, dan ada dua jenis Khyah, putih dan hitam; yang putih adalah yang baik.
statement.en: According to this author, Khyahs always dwell in the dark as they are afraid of the light, and there are two types, white and black; the white ones are the good ones.

kichkandi.depicted_variant: the alluring woman ghost identified by backward feet

visual_requirements.description: ONE young ADULT woman ghost, one head/two eyes/two arms/two legs, PALE skin, very long BLACK hair, fully opaque RED bridal clothes. BOTH FEET unnaturally reversed: face/chest toward camera while both foot TOES point AWAY from viewer and HEELS face camera. Ankles visible below raised hems, no extra feet.
Deadly lure to solitary men; no visual drain beams or invented floating aura. Menace solely backward feet, beckoning and close encounter.
Night village path alongside a river and distant plain cremation-ground stones, no visible bones/remains.

kichkandi.aura: LURE viewer with one beckoning hand while stepping close from dark riverside, inclined face intense, trailing red cloth; reverse feet clearly displayed in foreground at low angle. Grounded in kichkandi-c03, kichkandi-c04, kichkandi-c07, kichkandi-c09, kichkandi-c05, kichkandi-c08, kichkandi-c10.

basis_claims.quote: they are supposed to have unusually long black hair, pale and bony complexion and dressed up in a red bridal dress.

statement.id: Ia dikatakan berambut panjang hitam, berkulit pucat, dan memakai pakaian pengantin merah.
statement.en: She is said to have long black hair, a pale complexion and red bridal clothing.

basis_claims.quote: It is said that they can be identified by looking at their feet, which face backward.

statement.id: Kakinya dikatakan menghadap ke belakang.
statement.en: Her feet are said to face backward.

basis_claims.quote: People usually describe them as alluring and young female, who lures a lonely male traveler and saps their life force. The victims are said to turn out drained of their life and skinny. According to other tales told by locals and cab drivers, these spirits are also known to hitchhike late at night.

statement.id: Ia memikat pelancong laki-laki sendirian dan menyerap daya hidupnya.
statement.en: She lures a solitary male traveller and drains his life force.

basis_claims.quote: the kichkini (also known as kichkinni, kichkanya, or kichkandi), a young, beautiful, female ghost. She was a woman who had died in “unnatural circumstances,” by suicide, during childbirth, or through murder.

statement.id: Menurut artikel jurnal ini, kichkini (juga disebut kichkinni, kichkanya, atau kichkandi) adalah hantu perempuan muda yang cantik, seorang perempuan yang meninggal dalam "keadaan tidak wajar": bunuh diri, saat melahirkan, atau dibunuh.
statement.en: According to this journal article, the kichkini (also called kichkinni, kichkanya or kichkandi) is a young, beautiful female ghost, a woman who had died in "unnatural circumstances": by suicide, during childbirth or through murder.

basis_claims.quote: She wanders alone at night, searching for men to seduce. She is alluring but deadly; any man with whom she came into contact would fall ill, or die.

statement.id: Ia berkeliaran sendirian pada malam hari mencari laki-laki untuk dirayu; ia memikat tetapi mematikan, dan laki-laki yang bersentuhan dengannya akan jatuh sakit atau mati.
statement.en: She wanders alone at night searching for men to seduce; she is alluring but deadly, and any man who came into contact with her would fall ill or die.

basis_claims.quote: Appearing as a real woman, her feet— unnaturally twisted backward—identify her as a supernatural being.

statement.id: Ia tampak seperti perempuan sungguhan, tetapi kakinya yang terpelintir ke belakang menandainya sebagai makhluk gaib.
statement.en: She appears as a real woman, but her feet, unnaturally twisted backward, identify her as a supernatural being.

basis_claims.quote: Laxmi informed me that kichkini would walk alone at night, particularly around small villages and alongside rivers and cremation grounds.

statement.id: Seorang informan penelitian menuturkan bahwa kichkini berjalan sendirian pada malam hari, terutama di sekitar desa kecil serta di tepi sungai dan tempat kremasi.
statement.en: A research informant said that kichkini walk alone at night, particularly around small villages and alongside rivers and cremation grounds.

kijimuna.depicted_variant: the mischievous red-haired Okinawan banyan spirit

visual_requirements.description: ONE small wood spirit, child-like about3-4years form, one head/two eyes/two arms/two legs, wild thick BRIGHT RED hair and red-tinted skin, fully opaque simple plain tunic/short trousers. No horns/fangs/claws invented. Respectful powerful tree-spirit identity, no demonic features.
Wronged kijimuna can magically TRAP PEOPLE inside hollow trees; depict an adult silhouette enclosed far inside a separate dark hollow, without injury or energy effects.
Okinawan gajumaru banyan tree at night.

kijimuna.aura: THRUST one hand from a banyan tree hollow toward viewer, wild hair flaring, intense uncanny gaze and body leaning sharply out; thick roots loom close around the spirit. Grounded in kijimuna-c02, kijimuna-c03, kijimuna-c04, kijimuna-c06, kijimuna-c10, kijimuna-c01, kijimuna-c05.

basis_claims.quote: are mythological creatures said to inhabit the island of Okinawa.

statement.id: Kijimuna adalah makhluk mitologi yang dikatakan mendiami pulau Okinawa.
statement.en: The kijimuna are mythological creatures said to inhabit the island of Okinawa.

basis_claims.quote: They are described as resembling around a three or four-year-old child with wild red hair.

statement.id: Mereka digambarkan menyerupai anak berusia sekitar tiga atau empat tahun dengan rambut merah liar.
statement.en: They are described as resembling a child of around three or four years old with wild red hair.

basis_claims.quote: The kijimuna are small wood spirits according to Okinawan mythology.

statement.id: Menurut mitologi Okinawa, kijimuna adalah roh kayu kecil.
statement.en: According to Okinawan mythology, the kijimuna are small wood spirits.

basis_claims.quote: The kijimuna are said to live in trees, but the most common one is the 'gajumaru' or banyan tree.

statement.id: Kijimuna dikatakan tinggal di pohon, dan yang paling umum adalah gajumaru atau beringin.
statement.en: The kijimuna are said to live in trees, the most common being the gajumaru or banyan tree.

basis_claims.quote: Habitat: banyan trees on the islands of Okinawa

statement.id: Habitat kijimunā disebut pohon beringin di pulau-pulau Okinawa.
statement.en: The kijimunā's habitat is given as banyan trees on the islands of Okinawa.

basis_claims.quote: Physically, kijimunā are about the same height as a child, with wild and thick bright red hair, and red tinted skin.

statement.id: Secara fisik kijimunā setinggi anak-anak, dengan rambut merah terang yang liar dan tebal serta kulit kemerahan.
statement.en: Physically, kijimunā are about as tall as a child, with wild, thick, bright red hair and red-tinted skin.

basis_claims.quote: Cutting down the banyan tree in which they live is a sure way to earn their wrath. Kijimunā thus wronged have been known to murder livestock, sabotage boats so they sink while their owners are far out at sea, or magically trap people in hollow trees from which they cannot escape.

statement.id: Menebang pohon beringin tempat mereka tinggal pasti membangkitkan kemarahan mereka; kijimunā yang disakiti dikenal membunuh ternak, merusak perahu agar tenggelam saat pemiliknya jauh di laut, atau menjebak orang di pohon berongga secara gaib.
statement.en: Cutting down the banyan tree in which they live surely earns their wrath; wronged kijimunā are known to kill livestock, sabotage boats so they sink while owners are far out at sea, or magically trap people in hollow trees.

kijo.depicted_variant: the blue-skinned horned female demon of secluded mountain roads

visual_requirements.description: ONE adult woman-shaped DEMON, one head/TWO YELLOW eyes, BLUE SKIN, TWO sharp horns, TWO arms/TWO legs, long natural CLAWS on five-finger hands, fully opaque ragged ancient robe.
Stronger than most humans and magical, but no sourced concrete visual spell selected: no beams/glow; danger from clawed lunging body only.
Secluded mountain road beside dark cave entrance.

kijo.aura: LUNGE from mountain cave toward viewer, thrust clawed hand beside camera, twisted face and fierce yellow-eyed glare; robe swings with the attack. Grounded in kijo-c01, kijo-c08, kijo-c10, kijo-c09, kijo-c11.

basis_claims.quote: A kijo (鬼女, lit. demon woman) is an oni woman from Japanese legends.

statement.id: Kijo adalah oni perempuan dalam legenda Jepang.
statement.en: Kijo is a female oni in Japanese legends.

basis_claims.quote: Kijo are female demons. They resemble human women in most ways, although they are hideously ugly to behold. Some have red or yellow eyes, blue skin, sharp horns, long claws, or other supernatural features.

statement.id: Kijo adalah iblis perempuan yang mirip perempuan manusia tetapi sangat buruk rupa; sebagian bermata merah atau kuning, berkulit biru, bertanduk tajam, atau berkuku panjang.
statement.en: Kijo are female demons that resemble human women but are hideously ugly; some have red or yellow eyes, blue skin, sharp horns, or long claws.

basis_claims.quote: Kijo refers chiefly to women who have been transformed from humans into horrible monsters—either out of intense jealousy, wicked crimes, or a terrible grudge that twists the soul into pure hatred. ... These transformed women retreat from common society into more secluded places where they continue to perpetrate their wicked deeds.

statement.id: Kijo terutama adalah perempuan yang berubah menjadi monster akibat cemburu hebat, kejahatan, atau dendam; mereka menyingkir dari masyarakat ke tempat terpencil dan terus melakukan perbuatan jahat.
statement.en: Kijo refers chiefly to women transformed into monsters out of intense jealousy, wicked crimes, or a terrible grudge; they retreat from society to secluded places where they continue their wicked deeds.

basis_claims.quote: Kijo are stronger than most humans, though their strength pales in comparison to oni. These demonesses excel in magic; they accumulate powerful spells over their long lives. Kijo are capable of bestowing hexes and curses, brewing poisons and potions, and weaving complex illusions.

statement.id: Kijo lebih kuat daripada kebanyakan manusia (tetapi kalah dari oni), ahli sihir, dan mampu mengutuk, meracik racun dan ramuan, serta merajut ilusi rumit.
statement.en: Kijo are stronger than most humans (though weaker than oni), excel in magic, and can bestow hexes and curses, brew poisons and potions, and weave complex illusions.

basis_claims.quote: They can be found living in remote mountain caves, abandoned houses, or along mountain roads where they receive a steady supply of victims.

statement.id: Kijo dapat ditemui tinggal di gua gunung terpencil, rumah terbengkalai, atau di jalan pegunungan tempat mereka mendapat korban.
statement.en: Kijo can be found living in remote mountain caves, abandoned houses, or along mountain roads where they receive a steady supply of victims.

kong-koi.depicted_variant: the one-legged monkey-like tube-mouthed jungle ghost

visual_requirements.description: ONE ugly MONKEY/LANGUR-like ghost, one head/TWO eyes/TWO arms, EXACTLY ONE leg and ONE foot centered below body. Fly-like tubular mouth/proboscis instead of ordinary monkey lips. Coarse natural dark fur, no wings, no second leg.
Toe-blood sucking lore represented by tube mouth only, no victim, blood or bites.
Dark Thai/Lao jungle at night with forest floor ferns.

kong-koi.aura: HOP directly toward viewer at jungle floor, single foot tucked under body and arms reaching in balance, tubular mouth extended toward camera as if shouting. Grounded in kong-koi-c01, kong-koi-c17, kong-koi-c02.

basis_claims.quote: is a Lao and Thai jungle ghost. Their appearance is not easily characterized, but often described as a phantom with one leg. They move by hopping with one leg and shout, "Koi, koi, koi". Some people believe it has a fly-like tube mouth. Others describe it as looking like monkey or langur. Most agree this ghost is ugly and cannot climb trees

statement.id: Kong koi atau Phi Kong Koi (ผีกองกอย) adalah hantu hutan Laos dan Thailand, sering digambarkan berkaki satu, melompat sambil berteriak koi; sebagian percaya mulutnya berupa tabung seperti lalat, sebagian menggambarkannya mirip monyet atau lutung; kebanyakan sepakat ia buruk rupa dan tak bisa memanjat pohon.
statement.en: Kong koi or Phi Kong Koi (ผีกองกอย) is a Lao and Thai jungle ghost, often one-legged, hopping and shouting koi; some say it has a fly-like tube mouth, others that it looks like a monkey or langur; most agree it is ugly and cannot climb trees.

basis_claims.quote: It is believed that the Phi Kong Koi will suck blood from the toes of the sleeping traveler in the jungle; Travelers should keep the feet together or cross their feet when sleeping to protect themselves.

statement.id: Phi Kong Koi dipercaya mengisap darah dari jari kaki pengembara yang tidur di hutan; pengembara sebaiknya merapatkan atau menyilangkan kaki saat tidur.
statement.en: Phi Kong Koi is believed to suck blood from sleeping travellers' toes; travellers should keep their feet together or crossed when sleeping.

basis_claims.quote: นทธี ศศิวิมล สรุป ตำนานภูตผีปีศาจไทยไว้ว่า “โป่งค่างหรือกองกอย” เป็นผีป่าชนิดหนึ่ง มีปากเป็นท่อเหมือนแมลงวัน เคลื่อนที่โดยการกระโดด หน้าตาคล้ายลิงหรือค่าง บ้างเรียกผีโป่ง หรือผีกองกอย เชื่อว่าโป่งค่างชอบดูดเลือดจากหัวแม่เท้าของคนที่นอนค้างแรมในป่า

statement.id: Sebuah artikel jurnal Thailand, mengutip ringkasan legenda hantu Thai oleh Nathi Sasiwimon, menyebut "pong kang atau kong koi" sebagai sejenis hantu hutan bermulut tabung seperti lalat, bergerak dengan melompat, berwajah mirip monyet atau lutung, kadang disebut phi pong atau phi kong koi, dan dipercaya suka mengisap darah dari ibu jari kaki orang yang bermalam di hutan.
statement.en: A Thai journal article, citing Nathi Sasiwimon's summary of Thai ghost legends, describes the "pong kang or kong koi" as a forest ghost with a fly-like tube mouth that moves by hopping and looks like a monkey or langur, sometimes called phi pong or phi kong koi, and is believed to like sucking blood from the big toes of people camping overnight in the forest.

kuafu.depicted_variant: the Chinese giant pursuing the setting sun

visual_requirements.description: ONE human-shaped GIANT with one head/two eyes/TWO arms/TWO legs, fully opaque plain ancient robe; carries ONE WOODEN STAFF/club in one hand. No snakes in this HaiwaiBeiJing race variant.
Pursues sun and drinks Yellow/Wei rivers; physically large river water streams from free cupped hand as he pauses mid-stride to drink. No controlling sun or magical river levitation.
Yellow and Wei river landscape during sun pursuit.

kuafu.aura: RUN westward toward enormous distant sunset while turning torso near viewer, wooden staff thrust forward, thirsty face determined; near foot splashes across river shallows. Grounded in kuafu-c01, kuafu-c05, kuafu-c09, kuafu-c03.

basis_claims.quote: Kuafu (Chinese: 夸父) is a giant in Chinese mythology who wished to capture the Sun.  He was a grandson of Houtu.

statement.id: Kuafu adalah raksasa mitologi Tiongkok yang ingin menangkap matahari.
statement.en: Kuafu is a giant in Chinese mythology who seeks to capture the sun.

basis_claims.quote: Kuafu is a giant. One day, Kuafu decided to chase and catch the Sun. He followed the Sun from the East to the West, draining the Yellow River and the Wei River (all rivers and lakes crossing his path) to quench his burning thirst. However, the big rivers were also unable to quench his thirst, and as he searched for more water, he eventually died of dehydration.

statement.id: Ia mengejar matahari dari timur ke barat dan meminum Sungai Kuning serta Sungai Wei.
statement.en: He pursues the sun east to west and drinks from the Yellow and Wei rivers.

basis_claims.quote: The wooden club he was carrying grew into a vast forest of peach trees called the Deng Forest (鄧林).

statement.id: Tongkat kayunya berubah menjadi hutan pohon persik.
statement.en: His wooden club becomes a forest of peach trees.

basis_claims.quote: 夸父與日逐走，入日。渴，欲得飲，飲於河、渭，河、渭不足，北飲大澤。未至，道渴而死。棄其杖，化為鄧林。

statement.id: Dalam Haiwai Bei Jing, Kuafu berlomba lari dengan matahari lalu haus; ia minum dari Sungai He dan Sungai Wei yang tidak cukup, hendak minum di rawa besar di utara, tetapi mati kehausan di tengah jalan, dan tongkat yang ia buang menjadi hutan Deng.
statement.en: In the Haiwai Bei Jing, Kuafu races the sun and grows thirsty; he drinks from the He and Wei rivers, which are not enough, heads north to drink at the great marsh, and dies of thirst on the way; the staff he discarded turns into the Deng forest.

kudan-yokai.depicted_variant: the human-headed bovine calf speaking its prophecy

visual_requirements.description: ONE BOVINE CALF BODY with FOUR natural calf LEGS and CLOVEN HOOVES, ONE calf tail, ONE entirely HUMAN HEAD with TWO human eyes, human nose/mouth; no bovine snout, no cow ears/horns, no human torso or arms. Human neck joins calf shoulders.
Speaks human prophecy of disaster or bounty; no visual soundwaves, scrolling predictions, runes or generated plagues.
Minimal rural Japan barn threshold, neutral editorial setting, not stuffed specimen/showman exhibit.

kudan-yokai.aura: STEP into dark foreground while speaking directly toward viewer, mouth open mid-prophecy and severe concentrated human gaze; near cloven hoof lifts while all four legs remain readable. Grounded in kudan-yokai-c01, kudan-yokai-c05, kudan-yokai-c06, kudan-yokai-c13, kudan-yokai-c07, kudan-yokai-c15, kudan-yokai-c17, kudan-yokai-c02, kudan-yokai-c10.

basis_claims.quote: The kudan (件; literally "matter"; or "human-faced bovine"). is a yōkai of a "prophecy beast" type, whose news or urban legend has been disseminated in Japan since the Edo Period.

statement.id: Kudan adalah yōkai peramal Jepang dengan ciri manusia dan sapi.
statement.en: Kudan is a Japanese prophetic yōkai with human and bovine features.

basis_claims.quote: The human-faced, bovine-bodied kudan that allegedly appeared in "Mount Kurahashi", Tango Province (in today's Kyoto Prefecture) in the year Tenpō 7 (1836) was reported in a contemporary kawaraban.

statement.id: Selebaran bergambar tahun 1836 melaporkan kemunculannya di Provinsi Tango.
statement.en: An 1836 illustrated handbill reported an alleged appearance in Tango Province.

basis_claims.quote: The kudan is generally depicted as having the head of a human and the body of a bovine.

statement.id: Kudan umumnya digambarkan berkepala manusia dan bertubuh sapi.
statement.en: The kudan is generally depicted with a human head and a bovine body.

basis_claims.quote: An early attestation of kudan occurs in the aforementioned Mikkyoku nichijō (『密局日乗』) dated to Bunsei 2 (1819), where a human language-speaking and human-headed calf declared it should be given the name "kudan".

statement.id: Catatan awal tentang kudan terdapat dalam diary Mikkyoku nichijō bertanggal Bunsei 2 (1819), tentang anak sapi berkepala manusia yang berbicara dan menyatakan namanya harus "kudan".
statement.en: An early attestation of the kudan is in the diary Mikkyoku nichijō dated Bunsei 2 (1819), about a human-headed, human-speaking calf that declared it should be named "kudan".

basis_claims.quote: The kudan is typical of the so-called prophesy beasts (予言獣, yongenjū) of Japanese folklore, which not only portend plague or bounty, but prescribe the method on how to avoid being stricken.

statement.id: Kudan tergolong "binatang peramal" (yogenjū) dalam cerita rakyat Jepang, yang tidak hanya meramalkan wabah atau panen melimpah tetapi juga memberi cara menghindari bencana.
statement.en: The kudan is typical of the so-called prophecy beasts (yogenjū) of Japanese folklore, which not only portend plague or bounty but prescribe how to avoid being stricken.

basis_claims.quote: After the shogunate ended and the Meiji era began, the kudan was still mentioned in writings and Lafcadio Hearn heard about travelling showmen displaying an alleged stuffed specimen of a kudan.

statement.id: Setelah zaman keshogunan berakhir dan era Meiji dimulai, kudan masih disebut dalam tulisan, dan Lafcadio Hearn mendengar tentang pemain keliling yang memamerkan spesimen kudan yang diawetkan.
statement.en: After the shogunate ended and the Meiji era began, the kudan was still mentioned in writings, and Lafcadio Hearn heard of travelling showmen displaying an alleged stuffed kudan.

basis_claims.quote: argues that the kudan and the ushi-onna ought to be distinguished, due to a number of differences: the kudan is a calf born from cattle, the ushi-onna is a daughter of human parents

statement.id: Seorang penulis berpendapat kudan dan ushi-onna perlu dibedakan: kudan adalah anak sapi yang lahir dari sapi, sedangkan ushi-onna adalah putri orang tua manusia.
statement.en: A writer argues that the kudan and the ushi-onna ought to be distinguished: the kudan is a calf born from cattle, whereas the ushi-onna is a daughter of human parents.

basis_claims.quote: 日本の妖怪。半人半牛の姿で、生まれて数日の間に災害や疫病の予言をし、言い終えると死んでしまうとされる。
basis_claims.locator: デジタル大辞泉プラス「件」

statement.id: Kamus menggambarkan kudan sebagai yōkai berwujud setengah manusia setengah sapi yang, dalam beberapa hari setelah lahir, meramalkan bencana dan wabah lalu dikatakan mati setelah selesai berbicara.
statement.en: The dictionary describes the kudan as a half-human, half-bovine yōkai that in the first few days after birth prophesies disasters and epidemics and is said to die once it has spoken.

basis_claims.quote: Kudan are able to speak human languages from the day they are born. Immediately upon being born, a kudan gives one or more prophecies.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, kudan dapat berbicara bahasa manusia sejak lahir dan segera memberikan satu atau lebih ramalan.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, kudan can speak human languages from the day they are born and give one or more prophecies immediately after birth.

kurangaituku.depicted_variant: the wing-armed Maori part-woman part-bird pursuer

visual_requirements.description: ONE part-woman part-bird adult supernatural being, ONE human-shaped head/TWO eyes; TWO arms bearing WINGS joined along arms rather than extra separate wings; TWO legs. Fully opaque plain feather cloak/body clothing. Long spear-like extended LIPS capable of spearing birds, not normal beak replacing humanhead.
Documented flight in pursuit; natural wind and feathers physically move, no aura/runes.
Forest outside her cave, dark entrance and distant tree silhouettes.

kurangaituku.aura: FLY after the escapee toward low viewer, winged arms spread wide and thrust forward, long predatory lips and intent eyes dominate; no youth or victims shown. Grounded in kurangaituku-c01, kurangaituku-c06, kurangaituku-c08, kurangaituku-c02, kurangaituku-c07.

basis_claims.quote: Kurangaituku is a part-woman part-bird supernatural being in Māori mythology as told by the iwi (tribes) of Te Arawa and Raukawa.

statement.id: Kurangaituku adalah makhluk gaib separuh wanita dan separuh burung dalam mitologi Māori yang diceritakan oleh suku Te Arawa dan Raukawa.
statement.en: Kurangaituku is a part-woman part-bird supernatural being in Māori mythology told by Te Arawa and Raukawa iwi.

basis_claims.quote: He runs away from her but is caught and taken to her cave, where he is imprisoned along with other pet birds and lizards.

statement.id: Hatupatu ditangkap dan dibawa ke gua Kurangaituku tempat ia dikurung bersama burung dan kadal peliharaan.
statement.en: Hatupatu was caught and taken to her cave, imprisoned with pet birds and lizards.

basis_claims.quote: One day while Kurangaituku is out hunting, Hatupatu uses her taiaha (traditional weapon) to destroy her pet lizards and birds and steals her treasured korowai (feather cloaks).

statement.id: Hatupatu memusnahkan kadal dan burung peliharaan serta mencuri jubah bulu korowai milik Kurangaituku.
statement.en: Hatupatu destroyed her pet lizards and birds and stole her treasured korowai feather cloaks.

basis_claims.quote: KURANGAITUKU (myth.), an Ogress who had wings on her arms, could spear birds with her lips, and lived on raw food.

statement.id: Kamus Tregear mencatat Kurangaituku sebagai ogress yang bersayap pada lengannya, dapat menombak burung dengan bibirnya, dan hidup dari makanan mentah.
statement.en: Tregear's dictionary lists Kurangaituku as an Ogress who had wings on her arms, could spear birds with her lips and lived on raw food.

basis_claims.quote: She found the youth, Hatupatu, and took him to her home. He disliked the uncooked food, and induced the fairy to go farther and farther away each day hunting, while he stayed at home, cooking for himself

statement.id: Ia menemukan pemuda Hatupatu dan membawanya ke rumahnya; Hatupatu tidak suka makanan mentah dan membujuk sang peri pergi makin jauh setiap hari untuk berburu sementara ia tinggal di rumah memasak untuk dirinya sendiri.
statement.en: She found the youth Hatupatu and took him to her home; he disliked the uncooked food and induced the fairy to go farther and farther away each day hunting while he stayed at home cooking for himself.

basis_claims.quote: A bird went and told Kurangaituku, who flew after her truant

statement.id: Seekor burung pergi memberi tahu Kurangaituku, yang lalu terbang mengejar si pelarian.
statement.en: A bird went and told Kurangaituku, who flew after her truant.

obayifo.depicted_variant: Obayifo travelling in female human bodily form with source-specific phosphorescent underarm light

visual_requirements.description: ONE adult humanlike Ashanti witch-being in ordinary female bodily form; ONE head/TWO shifty sidelong eyes/TWO arms/TWO legs and FIVE natural fingers per hand. Fully OPAQUE worn long dress and opaque upper sleeves, no exposed torso or intimate areas. No horns, fangs or invented animal anatomy

Documented phosphorescence originates specifically beneath BOTH ARMPITS, small concentrated pale lights illuminate sleeveundersides and nearby ground; a faint light beneath opaque lower garment suggests the documented rear source without exposing anatomy. NO whole-body aura
Ashanti rural path at night, rough earth and distant dark houses

obayifo.aura: Documented phosphorescence originates specifically beneath BOTH ARMPITS, small concentrated pale lights illuminate sleeveundersides and nearby ground; a faint light beneath opaque lower garment suggests the documented rear source without exposing anatomy. NO whole-body aura [obayifo-c03, obayifo-c12]

basis_claims.quote: An obayifo is a vampire/witch-like mythological creature from West Africa coming from the folklore of the Ashanti.

statement.id: Obayifo adalah makhluk mitologis mirip vampir/penyihir (vampire/witch-like) dari Afrika Barat yang berasal dari cerita rakyat Ashanti.
statement.en: An obayifo is a vampire/witch-like mythological creature from West Africa, from the folklore of the Ashanti.

basis_claims.quote: In Ashanti folklore, obayifo are very common and may inhabit the bodies of any man or woman. They are described as having shifty eyes and being obsessed with food.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Ashanti, obayifo sangat umum dan dapat menghuni tubuh laki-laki atau perempuan mana pun; mereka digambarkan bermata jelalatan (shifty eyes) dan terobsesi pada makanan.
statement.en: In Ashanti folklore obayifo are very common and may inhabit the bodies of any man or woman; they are described as having shifty eyes and being obsessed with food.

basis_claims.quote: When travelling at night they are said to emit a phosphorescent light from their armpits and anus.

statement.id: Saat bepergian pada malam hari, mereka konon memancarkan cahaya fosforesen (phosphorescent light) dari ketiak dan anus.
statement.en: When travelling at night they are said to emit a phosphorescent light from their armpits and anus.

basis_claims.quote: People, typically women, who practiced bayi turned into the obayifo.

statement.id: Orang yang mempraktikkan bayi, biasanya perempuan (typically women), berubah menjadi obayifo.
statement.en: People, typically women, who practiced bayi turned into the obayifo.

basis_claims.quote: Although obayifo is used to describe both the men and women who practiced bayi and turned into the monster

statement.id: Istilah obayifo dipakai untuk laki-laki maupun perempuan yang mempraktikkan bayi dan berubah menjadi monster (turned into the monster).
statement.en: Obayifo describes both men and women who practiced bayi and turned into the monster.

basis_claims.quote: Při cestování v noci mají vydávat fosforeskující světlo vycházející z jejich podpaží a řitního otvoru.

statement.id: Saat bepergian pada malam hari (v noci), mereka konon memancarkan cahaya fosforesen (fosforeskující světlo) dari ketiak dan dubur.
statement.en: When travelling at night (v noci) they are said to give off a phosphorescent light (fosforeskující světlo) from their armpits and anus.

oci-koci.depicted_variant: Ochokochi in chest stone-axe protuberance variant, hairy human demon

visual_requirements.description: ONE human-shaped male demon, ONE head/TWO eyes/TWO arms/TWO legs, long sharp hand CLAWS; body covered in jet-BLACK HAIR except chest center carrying ONE outward-pointing BONE/STONE AXE-shaped PROTUBERANCE. No goathead/horns/hooves; opaque rough loinwrap under thick bodyfur
He attacks passersby and kills by embrace; grounddust scatters at bodily footcontact only, no resurrectionbeam or victimgore
shadowed Georgian/Megrel mountain forest trail, no victims

oci-koci.aura: He attacks passersby and kills by embrace; grounddust scatters at bodily footcontact only, no resurrectionbeam or victimgore [oci-koci-c07]

basis_claims.quote: Oçokoçi veya Oçi Koçi (Gürcüce: ოჩოკოჩი), Gürcü-Megrel-Laz mitolojisinde dağda yaşayan bir kişilik.

statement.id: Oçokoçi atau Oçi Koçi (ოჩოკოჩი) adalah sosok yang tinggal di gunung (dağda yaşayan) dalam mitologi Gürcü-Megrel-Laz.
statement.en: Oçokoçi or Oçi Koçi (ოჩოკოჩი) is a mountain-dwelling (dağda yaşayan) figure in Gürcü-Megrel-Laz mythology.

basis_claims.quote: Megrel halk inanışında kışın köylere dadanan ve erkek çocuklarla ahırdaki inek yavrularını yiyen vücudu kıllarla kaplı insan görünümünde bir iblistir.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Megrel, ia iblis (iblis) berwujud manusia bertubuh penuh bulu yang mendatangi desa pada musim dingin dan memakan anak laki-laki serta anak sapi di kandang.
statement.en: In Megrel folk belief it is a demon (iblis) of human appearance with a hair-covered body that haunts villages in winter and eats boys and calves in the barn.

basis_claims.quote: Oçokoçi, konuşmasını bilmez, ama çıkardığı ses insanlar için dayanılmaz bir sestir. Oçokoçi'nin bütün vücudu simsiyah tüylerle kaplıdır. Uzun ve keskin pençeleri vardır.

statement.id: Oçokoçi tidak bisa berbicara, tetapi suaranya tak tertahankan bagi manusia; seluruh tubuhnya berbulu hitam pekat (simsiyah) dan cakarnya panjang serta tajam.
statement.en: Oçokoçi cannot speak, but the sound it makes is unbearable to people; its whole body is covered in jet-black (simsiyah) hair and it has long sharp claws.

basis_claims.quote: Instead of hair on his breast, he has a protuberance in the form of a pointed bone or a stone-axe. He attacks passers by, whom he kills by embracing them.

statement.id: Alih-alih bulu di dadanya, ia memiliki tonjolan berbentuk tulang runcing atau kapak batu (stone-axe); ia menyerang orang lewat dan membunuh mereka dengan memeluk (embracing).
statement.en: Instead of hair on his breast he has a protuberance shaped like a pointed bone or a stone-axe; he attacks passers-by and kills them by embracing them.

basis_claims.quote: He is infatuated by the beauty of the Queen of the Forest, Tkashi-Mapa, after whom he chases. However, his attempts to catch her are often thwarted by the hunters who visit her forest.

statement.id: Ia tergila-gila pada kecantikan Ratu Hutan (Queen of the Forest), Tkashi-Mapa, dan mengejarnya, tetapi usahanya sering digagalkan para pemburu (hunters) yang datang ke hutannya.
statement.en: He is infatuated with the beauty of the Queen of the Forest, Tkashi-Mapa, and chases her, but his attempts are often thwarted by hunters who visit her forest.

okuri-inu.depicted_variant: Okuri-inu in wolf form at the instant of pouncing

visual_requirements.description: ONE dark natural WOLF-like quadruped, ONE head/TWO eyes/FOUR legs/ONE tail, natural wolf teeth/paws, no horns/extraeyes. Fully furred, not a breed portrait

dark mountain pass and forested road in Japan at night

okuri-inu.aura: Supernaturally fast pounce after traveler falls; physical soil/debris kick and tense motion only, no neon speedtrail or victim injury [okuri-inu-c04, okuri-inu-c05, okuri-inu-c06]

basis_claims.quote: The Okuri-inu (送り犬) (literally, 'escorting dog') is a kind of yōkai.

statement.id: Okuri-inu adalah yōkai mirip anjing dalam cerita rakyat Jepang.
statement.en: Okuri-inu is a doglike yōkai in Japanese folklore.

basis_claims.quote: There are stories of the okuri-inu from the Tōhoku region to Kyushu, but depending on the area it can be a wolf not a dog, and there are numerous differences in its behaviour.

statement.id: Bentuk daerahnya mencakup anjing maupun serigala.
statement.en: Its regional forms include both dogs and wolves.

basis_claims.quote: The okuri-inu closely follows people who are walking along mountain paths at nighttime.

statement.id: Ia mengikuti pejalan di jalan pegunungan pada malam hari.
statement.en: It follows people walking mountain paths at night.

basis_claims.quote: If by chance the person falls over they will be immediately eaten up, but if they pretend to be having a short rest they will not be attacked.

statement.id: Satu cerita menyebut ia menyerang ketika pejalan terjatuh.
statement.en: One story says it attacks if the traveler falls.

basis_claims.quote: The okuri inu follows lone travelers late on the road at night. It stalks them, keeping a safe distance, but following footstep for footstep, as long as they keep walking. If the traveler should trip or stumble, the okuri inu will pounce on them and rip them to shreds.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, okuri inu mengikuti pelancong yang sendirian larut malam di jalan, menjaga jarak aman, mengikuti langkah demi langkah selama mereka terus berjalan; bila pelancong tersandung, ia menerkam dan mencabik-cabiknya.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, the okuri inu follows lone travelers late at night, stalking them at a safe distance and following footstep for footstep as long as they keep walking; if the traveler trips or stumbles it pounces and rips them to shreds.

basis_claims.quote: The okuri inu is somewhat of a blessing and a curse. On the one hand, if one should trip and fall, it will pounce with supernatural speed and gobble him or her up. On the other hand, they are so ferocious that while they are following someone, no other dangerous yokai or wild animals will come close.

statement.id: Yokai.com menyebut okuri inu sebagai berkah sekaligus kutukan: ia menerkam dengan kecepatan supernatural bila orang jatuh, tetapi karena sangat garang, selama ia mengikuti seseorang tidak ada yōkai atau binatang buas berbahaya lain yang mendekat.
statement.en: Yokai.com calls the okuri inu somewhat of a blessing and a curse: it pounces with supernatural speed if one falls, but so ferocious that while it follows someone no other dangerous yokai or wild animals come close.

basis_claims.quote: Okuri inu 送り犬 おくりいぬ Translation: sending-off dog Alternate names: okuri ōkami (sending-off wolf) Habitat: dark mountain passes, forested roads

statement.id: Yokai.com menulis 送り犬 (おくりいぬ) dengan terjemahan "anjing pengantar", nama lain okuri ōkami ("serigala pengantar"), dan habitat jalur gunung gelap serta jalan berhutan.
statement.en: Yokai.com gives 送り犬 (おくりいぬ) with the translation "sending-off dog", the alternate name okuri ōkami ("sending-off wolf"), and dark mountain passes and forested roads as habitat.

olanoiko-zakurra.depicted_variant: Olanoiko zakurra as the large grey caveguardian dog

visual_requirements.description: ONE BIG GREY DOG spirit, ONE natural doghead/TWO eyes/FOUR legs/ONE tail, grey rough coat and normal canine teeth. No horns/extraeyes/fire
Attacks approaching cave visitors; physical cavegrit and dust from pawimpact only, no undocumented elemental power
entrance of Olanoi cave at Beizama, Basque rocky darkness

olanoiko-zakurra.aura: Attacks approaching cave visitors; physical cavegrit and dust from pawimpact only, no undocumented elemental power [olanoiko-zakurra-c03]

basis_claims.quote: Olanoiko zakurra ('el gos d'Olanoi', del basc Olanoiko 'd'Olanoi' i zakurra 'el gos') és un geni de la mitologia basca que adopta l'aparença d'un gran gos gris i que és el guardià de la cova Olanoi de Beizama.

statement.id: Olanoiko zakurra ("anjing Olanoi") adalah roh mitologi Basque berwujud anjing abu-abu besar yang menjaga gua Olanoi di Beizama.
statement.en: Olanoiko zakurra ('the dog of Olanoi') is a spirit of Basque mythology in the form of a big grey dog, guardian of the Olanoi cave at Beizama.

basis_claims.quote: Beizamako Olanoi kobazuloko zaindaria da txakur irelu handi hau, eta bertara hurbiltzen diren lagunei eraso egiten die.

statement.id: Roh anjing besar ini penjaga gua Olanoi di Beizama dan menyerang orang yang mendekat.
statement.en: This great dog spirit guards the Olanoi cave at Beizama and attacks those who come near.

basis_claims.quote: Zuzidun Txakurra, Olanoiko zakurra et Mirokutana sont des génies de la mythologie basque qui ont l'aspect d'un chien.

statement.id: Zuzidun Txakurra, Olanoiko zakurra, dan Mirokutana adalah roh mitologi Basque yang berwujud anjing.
statement.en: Zuzidun Txakurra, Olanoiko zakurra and Mirokutana are spirits of Basque mythology that look like dogs.

basis_claims.quote: Olanoiko zakurra Euskal Herriko mitologiaren irelu bat da, beste asko bezala leizezuloei lotuta.

statement.id: Olanoiko zakurra adalah salah satu irelu (roh) dalam mitologi Basque yang, seperti banyak lainnya, terkait dengan gua.
statement.en: Olanoiko zakurra is one of the irelu (spirits) of Basque mythology and, like many others, is linked to caves.

olokun.depicted_variant: Olokun in documented male half-human half-fish chained oceanbottom variant

olokun.aura: Sea in terrifying aspect and flood tradition: huge physical ocean surge moves around chained underwaterdivinity, sediment and bubbles stirred by tail, NO aura/neon/runes [olokun-c19, olokun-c20]

basis_claims.quote: Depending on the tradition, Olokun may be described as female, male or androgynous.

statement.id: Bergantung pada tradisinya, Olokun dapat digambarkan sebagai perempuan, laki-laki, atau androgini.
statement.en: Depending on the tradition, Olokun may be described as female, male or androgynous.

basis_claims.quote: In Santería, Olokun is associated with the depths of the ocean and its hidden riches. ... Some devotees see Olokun and Yemayá as aspects of the same orisha, while others regard them as spouses.

statement.id: Dalam Santería, Olokun dikaitkan dengan kedalaman samudra dan kekayaannya yang tersembunyi; sebagian pemuja memandang Olokun dan Yemayá sebagai aspek orisha yang sama, sedangkan yang lain menganggap mereka suami-istri.
statement.en: In Santería, Olokun is associated with the depths of the ocean and its hidden riches; some devotees see Olokun and Yemayá as aspects of the same orisha, others as spouses.

basis_claims.quote: Encarna al mar en su aspecto aterrador y extraño al hombre, y todas las riquezas del océano son suyas.

statement.id: Artikel ketiga menyebut Olokun mewujudkan laut dalam aspeknya yang menakutkan (aterrador) dan asing bagi manusia, dan semua kekayaan samudra (riquezas del océano) adalah miliknya.
statement.en: The third article says Olokun embodies the sea in its terrifying (aterrador) aspect, alien to humans, and all the riches of the ocean (riquezas del océano) are his.

basis_claims.quote: Obbatalá lo encadenó al fondo del océano, cuando intentó matar a la humanidad con el diluvio.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ketiga, Obbatalá merantainya (encadenó) di dasar samudra ketika ia mencoba membinasakan manusia dengan air bah (diluvio).
statement.en: According to the third article, Obbatalá chained (encadenó) him to the bottom of the ocean when he tried to kill humanity with the flood (diluvio).

basis_claims.quote: En ocasiones se le representa mitad hombre, mitad pez, aunque esto es indefinido

statement.id: Kadang ia digambarkan setengah manusia, setengah ikan (mitad hombre, mitad pez), walaupun hal ini tidak tetap.
statement.en: He is sometimes represented as half man, half fish (mitad hombre, mitad pez), though this is not fixed.

Wallclimbing and slippery oily escape: physical oily smears at contact and reflected black coating, no magical rays or victimscene

orang-minyak.aura: Wallclimbing and slippery oily escape: physical oily smears at contact and reflected black coating, no magical rays or victimscene [orang-minyak-c02]

basis_claims.quote: In Malay ghost beliefs, the Orang Minyak ("oily man" in Malay) is a supernatural creature coated with shiny black grease who abducts young women by night. The legend of the figure is first mentioned in a report from the Singaporean newspaper Berita Harian dated 12 October 1957.

statement.id: Dalam kepercayaan hantu Melayu, Orang Minyak ('orang berminyak') adalah makhluk gaib berlumur minyak hitam mengilap yang menculik perempuan muda pada malam hari; legendanya pertama disebut dalam laporan surat kabar Singapura Berita Harian, 12 Oktober 1957.
statement.en: In Malay ghost belief, the Orang Minyak ('oily man') is a supernatural being coated in shiny black grease who abducts young women at night; the legend is first mentioned in a Berita Harian (Singapore) report of 12 October 1957.

basis_claims.quote: Supposedly, the creature is able to climb walls and grab victims while evading capture due to its slippery coating. The coating was first described as consisting of hair oil, before later stories evolved into it being covered in coconut oil and soot; the genre movies have it covered in crude oil

statement.id: Makhluk ini konon dapat memanjat dinding dan menangkap korban sambil lolos berkat lapisan licinnya, yang mula-mula disebut minyak rambut, lalu minyak kelapa dan jelaga; film menggambarkannya berlumur minyak mentah.
statement.en: It supposedly climbs walls and grabs victims while escaping thanks to its slippery coating, first described as hair oil, later coconut oil and soot; films show it in crude oil.

basis_claims.quote: According to some folklorists, the Orang Minyak has been alternately described as appearing naked, or wearing "a black pair of swimming trunks".

statement.id: Menurut sebagian ahli folklor, Orang Minyak kadang digambarkan telanjang, kadang mengenakan "celana renang hitam".
statement.en: According to some folklorists, the Orang Minyak has been alternately described as appearing naked or wearing "a black pair of swimming trunks".

otora-kitsune.depicted_variant: Otora kitsune as the shrine fox with left-eye and left-leg healed injuries

visual_requirements.description: ONE natural FOX spirit, ONE head/TWO eyes/FOUR legs/ONE bushy tail; LEFT EYE clouded and narrowed from old healed injury, LEFT HINDLEG held stiff and cautiously raised from old healed injury. No fresh wounds/blood, no nine tails or extraeyes
Inari shrine associated with Nagashino Castle in Aichi, weathered stone steps and plain shrinewood without written signs

otora-kitsune.aura: Possession not externally visualized; menace/awe through named injured fox itself and tense approach, no ghostfaces/neonflames [otora-kitsune-c05, otora-kitsune-c09]

basis_claims.quote: おとら狐が人に憑くのは、本来長篠城の稲荷社の使いであったおとら狐が、長篠の合戦後に社を放置されたことを恨んでいるためといい、後にそれを鎮めるために長篠城の城藪稲荷におとら狐が祀られたと伝えられる。

statement.id: Otora kitsune disebut merasuki orang karena rubah itu, yang semula utusan kuil Inari di Benteng Nagashino, mendendam atas kuil yang ditelantarkan setelah Pertempuran Nagashino; belakangan ia dipuja di Jōyabu Inari di Benteng Nagashino untuk menenangkannya.
statement.en: The Otora kitsune is said to possess people because the fox, originally the messenger of the Inari shrine at Nagashino Castle, resents the shrine being neglected after the Battle of Nagashino; it was later enshrined at Jōyabu Inari at Nagashino Castle to pacify it.

basis_claims.quote: おとら狐（おとらぎつね）とは、愛知県に伝わる狐の妖怪。 ... おとら狐は人間に取り憑き、様々な悪戯する妖怪で、取り憑かれた人間は常時では考えられない言動を行う。

statement.id: Otora kitsune (おとら狐) adalah yōkai rubah yang diwariskan di Prefektur Aichi; ia merasuki manusia dan melakukan berbagai keusilan, sehingga orang yang dirasuki berbicara dan bertindak tidak seperti biasanya.
statement.en: The Otora kitsune (おとら狐) is a fox yōkai handed down in Aichi Prefecture; it possesses people and plays various pranks, so that a possessed person speaks and acts unlike their usual self.

basis_claims.quote: 後にそれを鎮めるために長篠城の城藪稲荷におとら狐が祀られたと伝えられる。後に社は、愛知県新城市の大通寺に移されている。

statement.id: Dikatakan bahwa kemudian, untuk menenangkannya, Otora kitsune dipuja di Jōyabu Inari di Benteng Nagashino; kuil itu belakangan dipindahkan ke Daitsūji di Kota Shinshiro, Prefektur Aichi.
statement.en: It is said that it was later enshrined at Jōyabu Inari at Nagashino Castle to pacify it; the shrine was afterwards moved to Daitsūji in Shinshiro City, Aichi Prefecture.

basis_claims.quote: おとら狐は長篠の合戦のとき、流弾で左の目を傷つけ、犀川で昼寝をしているとき、狙撃されて左の足を傷つけたので、取り憑かれた者は左眼から目脂を出し、左足が痛むという。

statement.id: Basis data Kaii-Yōkai Densho Nichibunken (International Research Center for Japanese Studies) meringkas catatan 1916 bahwa pada Pertempuran Nagashino mata kiri Otora kitsune terluka oleh peluru nyasar, dan ketika ia tidur siang di Sungai Sai ia ditembak hingga kaki kirinya terluka; karena itu orang yang dirasuki mengeluarkan kotoran mata dari mata kiri dan kaki kirinya sakit.
statement.en: The Kaii-Yōkai Densho Database of Nichibunken (International Research Center for Japanese Studies) summarises a 1916 record that at the Battle of Nagashino the Otora kitsune hurt its left eye with a stray bullet, and while napping at the Sai River it was shot and hurt its left leg; hence those possessed discharge from the left eye and have pain in the left leg.

ouni.depicted_variant: Ouni as the friendly long-black-haired hag spinning enormous hemp bundles

inside rural mountain hut late at night, rough timber and simple fiberwork table

ouni.aura: Friendly toward kind hosts and spins enormous bundles in one night; physical taut fiberstrands and growing pile of thread move through hands, no magical aura [ouni-c06, ouni-c07, ouni-c12]

statement.id: Ilustrasinya memberi sosok itu rambut panjang dan wajah mirip perempuan iblis.
statement.en: The illustration gives it long hair and a face resembling a demon woman.

basis_claims.quote: Ouni looks like an ugly old woman with an angry face and a body covered in long, black hair. She is a kind of yamauba, or mountain hag. She lives deep in the mountains, away from civilization, and only occasionally appears before humans.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, ouni tampak seperti perempuan tua buruk rupa berwajah marah dengan tubuh tertutup rambut hitam panjang; ia sejenis yamauba (nenek gunung) yang tinggal jauh di pegunungan dan hanya sesekali menampakkan diri kepada manusia.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, ouni looks like an ugly old woman with an angry face and a body covered in long black hair; she is a kind of yamauba, or mountain hag, who lives deep in the mountains and only occasionally appears before humans.

basis_claims.quote: Unlike most yamauba, ouni are friendly towards humans who treat them kindly. They occasionally visit rural houses or mountain huts late at night.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, tidak seperti kebanyakan yamauba, ouni bersahabat dengan manusia yang memperlakukannya dengan baik, dan sesekali mengunjungi rumah desa atau pondok gunung larut malam.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, unlike most yamauba, ouni are friendly toward humans who treat them kindly, and occasionally visit rural houses or mountain huts late at night.

basis_claims.quote: If they are kind and invite her in, during the night she spins an enormous amount of thread for the family and then vanishes without a trace.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, bila penghuni rumah ramah dan mengundangnya masuk, pada malam hari ia memintal benang dalam jumlah sangat banyak bagi keluarga itu lalu lenyap tanpa jejak.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, if the household is kind and invites her in, during the night she spins an enormous amount of thread for the family and then vanishes without a trace.

basis_claims.quote: Ouni 苧うに おうに Translation: ramie peat (named for her resemblance to these plants) ALTERNATIVE NAMES: wauwau Habitat: deep in the mountains

statement.id: Yokai.com menulis 苧うに (おうに) dengan terjemahan "gambut rami", nama lain wauwau, dan habitat jauh di pegunungan.
statement.en: Yokai.com gives 苧うに (おうに) with the translation "ramie peat", the alternative name wauwau, and deep in the mountains as habitat.

basis_claims.quote: The "o" (苧) in "ouni" refers to the ramie plant or to bundles of string made from ramie, hemp, among others, so it is said that Sekien gave it the name "ouni" because it conjures up the image of a yōkai with head and body hair made of layers of this "o".

statement.id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa "o" (苧) dalam "ouni" menunjuk rami atau gulungan benang dari rami dan semacamnya, sehingga dikatakan Sekien menamainya "ouni" karena membayangkan yōkai berambut kepala dan tubuh dari lapisan "o".
statement.en: Wikipedia notes that the "o" (苧) in "ouni" refers to the ramie plant or to bundles of string made from ramie, hemp and the like, so it is said Sekien named it "ouni" because it evokes a yōkai with head and body hair made of layers of this "o".

basis_claims.quote: the following example is from Kotaki, Nishikubiki, Echigo Province (now Itoigawa, Niigata Prefecture). ... a yamauba appeared and said "I'll also spin some" and started to help along. The yamauba bit the hemp and drew out strings and then spun bundles of string at a speed unbelievable for humans.

statement.id: Wikipedia mencatat tuturan dari Kotaki, Provinsi Echigo, tempat seorang yamauba muncul, ikut membantu memintal, menggigit rami dan menarik benang, lalu memintal gulungan benang dengan kecepatan tak masuk akal bagi manusia.
statement.en: Wikipedia records a tale from Kotaki, Echigo Province, in which a yamauba appeared and helped spin, biting the hemp to draw out strings and spinning bundles of string at a speed unbelievable for humans.

statement.en: The Pombero generally dwells in rural areas, in the forest, though he sometimes inhabits an abandoned house, deserted rooms in an occupied home, or empty barns.

basis_claims.quote: One common aspect of the myth among various Guaraní based societies is that the Pombero protects the birds from children who hunt them with slingshots.

statement.id: Unsur yang umum dalam mitos di berbagai masyarakat berbasis Guaraní adalah bahwa Pombero melindungi burung dari anak-anak yang memburunya dengan ketapel.
statement.en: A common element of the myth in various Guaraní-based societies is that the Pombero protects birds from children who hunt them with slingshots.

basis_claims.quote: The Pombero is difficult, if not impossible, to detect due to his silent movements as well as other supernatural abilities, such as being able to turn invisible, squeeze through impossibly narrow spaces, or other such feats.
