basis_claims.quote: Sedna (Inuktitut: ᓴᓐᓇ, romanized: Sanna , previously Sedna or Sidne) is the goddess of the sea and marine animals in Inuit religion, also known as the Mother of the Sea or Mistress of the Sea.

statement.id: Sedna (Inuktitut: ᓴᓐᓇ, Sanna; sebelumnya Sedna atau Sidne) adalah dewi laut dan hewan laut dalam agama Inuit, juga dikenal sebagai Ibu Laut atau Nyonya Laut.
statement.en: Sedna (Inuktitut: ᓴᓐᓇ, Sanna; previously Sedna or Sidne) is the goddess of the sea and marine animals in Inuit religion, also known as the Mother of the Sea or Mistress of the Sea.

basis_claims.quote: The story of Sedna, which is a creation myth, describes how she came to rule over Adlivun, the Inuit equivalent of the underworld.

statement.id: Kisah Sedna, yang merupakan mitos penciptaan, menceritakan bagaimana ia sampai menguasai Adlivun, padanan dunia bawah dalam kepercayaan Inuit.
statement.en: The story of Sedna, a creation myth, describes how she came to rule over Adlivun, the Inuit equivalent of the underworld.

basis_claims.quote: An origin myth tells how Sedna was once a girl who was thrown overboard from a vessel. While she tried to hang on, her fingers were cut off at the joints. She sank to the bottom of the sea, the segments of her fingers turning into sea mammals, and she became the Sea Woman, who was in control of these animals.

statement.id: Sebuah mitos asal-usul menceritakan bahwa Sedna dulunya seorang gadis yang dilempar dari kapal. Saat ia berpegangan, jari-jarinya dipotong di ruas-ruasnya. Ia tenggelam ke dasar laut, ruas-ruas jarinya menjadi mamalia laut, dan ia menjadi Wanita Laut (Sea Woman) yang menguasai hewan-hewan itu.
statement.en: An origin myth tells how Sedna was once a girl thrown overboard from a vessel; her fingers were cut off at the joints as she held on, the segments turned into sea mammals, and she sank to the sea bottom and became the Sea Woman, who controlled these animals.

basis_claims.quote: she became the Sea Woman, who was in control of these animals. According to some Iglulik Inuit and Baffin Islanders, she also ruled over the souls of those who had gone to the undersea land of the dead.

statement.id: Ia menjadi Wanita Laut yang menguasai hewan-hewan itu. Menurut sebagian orang Iglulik Inuit dan penduduk Baffin, ia juga menguasai jiwa orang-orang yang telah pergi ke negeri orang mati di bawah laut.
statement.en: She became the Sea Woman, who controlled these animals, and according to some Iglulik Inuit and Baffin Islanders she also ruled over the souls of those who had gone to the undersea land of the dead.

basis_claims.quote: According to Inuit belief, the Sea Woman had the power to withhold the sea animals when certain hunting, birth, and death taboos had been broken. In Greenland it was told that the transgressions would materialize as dirt in the Sea Woman's hair, making her feel uncomfortable; because she had no fingers, she was unable to comb her hair.

statement.id: Menurut kepercayaan Inuit, Wanita Laut berkuasa menahan hewan laut bila pantangan tertentu tentang perburuan, kelahiran, dan kematian dilanggar. Di Greenland diceritakan bahwa pelanggaran itu menjadi kotoran di rambutnya hingga ia tidak nyaman; karena tak berjari, ia tidak dapat menyisir rambutnya.
statement.en: According to Inuit belief the Sea Woman could withhold the sea animals when certain hunting, birth, and death taboos were broken; in Greenland the transgressions were said to become dirt in her hair, making her uncomfortable, and having no fingers she could not comb it.

basis_claims.quote: Before the shaman could comb Sedna's hair he had to fight her. Afterward, she would set the sea animals free, and the shaman would return

statement.id: Sebelum dapat menyisir rambut Sedna, sang dukun harus melawannya. Setelah itu ia membebaskan hewan-hewan laut, dan sang dukun kembali.
statement.en: Before the shaman could comb Sedna's hair he had to fight her; afterward she would set the sea animals free and the shaman would return.

basis_claims.quote: Seals and other sea animals were the basis of the existence of nearly all Inuit. The relationship with the Sea Woman was therefore important but very sensitive: she not only controlled these animals, they originated from her.

statement.id: Anjing laut dan hewan laut lain menjadi dasar kehidupan hampir semua orang Inuit. Karena itu hubungan dengan Wanita Laut penting tetapi sangat peka: ia tidak hanya menguasai hewan-hewan itu, mereka berasal darinya.
statement.en: Seals and other sea animals were the basis of nearly all Inuit existence, so the relationship with the Sea Woman was important but very sensitive: she not only controlled these animals, they originated from her.

basis_claims.quote: When she still clung to the side of the boat with the stumps of her fingers, her father cut them off at the last joint, and these segments turned into walruses. Sometimes the order of the creation of the sea animals is different, with whales being created first (the girl's nails are associated with baleen), followed by small seals and bearded seals.

statement.id: Ketika ia masih berpegangan dengan sisa-sisa jarinya, ayahnya memotongnya pada ruas terakhir dan potongan itu menjadi walrus. Kadang urutan terciptanya hewan laut berbeda: paus tercipta lebih dulu (kuku sang gadis dikaitkan dengan balin), disusul anjing laut kecil dan anjing laut berjanggut.
statement.en: When she still clung with the stumps of her fingers, her father cut them off at the last joint and these segments turned into walruses; sometimes the order differs, with whales created first (the girl's nails are linked to baleen), then small seals and bearded seals.

basis_claims.quote: in art Sedna is usually depicted with the head and upper body of a woman and the tail of a marine mammal, similar to a mermaid.

statement.id: Dalam seni, Sedna biasanya digambarkan berkepala dan berbadan atas perempuan dengan ekor mamalia laut, mirip putri duyung.
statement.en: In art Sedna is usually depicted with the head and upper body of a woman and the tail of a marine mammal, similar to a mermaid.

statement.en: The legend of alligators inhabiting the sewer system of New York City is a widely circulated urban myth; it suggests that alligators navigate the city's sewers, preying on rats and other refuse, and posing a threat to sewer workers, who are said to carry firearms for protection.

basis_claims.quote: The sewer alligator is an urban legend about alligators that are said to live in sewers outside alligators' native range.

statement.id: Aligator saluran air adalah legenda urban tentang aligator yang dikatakan hidup di saluran air di luar wilayah asli aligator.
statement.en: The sewer alligator is an urban legend about alligators that are said to live in sewers outside alligators' native range.

basis_claims.quote: According to the lore, these alligators are often described as large and vicious, with some attributing a lack of pigmentation to their purported status as "albinos."

statement.id: Menurut kisahnya, aligator ini sering digambarkan besar dan buas, dengan sebagian orang mengaitkan kurangnya pigmen dengan status mereka yang konon 'albino'.
statement.en: According to the lore, these alligators are often described as large and vicious, with some attributing a lack of pigmentation to their purported status as 'albinos'.

shangyang.depicted_variant: the one-legged bird dancing as a water omen before the hall of Qi

visual_requirements.description: ONE natural BIRD, one head/TWO eyes, ONE beak, TWO wings, EXACTLY ONE LEG and ONE birdfoot beneath body. No second leg folded or hidden. Brownblack feather species editorial, not a fiery phoenix or crane dragon.
Predicts heavy rain, NOT controls it: natural heavy rain begins beyond hall with water rushing into a repaired drainagechannel. No magicglow.
Court of Qi before a plain ancient hall; drained stonecourtyard in rain, no signs or inscriptions.

shangyang.aura: HOP toward viewer with both wings spread dramatically, singlefoot clearly airborne and whole leg visible under body, alert stern gaze. Grounded in shangyang-c03, shangyang-c07, shangyang-c01, shangyang-c04, shangyang-c08, shangyang-c09.

basis_claims.quote: The Shangyang (商羊), (or shang yang) in Chinese mythology was a rainbird (i.e. it could predict rain). It was one of several important mythical birds in this tradition. The Shangyang was particularly associated with the Lord of Rain, Yu Shi. Once, the Shangyang was said to have visited the royal court of Qi, where it danced on one leg.

statement.id: Shangyang adalah burung mitologi Tiongkok yang dapat meramalkan hujan.
statement.en: Shangyang is a Chinese mythological bird capable of predicting rain.

basis_claims.quote: The Shangyang (商羊), (or shang yang) in Chinese mythology was a rainbird (i.e. it could predict rain). It was one of several important mythical birds in this tradition. The Shangyang was particularly associated with the Lord of Rain, Yu Shi. Once, the Shangyang was said to have visited the royal court of Qi, where it danced on one leg.

statement.id: Sebuah kisah menyebutnya menari dengan satu kaki di istana Qi.
statement.en: One account describes it dancing on one leg at the court of Qi.

basis_claims.quote: Confucius, who was familiar with the Shangyang, predicted heavy rain and advised the people to dig drainage channels and build dikes. By following the sage's advice, Qi avoided the disaster caused by a subsequent flood, while other states that ignored this advice were heavily damaged.

statement.id: Konfusius, yang mengenal Shangyang, meramalkan hujan lebat dan menasihati rakyat menggali saluran dan membangun tanggul; dengan mengikuti nasihat itu Qi terhindar dari bencana banjir yang menyusul, sedangkan negara lain yang mengabaikannya rusak parah.
statement.en: Confucius, who was familiar with the Shangyang, predicted heavy rain and advised the people to dig drainage channels and build dikes; by following this advice Qi avoided the flood that followed, while other states that ignored it were heavily damaged.

basis_claims.quote: 齊有一足之鳥，飛集於宮朝，下止於殿前，舒翅而跳。齊侯大怪之，使使聘魯，問孔子。

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik ini, seekor burung berkaki satu (一足之鳥) terbang ke istana negeri Qi (齊), mendarat di depan balai, dan melompat dengan sayap terkembang; Marquis Qi (齊侯) heran lalu mengutus orang ke negeri Lu (魯) untuk bertanya kepada Konfusius (孔子).
statement.en: In this classical text, a one-legged bird (一足之鳥) flies into the court of Qi (齊), lands before the hall, and hops with spread wings; the Marquis of Qi (齊侯) is astonished and sends an envoy to Lu (魯) to ask Confucius (孔子).

basis_claims.quote: 孔子曰：「此鳥名曰商羊，水祥也。昔童兒有屈其一腳，振訊兩眉，而跳且謠曰：『天將大雨，商羊鼓舞。』今齊有之，其應至矣。」

statement.id: Konfusius (孔子) berkata bahwa burung itu bernama Shangyang (商羊), pertanda air (水祥); dulu anak-anak menekuk satu kaki, mengerutkan alis, melompat sambil bernyanyi "Langit akan menurunkan hujan lebat, Shangyang menari", dan kini Qi memilikinya sehingga pertandanya telah tiba.
statement.en: Confucius (孔子) says the bird is named Shangyang (商羊), a water omen (水祥); children once bent one leg, knitted their brows, and hopped singing "Heaven will send great rain, the Shangyang dances", and now that Qi has it, the sign has arrived.

basis_claims.quote: 急告民趨治溝渠，修堤防，將有大水為災。頃之大霖雨，水溢泛諸國，傷害民人。唯齊有備，不敗。

statement.id: Rakyat segera diberi tahu agar membenahi parit dan memperbaiki tanggul karena banjir besar akan datang; tak lama kemudian hujan deras turun, air meluap ke berbagai negara dan melukai penduduk, tetapi hanya Qi (齊) yang siap dan tidak rusak.
statement.en: The people were told urgently to repair ditches and dikes because a great flood was coming; soon heavy rain fell, water overflowed many states and harmed the people, but only Qi (齊), which had prepared, was not ruined.

Field at SUNSET with tall stalks and a confusing path junction.

statement.en: In Slavic paganism Sheka is a field spirit: a deformed dwarf with differently coloured eyes and grass instead of hair, appearing at noon or sunset in all-black or all-white clothes.

basis_claims.quote: Sheka in Slavic paganism is field spirit ... According to local beliefs it leads wandering people in a field astray, give them diseases or ride them over with horses if they are found asleep. It enjoys pulling the hair of peasants working in the midday.

statement.id: Dalam paganisme Slavia, Sheka menurut kepercayaan setempat menyesatkan orang yang mengembara di ladang, menularkan penyakit, atau melindas orang yang tertidur dengan kuda; ia senang menarik rambut petani yang bekerja di siang hari.
statement.en: In Slavic paganism, according to local beliefs, Sheka leads wandering people astray in a field, gives them diseases or rides them over with horses if they are found asleep; it enjoys pulling the hair of peasants working at midday.

basis_claims.quote: Sheka in Slavic paganism is field spirit ... It also makes little children get lost in cornfields.

statement.id: Dalam paganisme Slavia, Sheka membuat anak-anak kecil tersesat di ladang jagung (cornfield).
statement.en: In Slavic paganism, Sheka makes little children get lost in cornfields.

basis_claims.quote: It has no facial features, but located in its butt hole is a large eye which shines like lightning.

basis_claims.quote: Before they can answer, the shirime drops its kimono to the ground and bends over, spreading its butt cheeks and revealing the giant, shining eye located inside of its butt hole.

statement.id: Sebelum mereka menjawab, shirime menjatuhkan kimononya, membungkuk, dan memperlihatkan mata raksasa yang bersinar di lubang pantatnya.
statement.en: Before they can answer, shirime drops its kimono, bends over, and reveals the giant shining eye in its butt hole.

basis_claims.quote: Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god. He usually appears with Qianliyan as a guardian of the temples of the sea goddess Mazu.

statement.en: Shunfeng'er is a Chinese sea and door god guarding Mazu temples with Qianliyan.

basis_claims.quote: The name "Shunfeng'er" literally means "Wind Accompanying Ears" in reference to his ability to hear any sound carried upon the wind.

statement.id: Namanya mengacu pada kemampuan mendengar suara yang dibawa angin.
statement.en: His name refers to hearing sounds carried by the wind.

basis_claims.quote: Shunfeng'er's sharp hearing is employed to help sailors distinguish favorable winds from coming storms. In some accounts, he is capable of hearing everything in the world, no matter how quietly spoken, and was therefore also worshipped as a witness and guarantor of oaths and contracts.

statement.id: Pendengaran Shunfeng'er yang tajam dipakai untuk membantu pelaut membedakan angin yang baik dari badai yang akan datang; dalam sebagian kisah ia mampu mendengar segalanya di dunia, sepelan apa pun, sehingga juga dipuja sebagai saksi dan penjamin sumpah dan kontrak.
statement.en: Shunfeng'er's sharp hearing is used to help sailors tell favorable winds from coming storms; in some accounts he can hear everything in the world however quietly spoken, and was therefore also worshipped as a witness and guarantor of oaths and contracts.

basis_claims.quote: Shunfeng'er is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed or befriended by the sea goddess Mazu.

statement.en: Shunfeng'er is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed or befriended by the sea goddess Mazu.

basis_claims.quote: By one account, he and Qianliyan appeared off Meizhou Island during a storm and were defeated by Mazu's magical silk scarf, which blew clouds of sand into their ears and eyes. After their submission, they pledged their loyalty when she kindly healed them of the damage she had caused them.

statement.id: Menurut satu kisah, ia dan Qianliyan muncul di lepas pantai Pulau Meizhou saat badai dan dikalahkan oleh selendang sutra sakti Mazu yang meniupkan awan pasir ke telinga dan mata mereka; setelah tunduk, mereka berjanji setia ketika Mazu menyembuhkan luka yang ditimbulkannya.
statement.en: By one account, he and Qianliyan appeared off Meizhou Island during a storm and were defeated by Mazu's magical silk scarf, which blew clouds of sand into their ears and eyes; after submitting they pledged loyalty when she healed the damage she had caused.

basis_claims.quote: Shunfeng'er typically appears as a red- or brown-skinned demon cupping a hand to one of his ears. He also occasionally appears with three heads and six arms.

statement.id: Shunfeng'er biasanya digambarkan sebagai iblis berkulit merah atau cokelat yang menangkupkan tangan ke salah satu telinganya, dan kadang-kadang bertiga kepala dan berlengan enam.
statement.en: Shunfeng'er typically appears as a red- or brown-skinned demon cupping a hand to one of his ears, and occasionally with three heads and six arms.

basis_claims.quote: 在媽祖廟裡，千里眼和順風耳分別站立於媽祖的左右兩側 ... 而順風耳則手舉至側耳做聽音狀的姿態，以其無遠弗屆的聽力，為媽祖偵聽世上的一切事物。祂們的另一手則持有兵器。

statement.id: Di kuil Mazu (媽祖), 千里眼 dan 順風耳 berdiri di kiri dan kanan Mazu; 順風耳 mengangkat tangan ke samping telinga dalam sikap mendengar, memakai pendengarannya yang tak terbatas untuk menyelidiki segala hal di dunia bagi Mazu, dan tangan yang lain memegang senjata.
statement.en: In Mazu (媽祖) temples, 千里眼 and 順風耳 stand on Mazu's left and right; 順風耳 raises a hand to his ear in a listening pose, using his boundless hearing to scout everything in the world for Mazu, and the other hand holds a weapon.

basis_claims.quote: 關於千里眼和順風耳的傳說不一，總的來說，祂們原來是在桃花山上的妖精，不僅面貌猙獰，使居民恐懼外，更時常擾亂地方、為害百姓。最後為媽祖收伏，成為隨駕將軍。

statement.id: Legenda tentang 千里眼 dan 順風耳 berbeda-beda, tetapi pada umumnya keduanya semula adalah siluman di Gunung Peach Blossom (桃花山) yang berwajah garang, menakuti penduduk, dan sering mengganggu daerah itu serta merugikan rakyat, hingga akhirnya ditaklukkan Mazu (媽祖) dan menjadi jenderal pengiringnya.
statement.en: Legends about 千里眼 and 順風耳 differ, but generally they were originally spirit-monsters on Peach Blossom Mountain (桃花山) with fierce faces who frightened residents and often disturbed the area and harmed the people, until Mazu (媽祖) subdued them and they became her attendant generals.

statement.en: Shuten-dōji is an oni leader killed by Minamoto no Raikō in Japanese legend.

basis_claims.quote: Shuten-dōji had his lair at Mount Ōe (大江山) northwest of the city of Kyoto, or Mount Ibuki, depending on the version.

statement.id: Berbagai versi menempatkan sarangnya di Gunung Ōe atau Gunung Ibuki.
statement.en: Accounts place his dwelling on Mount Ōe or Mount Ibuki.

basis_claims.quote: 丹波の大江山に住んでいたという伝説上の鬼の頭目。都に出ては婦女・財宝を奪ったので、勅命により、源頼光が四天王を率いて退治したという。

statement.id: デジタル大辞泉は、酒呑童子を丹波の大江山に住んだという伝説上の鬼の頭目とし、都で婦女や財宝を奪ったため、勅命により源頼光が四天王を率いて退治したと記す。
statement.en: The Digital Daijisen dictionary describes Shuten-dōji as a legendary leader of the oni said to live on Ōeyama in Tanba, who plundered women and treasure in the capital and was said to have been destroyed by Minamoto no Raikō leading his Four Guardian Kings under imperial command.

basis_claims.quote: 酒呑童子の名称は,《大江山絵詞》では〈酒を深く愛する者〉ゆえの名となっている
basis_claims.locator: 世界大百科事典 (平凡社)

statement.id: 世界大百科事典によれば、『大江山絵詞』では酒呑童子の名は「酒を深く愛する者」であることに由来する。
statement.en: According to the Heibonsha World Encyclopedia, in the Ōeyama Ekotoba the name Shuten-dōji comes from his being someone who deeply loves sake.

basis_claims.quote: According to the Ōeyama Ekotoba version, Shuten-dōji returned to his true form when he slept. He was 50 feet in height, had a red body and a five-horned head, with fifteen eyes

statement.id: Menurut versi Ōeyama Ekotoba, Shuten-dōji kembali ke wujud aslinya saat tidur: setinggi 50 kaki, bertubuh merah, berkepala bertanduk lima, dan bermata lima belas.
statement.en: According to the Ōeyama Ekotoba version, Shuten-dōji returned to his true form when he slept: 50 feet tall, with a red body and a five-horned head with fifteen eyes.

sihuhata.depicted_variant: the four-eared five-eyed black bearlike charcoal eater of Lanna lore

visual_requirements.description: ONE BLACK-HAIRED BEARLIKE creature, ONE head with EXACTLY FOUR distinct round bearears (two on each side) and EXACTLY FIVE EYES (two naturaleyes, two higher broweyes, one centerforehead eye), FOUR bearlimbs and ONE short beartail. No horns or extraheads.
Eats burningcharcoal and digests it into gold: physical emberlight at mouth/paw and a few smallgold pieces behind on floor, no excretion/anatomical display or glowing aura.
Simple rural Lanna home earthenfloor and darkwood doorway, creature brought home in story.

sihuhata.aura: BITE glowing burningcharcoal held in one forepaw, turn five-eyed face directly toward viewer, other forepaw plants hard on earthenfloor with sharp intent;4ears/5eyes allvisible. Grounded in sihuhata-c01, sihuhata-c02, sihuhata-c07, sihuhata-c08, sihuhata-c05.

basis_claims.quote: It is usually described as a large animal with four ears and five eyes.

statement.id: Sihuhata adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Lanna Thailand utara, biasanya memiliki empat telinga dan lima mata.
statement.en: Sihuhata is a creature of Northern Thailand's Lanna folklore, usually having four ears and five eyes.

basis_claims.quote: In one Lanna manuscript version, it resembles a bear, eats burning charcoal, and produces gold as excrement.

statement.id: Satu versi naskah menggambarkan makhluk mirip beruang yang makan arang menyala dan menghasilkan kotoran emas.
statement.en: One manuscript version describes a bearlike creature eating burning charcoal and producing gold as excrement.

basis_claims.quote: He brings the animal home and tries to feed it grass and leaves, but it refuses them.

statement.id: Seorang anak menangkap makhluk itu dan membawanya pulang; ia menolak rumput dan daun.
statement.en: A boy catches the creature and brings it home; it refuses grass and leaves.

basis_claims.quote: After three days he caught a strange animal that was like a bear, with black hair, and had got four ears and five eyes.

statement.id: Dalam penceritaan ulang legenda di jurnal ini, setelah tiga hari seorang anak laki-laki menangkap hewan aneh seperti beruang berbulu hitam dengan empat telinga dan lima mata.
statement.en: In the legend as retold in this journal article, after three days a boy caught a strange animal like a bear, with black hair, four ears and five eyes.

basis_claims.quote: The next day the boy was very surprised to see that the strange beast had digested the coals into gold.

statement.id: Keesokan harinya anak itu terkejut melihat hewan aneh itu telah mencerna bara menjadi emas.
statement.en: The next day the boy was very surprised to see the strange beast had digested the coals into gold.

spirit-turtle.depicted_variant: the five-colored thousand-year-old spiritual turtle of Baopuzi

visual_requirements.description: ONE LIVING TURTLE, ONE head/TWO natural turtleeyes, FOUR normal turtlelegs and ONE tail, ONE ancient shell marked with FIVE clear colors BLUE, RED, YELLOW, WHITE and BLACK. No dragonhead, feathers, horns or giantarchitecture on shell.
No documented superpower selected; thousandyear longevity c06/c12 conveyed through ancient tactile shell, no aura/magic or giant size.
Minimal darkstone and wetearth, neutral editorial scenery for EastAsian turtle; no invented named place.

spirit-turtle.aura: STRIDE up a roughstone bank toward close viewer, one forefoot gripping stone and head thrust forward, tail sweeping wetearth; fivecolored weatheredshell looming in closeperspective. Grounded in spirit-turtle-c01, spirit-turtle-c05, spirit-turtle-c06, spirit-turtle-c12, spirit-turtle-c02.

basis_claims.quote: The spirit turtle (Chinese: 靈龜) or spirit tortoise is a turtle originated from Chinese mythology and spread with East Asian cultural sphere.

statement.id: Kura-kura roh adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
statement.en: The spirit turtle is a creature of Chinese mythology.

basis_claims.quote: It is believed by East Asian cultures, like other turtles in mythology, to represent longevity (壽命).

statement.id: Ia melambangkan umur panjang dalam tradisi Asia Timur.
statement.en: It represents longevity in East Asian traditions.

basis_claims.quote: According to the Shuyiji (述異記 Tales of Strange Matters) compiled by Ren Fang, a turtle that has lived for one thousand years has grown hair, a five thousand year old tortoise is called a "divine turtle" (神龜) and an animal older than ten thousand years is called a "spiritual turtle" (靈龜).

statement.id: Shuyiji menyebut kura-kura yang berusia lebih dari sepuluh ribu tahun sebagai kura-kura roh.
statement.en: The Shuyiji calls a turtle older than ten thousand years spiritual.

basis_claims.quote: The Baopuzi gives a slightly different account, describing the spirit turtle as one thousand years old.

statement.id: Baopuzi justru menggambarkan kura-kura roh berusia seribu tahun.
statement.en: The Baopuzi instead describes a thousand-year-old spirit turtle.

basis_claims.quote: The Baopuzi gives a slightly different account, describing the spirit turtle as one thousand years old. ... The text continues to describe the turtle as having five colors: blue, red, yellow, white, and black; together representing the five elements.

statement.id: Baopuzi menggambarkan kura-kura roh berusia seribu tahun dan berlanjut menyebut kura-kura itu berlima warna, biru, merah, kuning, putih, dan hitam, yang bersama-sama mewakili lima unsur.
statement.en: The Baopuzi describes the spirit turtle as one thousand years old and goes on to describe the turtle as having five colors, blue, red, yellow, white and black, together representing the five elements.

suijin.depicted_variant: the freshwater waterdeity manifesting in sourced serpentform

visual_requirements.description: ONE LIVING SERPENT deity, ONE natural snakehead/TWO eyes, long continuous snakebody/ONE tapering tail, NO legs/arms/wings/horns/dragonwhiskers. Wet natural scale texture, no invented crown.
Presides over freshwater/ricefieldwater and bringsfertility: forceful cleanwater flows through irrigationweir into paddies, physically turbulent but no beams/glow.
Freshwater irrigationweir beside ricepaddies, small plain uninscribed stoneshrine in distance.

suijin.aura: RISE and COIL forcefully across freshwaterweir toward close viewer, head lifted with composed protective intent, body displaces water into two visible irrigationchannels. Grounded in suijin-c01, suijin-c02, suijin-c06, suijin-c05, suijin-c08, suijin-c11, suijin-c12.

basis_claims.quote: Suijin or Mizugami ... lit. "water god/deity") is a general name for the god of water in Japanese mythology.

statement.id: Suijin atau Mizugami ("dewa air") adalah nama umum untuk dewa air dalam mitologi Jepang.
statement.en: Suijin or Mizugami ("water god/deity") is a general name for the god of water in Japanese mythology.

basis_claims.quote: The term refers to the heavenly and earthly manifestations of the benevolent Shinto divinity of water (mainly freshwater), as well as to a wide variety of mythical and magical creatures found in lakes, ponds, springs, and wells, including serpents (snakes, dragons, eels, fish, turtles), and the flesh-eating kappa.

statement.id: Istilah ini merujuk pada perwujudan surgawi dan duniawi dewa air Shinto yang baik hati (terutama air tawar), serta beragam makhluk gaib di danau, kolam, mata air, dan sumur, termasuk ular, naga, belut, ikan, kura-kura, dan kappa pemakan daging.
statement.en: The term refers to the heavenly and earthly manifestations of the benevolent Shinto divinity of water (mainly freshwater) and to many mythical creatures in lakes, ponds, springs and wells, including serpents, dragons, eels, fish, turtles and the flesh-eating kappa.

basis_claims.quote: 水神の実態は複雑多様であるが，もっとも典型的なのは農耕社会における水田稲作民にとっての守護神である。水神は豊穣をもたらす神であり，田の神と同一視されている。一般には，水田の用水堰か水田のほとりの石祠に祭られている。また山中の水源地に水分（みくまり）神として祭られる場合は，山の神と同一視される。
basis_claims.locator: Bagian 日本 (世界大百科事典)

statement.id: Wujud dewa air beragam, tetapi yang paling khas adalah pelindung petani sawah; ia dewa yang membawa kesuburan, disamakan dengan dewa sawah, dan dipuja di bendungan atau kuil batu di tepi sawah; bila dipuja di sumber air pegunungan sebagai dewa pembagi air (mikumari), ia disamakan dengan dewa gunung.
statement.en: The water deity takes many forms, but the most typical is the guardian of rice-paddy farmers; it brings fertility, is identified with the rice-field deity, and is enshrined at irrigation weirs or stone shrines beside paddies; when enshrined at mountain water sources as the water-distributing deity (mikumari), it is identified with the mountain deity.

basis_claims.quote: 水神の表徴として代表的なのは河童である。水の妖怪であるが，水神が河童の姿をとったと想像される民間伝承は多い。また水神は，竜やヘビ，ウナギ，サル，クモなどの姿をとると信じられている。
basis_claims.locator: Bagian 日本 (世界大百科事典)

statement.id: Lambang khas dewa air adalah kappa; banyak cerita rakyat membayangkan dewa air berwujud kappa, dan ia dipercaya juga berwujud naga, ular, belut, monyet, atau laba-laba.
statement.en: The typical emblem of the water deity is the kappa; many folk tales imagine the water deity taking kappa form, and it is believed also to take the form of a dragon, snake, eel, monkey or spider.

basis_claims.quote: People worship Suijin with offerings, believing that doing so will ensure pure and unpolluted water for drinking, agriculture, and sanitation, and will bring success in fishing trips, fertility, motherhood, and easy childbirth.

statement.id: Orang memuja Suijin dengan persembahan, percaya hal itu menjamin air yang bersih untuk minum, pertanian, dan sanitasi, serta membawa keberhasilan melaut, kesuburan, keibuan, dan persalinan mudah.
statement.en: People worship Suijin with offerings, believing this ensures pure and unpolluted water for drinking, agriculture and sanitation and brings success in fishing, fertility, motherhood and easy childbirth.

basis_claims.quote: すい‐じん【水神】 水をつかさどる神。飲み水や田の水などを支配する神。水伯。
basis_claims.locator: Entri 水神 (デジタル大辞泉)

statement.id: Kamus Jepang mendefinisikan suijin sebagai dewa yang menguasai air, termasuk air minum dan air sawah; disebut juga suihaku.
statement.en: A Japanese dictionary defines suijin as a deity who presides over water, including drinking water and water for rice fields; also called suihaku.

basis_claims.quote: Suijin appears as a stone plaque or even a small stone set upright near the emergence of a spring.

statement.id: Suijin tampil sebagai lempeng batu atau bahkan batu kecil yang ditegakkan di dekat tempat munculnya mata air.
statement.en: Suijin appears as a stone plaque or even a small stone set upright near the emergence of a spring.

taniwha.depicted_variant: the inland whale-sized tuatara-like ancestral waterguardian

visual_requirements.description: ONE huge TUATARA/GECKO-like reptilian guardian of whale-like dimensions, ONE head/TWO eyes, FOUR lizardlegs, ONE long lizardtail, ONE row of spines alongback. No wings, dragonhorns or extraheads.
Can tunnel earth and uproot trees: physical tornriverbank/uprooting c05, no firebreath/lightning. Guardian shown imposing not eating or persecuting people.
Deep riverpool beside dark cave and forestbank in Aotearoa, dangerous naturalcurrent.

taniwha.aura: BURROW upward from riverbank and PLANT broad forefeet toward lowviewer, backspines tower, muddy earth rolls aside and one tree tips with exposed uprooted roots. Grounded in taniwha-c01, taniwha-c02, taniwha-c05.

basis_claims.quote: In Māori mythology, taniwha ... are large supernatural beings that live in deep pools in rivers, dark caves, or in the sea, especially in places with dangerous currents or deceptive breakers (giant waves).

statement.id: Taniwha adalah makhluk gaib besar yang hidup di lubuk sungai dalam, gua, atau laut berarus kuat.
statement.en: Taniwha are large supernatural beings living in deep river pools, caves, or seas with dangerous currents.

basis_claims.quote: They may be considered highly respected kaitiaki (protective guardians) of people and places, or in some traditions as dangerous, predatory beings

statement.id: Taniwha dihormati sebagai kaitiaki penjaga pelindung manusia dan tempat.
statement.en: Taniwha are respected as kaitiaki protective guardians of people and places.

basis_claims.quote: In inland waters, they may still be of whale-like dimensions, but look more like a gecko or a tuatara, having a row of spines along the back. Other taniwha appear as a floating log, which behaves in a disconcerting way. Some can tunnel through the earth, uprooting trees in the process.

statement.id: Di perairan pedalaman, mereka mungkin tetap berukuran sebesar paus tetapi tampak lebih mirip cicak atau tuatara dengan deretan duri di punggung; taniwha lain tampak sebagai batang kayu apung yang bertingkah mengganggu, dan sebagian dapat menerobos tanah sambil mencabut pohon.
statement.en: In inland waters they may still be of whale-like dimensions but look more like a gecko or tuatara with a row of spines along the back; other taniwha appear as a floating log that behaves disconcertingly, and some can tunnel through the earth, uprooting trees.

tezcatlipoca.depicted_variant: the smokingmirror Aztec deity with obsidian leftfoot and four arrows

visual_requirements.description: ONE human-shaped male deity, ONE head/TWO eyes/TWO arms/TWO legs, but anatomical LEFT FOOT is replaced entirely by ONE polished BLACK OBSIDIAN roundMIRROR at leftankle; anatomicalRIGHTfoot normal. Fullyopaque plain warriorcostume. AnatomicalRIGHThand holds EXACTLY FOUR separated ARROWS, fourarrowheads plainlycountable; a single TURQUOISE SNAKE coils nearby.

Associated with night/hurricanes/obsidian/conflict; naturalviolentwind blows dust and trees, mirrored blacksurface releases restrained ordinarysmoke as visualinterpretation of SmokingMirror name, no lasers/runes/glow.
Crossroads at dead ofnight, ancient Mesoamerican darkroad, no invented templedecoration or letters.

tezcatlipoca.aura: STRIDE toward lowviewer at crossroads, raise fourarrows in righthand and set leftanklemirror closeabove wetstone, freehand opens incommand; hurricane wind pulls opaque cloak. Grounded in tezcatlipoca-c05, tezcatlipoca-c11, tezcatlipoca-c15, tezcatlipoca-c16, tezcatlipoca-c01, tezcatlipoca-c13, tezcatlipoca-c14.

basis_claims.quote: He is associated with a variety of concepts, including the night sky, hurricanes, obsidian, and conflict.

statement.id: Ia diasosiasikan dengan langit malam, badai angin topan, obsidian, dan konflik.
statement.en: He is associated with a variety of concepts, including the night sky, hurricanes, obsidian, and conflict.

basis_claims.quote: Tezcatlipoca (pron. Tez-ca-tli-po-ca) or 'Smoking Mirror' in Nahuatl was one of the most important gods in Postclassical Mesoamerican culture and particularly important for the Toltecs and the Aztecs, especially at Texcoco.

statement.id: Tezcatlipoca atau 'Cermin Berasap' dalam bahasa Nahuatl adalah salah satu dewa terpenting dalam budaya Mesoamerika Pascaklasik dan sangat penting bagi bangsa Toltec dan Aztec, terutama di Texcoco.
statement.en: Tezcatlipoca, or 'Smoking Mirror' in Nahuatl, was one of the most important gods in Postclassical Mesoamerican culture and particularly important for the Toltecs and the Aztecs, especially at Texcoco.

basis_claims.quote: When the special month finally came around the impersonator was handsomely dressed in a warrior costume and in a symbolic wedding festival he married his four goddesses. Honoured with flowers and dances the man-god was then ferried to a dedicated temple where he was promptly sacrificed and his heart removed using an obsidian knife in order to honour the real Tezcatlipoca.

statement.id: Ketika bulan khusus itu tiba, sang peniru berpakaian prajurit dan dalam pesta pernikahan simbolis menikahi empat dewinya. Dihormati dengan bunga dan tarian, ia lalu dibawa ke kuil khusus tempat ia segera dikorbankan dan jantungnya diambil dengan pisau obsidian untuk menghormati Tezcatlipoca yang sejati.
statement.en: When the month came, the impersonator was dressed in a warrior costume and in a symbolic wedding festival married his four goddesses; honoured with flowers and dances, the man-god was then ferried to a dedicated temple where he was sacrificed and his heart removed with an obsidian knife to honour the real Tezcatlipoca.

basis_claims.quote: Ever-present, the god could intervene directly in human affairs to bring both happiness and sorrow. Tezcatlipoca could take on more sinister connotations when he was known as lord of the shadows or night, a sorcerer of black magic and the bringer of evil, death and destruction

statement.id: Sang dewa selalu hadir dan dapat campur tangan langsung dalam urusan manusia untuk membawa kebahagiaan maupun kesedihan; Tezcatlipoca bisa bermakna lebih suram ketika dikenal sebagai penguasa bayang-bayang atau malam, penyihir ilmu hitam, dan pembawa kejahatan, kematian, dan kehancuran.
statement.en: The ever-present god could intervene directly in human affairs to bring both happiness and sorrow; Tezcatlipoca could take on more sinister connotations as lord of the shadows or night, a sorcerer of black magic and the bringer of evil, death and destruction.

basis_claims.quote: Also associated with conflict he was known as Yaotl or 'Enemy' and was patron of warriors and their training camps (telpochcalli). He was not always protective to soldiers, though, for sometimes he could be found at crossroads at the dead of night, ready to challenge any unsuspecting warriors.

statement.id: Dikaitkan dengan konflik, ia dikenal sebagai Yaotl atau 'Musuh' dan menjadi pelindung prajurit serta kamp pelatihan mereka (telpochcalli); namun ia tidak selalu melindungi prajurit, sebab kadang ia dapat ditemui di persimpangan jalan pada tengah malam, siap menantang prajurit yang lengah.
statement.en: Associated with conflict, he was known as Yaotl or 'Enemy' and was patron of warriors and their training camps (telpochcalli); he was not always protective to soldiers, for sometimes he could be found at crossroads at the dead of night, ready to challenge any unsuspecting warriors.

basis_claims.quote: in later depictions of the god he has a polished black obsidian mirror instead of a left foot. This replacement of the foot is a reference to a wound he received in his famous battle with Tlaltecuhtli during the Creation.

statement.id: Dalam penggambaran yang lebih belakangan, sang dewa memiliki cermin obsidian hitam mengilap sebagai pengganti kaki kiri; pergantian kaki itu merujuk pada luka yang ia terima dalam pertempuran terkenalnya dengan Tlaltecuhtli saat Penciptaan.
statement.en: In later depictions of the god he has a polished black obsidian mirror instead of a left foot, a reference to a wound he received in his famous battle with Tlaltecuhtli during the Creation.

basis_claims.quote: He is often in the company of a turquoise snake ... Sometimes he carries four arrows in his right hand, weapons he uses to punish wrongdoers.

statement.id: Ia sering ditemani ular pirus dan kadang membawa empat anak panah di tangan kanannya, senjata yang ia pakai untuk menghukum pelaku kejahatan.
statement.en: He is often in the company of a turquoise snake and sometimes carries four arrows in his right hand, weapons he uses to punish wrongdoers.

three-legged-crow.depicted_variant: the red three-legged solar crow of EastAsian myth

visual_requirements.description: ONE RED CROW, ONE head/TWO eyes/ONE crowbeak, TWO wings, EXACTLY THREE LEGS and THREE SEPARATE crowfeet beneathbody, single natural crowtail. No phoenixcrest/horns or extra wings.
Represents sun and called qi ofsun; actual blazingSOLARDISC behindbird lights redfeathers, bird emits no flame/energybeam.
Sky before the Sun, distant fusangtree silhouette lowerframe from suntransport tale, no humans.

three-legged-crow.aura: SWOOP straight toward lowviewer from before solar disc, spread bothwings, fan THREE legs into CLEAR separateleft/center/right positions with feetcurled naturally as it descends. Grounded in three-legged-crow-c01, three-legged-crow-c03, three-legged-crow-c05, three-legged-crow-c07, three-legged-crow-c13.

basis_claims.quote: The three-legged (or tripedal) crow is a mythological creature in various mythologies and arts of East Asia. It is believed to inhabit and represent the Sun.

statement.id: Gagak berkaki tiga adalah makhluk mitologis Asia Timur yang mewakili matahari.
statement.en: The three-legged crow is an East Asian mythological creature representing the sun.

basis_claims.quote: It is also mentioned in the Shanhaijing. The earliest known depiction of a three-legged crow appears in Neolithic pottery of the Yangshao culture.

statement.id: Shanhaijing memuat penyebutan gagak berkaki tiga.
statement.en: The Shanhaijing includes a reference to the three-legged crow.

basis_claims.quote: The most popular depiction and myth of a sanzuwu is of a sun crow called the Yangwu (陽烏), more commonly referred to as the Jinwu (金烏; 'golden crow') or "golden crow". Even though it is described as a corvid, it is usually coloured red instead of black.

statement.id: Gagak matahari sering diberi warna merah meski disebut gagak emas.
statement.en: The sun crow is often colored red despite the name golden crow.

basis_claims.quote: 《論衡》曰：儒者言：日中有三足烏。日，火也。烏入火中燋爛，安得立？然烏，日氣也。

statement.id: Taiping Yulan (太平御覽) mengutip Lunheng (論衡): kaum sarjana (儒者) mengatakan di dalam matahari ada burung gagak berkaki tiga (三足烏); matahari adalah api, dan gagak yang masuk ke dalam api akan hangus, tetapi gagak adalah "qi matahari" (日氣).
statement.en: The Taiping Yulan (太平御覽) quotes the Lunheng (論衡): the scholars (儒者) say there is a three-legged crow (三足烏) in the sun; the sun is fire and a crow entering fire would be scorched, yet the crow is the "qi of the sun" (日氣).

basis_claims.quote: 大荒之中，有山名曰孽搖頵羝，上有扶木，柱三百里，其葉如芥。有谷曰溫源谷。湯谷上有扶木。一日方至，一日方出，皆載于烏。

statement.id: Shanhaijing (山海經), Dahuang dong jing, menyebut di Tanggu (湯谷) ada pohon fusang (扶木); ketika satu matahari tiba, satu matahari lain keluar, dan semuanya dibawa oleh gagak (載于烏).
statement.en: The Shanhaijing (山海經), Dahuang dong jing, says that at Tanggu (湯谷) there is a fusang tree (扶木); as one sun arrives another goes out, and all are carried by crows (載于烏).

tinirau.depicted_variant: the Polynesian fishguardian with one sidehuman and the otherfish

visual_requirements.description: ONE upright deity with ONE head/TWO eyes, entire anatomical RIGHT SIDE human and LEFT SIDE fish: rightfacehalf human, leftfacehalf scaled fish/gill, rightbodyhalf fullyopaque cloth, leftbodyhalf smooth fishscales. ONE humanrightarm/hand and ONE leftpectoralFIN instead of leftarm; ONE humanrightleg and ONE long fishtail forms leftlowerhalf. No extra arms/wings or mermaid humanupper/fishlower arrangement.
Guardian/lord offish with breedingfishpreserves: livingfish gather in naturalpool, water displaced physically byfishside, no inventedcontrolbeam/aura.
Motutapu holyisland fishpreserve, darkbreedingpools beside rockyshore.

tinirau.aura: TURN towardlowviewer and EXTEND humanhand protectively over fishpool while fishside tail pushes up a physicalwaterwake, leftfin opens andschool of fish circles nearby. Grounded in tinirau-c01, tinirau-c02, tinirau-c08, tinirau-c04, tinirau-c06, tinirau-c05.

basis_claims.quote: In Polynesian mythology, stories about Tinirau are found throughout the islands of Polynesia. He is a guardian of fish.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Polinesia, kisah Tinirau tersebar luas dan ia adalah penjaga ikan.
statement.en: In Polynesian mythology, Tinirau is celebrated as a guardian of fish.

basis_claims.quote: In some traditions, he has a dual nature; one destructive as the guardian of sharks, and one a kind, handsome male youth; in others, his right side is human and his left side is a fish.

statement.id: Dalam beberapa tradisi ia memiliki watak ganda dan bertubuh separuh manusia separuh ikan.
statement.en: In some traditions he has a dual nature, with one side human and the other fish.

basis_claims.quote: the tutelary deity of fishes ; a son of Tangaroa, the Lord of Ocean.

statement.id: Menurut Tregear, Tinirau adalah dewa pelindung ikan dan putra Tangaroa, Penguasa Samudra.
statement.en: According to Tregear, Tinirau is the tutelary deity of fishes and a son of Tangaroa, the Lord of Ocean.

basis_claims.quote: Tinirau dwelt in Holy Island (Motutapu), and this account of his residence is agreed to by all Polynesians

statement.id: Menurut Tregear, Tinirau tinggal di Pulau Suci (Motutapu), dan keterangan tentang tempat tinggalnya ini disepakati oleh semua orang Polinesia.
statement.en: According to Tregear, Tinirau dwelt in Holy Island (Motutapu), an account of his residence agreed to by all Polynesians.

basis_claims.quote: The home of Tinirau was a preserve for fish, and surrounded with pools for breeding fish

statement.id: Menurut Tregear, rumah Tinirau adalah cagar ikan yang dikelilingi kolam pembiakan ikan.
statement.en: According to Tregear, the home of Tinirau was a preserve for fish, surrounded with pools for breeding fish.

basis_claims.quote: He was half a fish. Motu-tapu was given to him as his inheritance. He was lord of all fish.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi Mangaia dalam Tregear, Tinirau setengah ikan, mewarisi Motu-tapu, dan menjadi penguasa semua ikan.
statement.en: In the Mangaian tradition recorded by Tregear, Tinirau was half a fish, was given Motu-tapu as his inheritance and was lord of all fish.

tsurube-otoshi.depicted_variant: the gigantic disembodied humanhead falling from treetops

visual_requirements.description: ONE GIGANTIC HUMAN HEAD, TWO naturaleyes/ONE nose/mouth, NO body/arms/legs, NO visible wound or severedneck; smooth shadowunderchin hides base. Normalhumanteeth, no demonhorns. PhysicalFLAMES surround fallinghead.
Drops from trees like stone and can be flamewreathed: realorangeflames/embers fall alonghead, no genericghostlight/runes, no injuredvictims.
Kansai foresttreetops at latenight, trunks muchsmaller than gianthead.

statement.id: Jing adalah kategori roh gaib dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
statement.en: Jing is a category of supernatural spirit in Chinese tradition.

basis_claims.quote: 又萬物之老者，其精悉能假讬人形，以眩惑人目而常試人，唯不能於鏡中易其真形耳。

statement.id: Menurut Baopuzi, jing semua benda yang sudah tua dapat menyamar sebagai manusia untuk menyilaukan mata dan terus menguji orang, tetapi tidak dapat mengubah wujud aslinya di dalam cermin.
statement.en: According to the Baopuzi, the jing of all aged things can all assume human form to dazzle people's eyes and constantly test them, but cannot change their true form in a mirror.

basis_claims.quote: 若是鳥獸邪魅，則其形貌皆見鏡中矣。又老魅若來，其去必卻行，行可轉鏡對之，其後而視之，若是老魅者，必無踵也

statement.id: Menurut Baopuzi, jika yang datang adalah siluman burung atau hewan, wujudnya tampak di cermin; siluman tua yang datang juga pergi dengan berjalan mundur dan tidak punya tumit.
statement.en: According to the Baopuzi, if the visitor is a bird- or beast-spirit its form shows in the mirror; an old spirit that comes also leaves walking backwards and has no heels.

basis_claims.quote: 於是二人顧視鏡中，乃是鹿也。因問之曰：汝是山中老鹿，何敢詐為人形。言未絕，而來人即成鹿而走去。

statement.id: Dalam kisah Baopuzi tentang dua orang di sebuah gua batu, seorang pengunjung berpakaian seperti manusia tampak sebagai rusa di cermin; ketika ditegur sebagai rusa tua, ia berubah menjadi rusa dan lari.
statement.en: In a Baopuzi tale of two men in a stone chamber, a visitor dressed as a person appears as a deer in the mirror; when addressed as an old deer he turns into a deer and runs off.

statement.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, Chaofeng is a dragon offspring in Li Dongyang’s account in the Huailutang ji (懐麓堂集), depicted as a phoenix-like bird.

basis_claims.quote: 険しいところを好み、遠くを眺める事を好むともされることから、建物の屋根の軒に置かれる。

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, ia konon menyukai tempat terjal dan memandang jauh.
statement.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, it is said to favor steep places and distant views.

basis_claims.quote: 険しいところを好み、遠くを眺める事を好むともされることから、建物の屋根の軒に置かれる。

statement.id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, kegemaran itu menjelaskan penempatannya pada tepi atap bangunan.
statement.en: According to Japanese Wikipedia, this preference explains its placement on the eaves of roofs.

basis_claims.quote: 龍生九子，不成龍，各有所好。囚牛，好音樂，以飾胡琴。睚眦，好殺，以飾刀柄。嘲風，好險，在殿角。蒲牢，好鳴，取為鐘紐。狻猊，好座，取為佛座。霸下，好負重，為碑座。狴犴，好訟，為獄門。屓屭，好文，在碑兩傍。蚩吻，好吞，在殿脊。弘治間，泰陵令中官問龍生九子名目於李少師東陽，李不能悉，詢於吏部劉員外績，乃得其說，於故冊面上所錄，然亦不知所從出，因據以復。

statement.id: Dalam Shuo Lüe (說略, karya Gu Qiyuan, Ming), daftar sembilan putra naga yang "tidak menjadi naga, masing-masing punya kegemaran" memuat 嘲風 yang gemar bahaya (好險) dan berada di sudut istana (在殿角). Teksnya menambahkan bahwa pada masa Hongzhi (弘治) kaisar (泰陵) menyuruh seorang kasim menanyakan nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang (李東陽); Li tidak dapat menyebut semuanya, bertanya kepada Liu Ji (劉績), dan memperoleh keterangannya dari catatan lama yang asal-usulnya pun tidak diketahui.
statement.en: In the Shuo Lüe (說略, by Gu Qiyuan, Ming), the list of the dragon's nine sons that "did not become dragons, each with its own fondness" includes 嘲風, which likes danger (好險) and is at palace corners (在殿角). The text adds that in the Hongzhi (弘治) period the emperor (泰陵) had a eunuch ask Li Dongyang (李東陽) for the names of the nine sons; Li could not give them all, asked Liu Ji (劉績), and obtained the account from an old register whose origin was also unknown.

basis_claims.quote: 洵一作「旬」山，其陽多金，其陰多玉。有獸焉，其狀如羊而無口，不可殺也，〈稟氣自然〉其名曰䍺。

statement.id: Dalam Shan Hai Jing (南山經), di gunung 洵 ada hewan yang bentuknya seperti domba tetapi tanpa mulut dan tidak dapat dibunuh (catatan tafsir: 稟氣自然); namanya 䍺.
statement.en: In the Shan Hai Jing (南山經), on Xun mountain (洵) there is a beast shaped like a sheep but without a mouth, which cannot be killed (commentary: 稟氣自然); it is named 䍺.

basis_claims.quote: 患（羊患）是中國古代的傳說生物，於《山海经》有记载。 ... 《山海經·南山經》：「又東四百里，曰洵山，其陽多金，其陰多玉。有獸焉，其狀如羊而無口，不可殺也，其名曰䍺。」

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa menyebut 患 (羊患) sebagai makhluk legendaris Tiongkok kuno yang tercatat dalam Shan Hai Jing, dan mengutip kalimat 南山經 tentang hewan seperti domba tanpa mulut bernama 䍺.
statement.en: Chinese Wikipedia calls 患 (羊患) a legendary creature of ancient China recorded in the Shan Hai Jing, and quotes the 南山經 line about the sheep-like beast without a mouth named 䍺.

basis_claims.quote: It represents the west in terms of direction and the autumn season.

statement.id: Harimau Putih berhubungan dengan arah barat dan musim gugur.
statement.en: The White Tiger corresponds to west and autumn.

basis_claims.quote: 西方，金也，其帝少昊，其佐蓐收，執矩而治秋。其神為太白，其獸白虎，其音商，其日庚辛。

statement.id: Huainanzi bab Tianwen xun (天文訓) menyebut bahwa arah barat adalah logam (金), kaisarnya Shaohao (少昊), pembantunya Rushou (蓐收) yang memegang penyiku dan mengatur musim gugur (治秋); rohnya adalah Taibai (太白) dan binatangnya (獸) adalah Harimau Putih (白虎).
statement.en: The Huainanzi chapter Tianwen xun (天文訓) says the west is metal (金), its emperor is Shaohao (少昊) and its assistant Rushou (蓐收), who holds the square and governs autumn (治秋); its spirit is Taibai (太白) and its beast (獸) is the White Tiger (白虎).

statement.en: La Xtabay is a Yucatec Maya folklore tale about a demonic femme fatale who preys upon men in the Yucatan Peninsula.

basis_claims.quote: She is said to dwell in the forest to lure men to their deaths with her incomparable beauty.

statement.en: She is described as having beautiful, shining black hair that falls down to her ankles and wearing a white dress.

basis_claims.quote: Utz-colel prayed to evil spirits who fulfilled her desire to become a woman again so that she too might become a beautiful flower in death, but, incapable of love and motivated only by jealousy and rage, she became instead the demon Xtabay, outwardly a beautiful woman but inwardly cruel and predatory of heart.

statement.id: Utz-colel berdoa kepada roh jahat yang mengabulkan keinginannya menjadi perempuan lagi agar ia pun menjadi bunga yang indah setelah mati, tetapi karena tak mampu mencinta dan hanya digerakkan iri dan amarah, ia justru menjadi iblis Xtabay, tampak cantik di luar namun kejam dan buas di dalam hati.
statement.en: Utz-colel prayed to evil spirits, who granted her wish to become a woman again so she too might become a beautiful flower in death, but, incapable of love and driven only by jealousy and rage, she became instead the demon Xtabay, outwardly a beautiful woman but inwardly cruel and predatory.

basis_claims.quote: She waits behind a ceiba tree (a sacred tree in Maya culture) and is said to comb her hair with the spines of the Tzacam cactus.

statement.id: Ia menunggu di balik pohon ceiba (pohon suci dalam budaya Maya) dan konon menyisir rambutnya dengan duri kaktus Tzacam.
statement.en: She waits behind a ceiba tree (a sacred tree in Maya culture) and is said to comb her hair with the spines of the Tzacam cactus.

basis_claims.quote: There, she brushes her hair and waits for drunk, lost men, who find themselves stumbling through the night.

statement.id: Di sana ia menyisir rambutnya dan menunggu lelaki mabuk yang tersesat dan terhuyung-huyung di malam hari.
statement.en: There she brushes her hair and waits for drunk, lost men stumbling through the night.

basis_claims.quote: Many versions of the Nihon Shoki and the Kojiki state that after Izanagi saw his wife in such a state and fled in terror, Izanami sent the Yomotsu-shikome, 150 warriors, and the eight thunder kami after him.

statement.en: They pursue Izanagi when he flees the underworld.

basis_claims.quote: [Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami] (Kojiki) The "eight kinds of thunder kami" that festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by her consort Izanagi in the underworld of Yomi.

statement.id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Shinto, Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami dalam Kojiki adalah "delapan jenis kami petir" yang membusuk di dalam jasad Izanami, seperti dilihat suaminya Izanagi di dunia bawah Yomi.
statement.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, the Yakusa no ikazuchi no kami of the Kojiki are the "eight kinds of thunder kami" that festered inside Izanami's corpse as seen by her consort Izanagi in the underworld of Yomi.

basis_claims.quote: According to the various Kojiki and Nihongi accounts mentioned above, Izanami ordered the "hags of Yomi" and the eight thunder kami to chase Izanagi ... Izanagi, however, threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka (the "Even Pass of Yomi"), and thus dispersed his pursuers.

statement.id: Menurut berbagai catatan Kojiki dan Nihongi, Izanami memerintahkan "nenek-nenek Yomi" dan delapan kami petir mengejar Izanagi; Izanagi melempar buah persik gaib di Yomotsuhirasaka dan mengusir para pengejarnya.
statement.en: According to the various Kojiki and Nihongi accounts, Izanami ordered the "hags of Yomi" and the eight thunder kami to chase Izanagi; Izanagi threw down magical peaches at Yomotsuhirasaka and thus dispersed his pursuers.

basis_claims.quote: The animal is said to have a red shining mirror, like hot glowing coal, on its head, thought to be a precious stone.

statement.en: In the Chilote mythology of southern Chile the carbunclo is said to be the "guardian of the metals"; descriptions vary from a luminescent small dog, a luminescent bivalve or a cat with a luminescent tuft under its beard to a greenish-red fiery light reminiscent of fireflies.

basis_claims.quote: The carbunclo is said to manifest itself at night around the Southern Hemisphere winter solstice (late June).

statement.id: Konon carbunclo menampakkan diri pada malam hari sekitar titik balik matahari musim dingin belahan bumi selatan (akhir Juni).
statement.en: The carbunclo is said to manifest itself at night around the Southern Hemisphere winter solstice (late June).
