basis_claims.quote: The story holds that Sister Marie's head was never found, resulting in her spirit forever roaming the area in search of it.

statement.id: Menurut cerita, kepala Suster Marie tidak pernah ditemukan, sehingga rohnya terus berkeliaran di daerah itu untuk mencarinya.
statement.en: The story holds that Sister Marie's head was never found, so her spirit forever roams the area searching for it.

basis_claims.quote: one night, around 1758, after having helped a woman through a difficult childbirth, Sister Marie Inconnue was returning to the settlement at the cove — at the time home to a battery of 16 cannons and a small detachment of soldiers.
basis_claims.locator: The tale of the headless nun

statement.id: Menurut penuturan pemandu wisata, sekitar 1758, setelah menolong seorang perempuan melahirkan dengan sulit, Suster Marie Inconnue pulang ke permukiman di teluk kecil itu, yang saat itu memiliki baterai 16 meriam dan sepasukan kecil tentara.
statement.en: In the tour guide's telling, one night around 1758, after helping a woman through a difficult childbirth, Sister Marie Inconnue was returning to the settlement at the cove, then home to a battery of 16 cannons and a small detachment of soldiers.

basis_claims.quote: As she crossed the footbridge over Crow Brook, she was set upon. Some say it was a pair of leprous sailors from L'Indienne de Morlaix, out for revenge on those who had imprisoned them. Others insist that it was a mad trapper, wild and desperate from years living in the woods.
basis_claims.locator: The tale of the headless nun

statement.id: Ketika ia menyeberangi jembatan kecil di atas Crow Brook, ia diserang. Ada yang mengatakan pelakunya dua pelaut berkusta dari L'Indienne de Morlaix yang membalas dendam; yang lain berkeras pelakunya seorang penjerat liar yang putus asa setelah bertahun-tahun hidup di hutan.
statement.en: As she crossed the footbridge over Crow Brook she was attacked. Some say the attackers were a pair of leprous sailors from L'Indienne de Morlaix seeking revenge; others insist it was a mad trapper, wild and desperate from years in the woods.

basis_claims.quote: Her body was sent to France for burial, but her head was never recovered. Since that day, it is said that the ghost of Sister Marie still roams the cove, still diligently protecting the treasure — and searching for the head that will make her whole again.
basis_claims.locator: The tale of the headless nun

statement.id: Jasadnya dikirim ke Prancis untuk dimakamkan, tetapi kepalanya tak pernah ditemukan; sejak itu hantu Suster Marie konon masih berkeliaran di teluk kecil itu, menjaga harta karun dan mencari kepalanya.
statement.en: Her body was sent to France for burial but her head was never recovered; since then the ghost of Sister Marie is said to roam the cove, still guarding the treasure and searching for her head.

hiderigami.depicted_variant: Sekien variant of Hiderigami as a one-armed one-eyed drought beast

visual_requirements.description: One small beast with exactly ONE ARM and exactly ONE EYE, no second arm or hidden eye; squat hairy body, one centered face eye, two bent hind legs. The single long arm thrust to foreground; opposite shoulder smooth and armless. No horns or wings
Drought it brings expressed by entirely dry cracked soil and withered plants, no fire breath or heat beams
A drought-stricken dry landscape with no named geography invented

hiderigami.aura: Drought it brings expressed by entirely dry cracked soil and withered plants, no fire breath or heat beams [hiderigami-c01, hiderigami-c11]

basis_claims.quote: is a mythical species of yaoguai or yōkai in Chinese and Japanese folklore that holds the power to cause droughts.

statement.id: Hiderigami ("dewa kekeringan"), atau Hanba, adalah spesies mitos yaoguai atau yōkai dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok dan Jepang yang memiliki kekuatan menyebabkan kekeringan.
statement.en: Hiderigami ("god of drought"), or Hanba, is a mythical species of yaoguai or yōkai in Chinese and Japanese folklore that holds the power to cause droughts.

basis_claims.quote: In Toriyama Sekien's Illustrated One Hundred Demons from the Present and the Past, it is referred to as Hiderigami ... and is drawn as a beast with one arm and one eye.

statement.id: Dalam Illustrated One Hundred Demons from the Present and the Past karya Toriyama Sekien, ia disebut Hiderigami dan digambar sebagai makhluk buas berlengan satu dan bermata satu.
statement.en: In Toriyama Sekien's Illustrated One Hundred Demons from the Present and the Past it is called Hiderigami and drawn as a beast with one arm and one eye.

basis_claims.quote: 魃（ばつ、ひでりがみ）は、中国神話に登場する旱魃の神である。 特定の神の名ではなく、各地の山川に旱魃を起こす神がおり、それぞれにより姿も性質も異なる。

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Jepang menyebut 魃 sebagai dewa kekeringan dalam mitologi Tiongkok; itu bukan nama satu dewa tertentu, melainkan dewa-dewa penyebab kekeringan di gunung dan sungai berbagai tempat, yang masing-masing berbeda rupa dan sifatnya.
statement.en: Japanese Wikipedia calls 魃 a god of drought appearing in Chinese mythology; it is not the name of one specific god but of drought-causing gods in the mountains and rivers of various places, each differing in form and nature.

basis_claims.quote: 頭の上に目があり、風のように走り、これが現れると大旱魃になるが、厠に投げ込むと死んでしまうという。

statement.id: Disebutkan ia bermata di atas kepala dan berlari secepat angin; bila muncul terjadi kekeringan besar, tetapi bila dilemparkan ke dalam kakus ia mati.
statement.en: It is said to have eyes on top of its head and to run like the wind; when it appears a great drought occurs, but it dies if thrown into a privy.

hong-rainbow-dragon.depicted_variant: the early arched two-ended serpent depiction of Hong

visual_requirements.description: Exactly TWO smooth reptilian serpent heads, one at EACH OPPOSITE END of a SINGLE uninterrupted arched snake body, no tail beyond either head, no branches; each head twoeyes and open mouth. No legs, arms, wings, horns, antlers, whiskers or mane
The living rainbow dragon is an ill omen appearing after rainfall; subtle natural rainbow colors on scales from postrain light, not neon ribbons or power beams
Dark sky just after a rain shower

hong-rainbow-dragon.aura: The living rainbow dragon is an ill omen appearing after rainfall; subtle natural rainbow colors on scales from postrain light, not neon ribbons or power beams [hong-rainbow-dragon-c05]

basis_claims.quote: Hong or jiang (Chinese: 虹; pinyin: hóng or jiàng; Wade–Giles: hung or chiang; lit. 'rainbow') is a Chinese dragon with two heads on each end in Chinese mythology, comparable with Rainbow Serpent legends in various cultures and mythologies.

statement.id: Hong atau jiang adalah naga pelangi mitologi Tiongkok yang memiliki kepala pada kedua ujung tubuh.
statement.en: Hong, or jiang, is a Chinese mythological rainbow dragon with heads at both ends.

basis_claims.quote: However, the oldest characters for "rainbow" in Shang dynasty oracle bone script were pictographs of an arched dragon or serpent with open-mouthed heads at both ends.

statement.id: Aksara pelangi kuno zaman Shang berbentuk naga melengkung berkepala dua.
statement.en: Ancient Shang rainbow characters depict an arched two-headed dragon.

basis_claims.quote: Although many ancient cultures believed rainbows were good omens,"Carr explains, "the Chinese saw them as meteorological disasters. Unlike the auspicious [long] 龍 dragon symbolizing forthcoming rain, the two-headed [hong] 虹 was inauspicious because it appeared after a rain shower."

statement.id: Michael Carr, dikutip Wikipedia, menyatakan bahwa orang Tiongkok melihat pelangi sebagai bencana meteorologis; berbeda dengan naga long (龍) yang membawa hujan dan bertuah, hong (虹) yang berkepala dua dianggap tidak bertuah karena muncul setelah hujan.
statement.en: Carr, as quoted in Wikipedia, states that the Chinese saw rainbows as meteorological disasters; unlike the auspicious long (龍) dragon that symbolizes coming rain, the two-headed hong (虹) was inauspicious because it appeared after a rain shower.

basis_claims.quote: Eberhard notes, "In early reliefs, the rainbow is shown as a snake or a dragon with two heads. In West China they give it the head of a donkey, and it rates as a lucky symbol."

statement.id: Eberhard, dikutip Wikipedia, mencatat bahwa relief awal menggambarkan pelangi sebagai ular atau naga berkepala dua, dan di Tiongkok Barat diberi kepala keledai serta dianggap lambang keberuntungan.
statement.en: Eberhard, as quoted in Wikipedia, notes that early reliefs show the rainbow as a snake or two-headed dragon, and in West China it is given a donkey's head and counted a lucky symbol.

hudson-river-monster.depicted_variant: Alleged1886 hundred-foot sea serpent account; not2006 manatee and not claimed real species.

visual_requirements.description: Reported100-foot sea serpent with huge head
Rearing up to ten feet from river, physical splashes
Hudson River

hudson-river-monster.aura: Threat comes from the reported huge head and rearing serpent body (hudson-river-monster-c06).

basis_claims.quote: In New York folklore, the Hudson River Monster, popularly known as "Kipsy" or less commonly "Keepsie" or "Libby" (after the Statue of Liberty) is an aquatic serpentine monster reportedly spotted along the Hudson River and New York Harbor since 1886.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat New York, Hudson River Monster ("Kipsy", juga "Keepsie" atau "Libby") adalah monster air mirip ular yang dilaporkan terlihat di Sungai Hudson dan Pelabuhan New York sejak 1886.
statement.en: In New York folklore, the Hudson River Monster ("Kipsy", also "Keepsie" or "Libby") is a serpentine water monster reported along the Hudson River and New York Harbor since 1886.

basis_claims.quote: In 1886 dozens of people insisted they had seen a 100-foot-long sea serpent with a huge head in the Hudson River repeatedly rearing as high as ten feet in the air.

statement.id: Pada 1886, puluhan orang bersikeras telah melihat ular laut sepanjang 100 kaki berkepala besar di Sungai Hudson yang berulang kali menegak setinggi sepuluh kaki ke udara.
statement.en: In 1886, dozens of people insisted they had seen a 100-foot-long sea serpent with a huge head in the Hudson River, repeatedly rearing as high as ten feet in the air.

huoshu.depicted_variant: Shenyijing thousand-jin long white-haired mouse, not rat-sized Yan-island variant.

visual_requirements.description: Mouse with long fine white hair, thousand-jin weight in selected Shenyijing version
Dwells in fire/red while inside, white fur when outside
Fire Mountain/inexhaustible trees

huoshu.aura: Awe comes from the great white-haired mouse emerging unhurt from fire in inexhaustible trees (huoshu-c07, huoshu-c09).

basis_claims.quote: The huoshu is said to dwell inside fire within incombustible trees growing in mountains in southern China. Cloth woven from its hair is said to became clean when burnt, and is thus equated with the item known as huo huan bu (火浣布) or "fire-laundered cloth", which is thought in reality to have been a type of asbestos cloth.

statement.id: Hewan ini dipercaya tinggal dalam api pada pohon yang tidak terbakar.
statement.en: The animal is said to dwell in fire within trees that cannot burn.

basis_claims.quote: Within such fire dwells a mouse. It weighs 100 jin/ catties (var. 1000 catties)., and has hairs  2 chi long,, fine white hair, like silk.

statement.id: Shenyi Jing menggambarkan tikus dalam api dengan rambut putih halus seperti sutra.
statement.en: The Shenyi Jing describes a fire-dwelling mouse with fine white hair like silk.

basis_claims.quote: 不尽木火中有鼠，重千斤，毛長二尺餘，細如絲。但居火中，洞赤，時時出外，而毛白，以水逐而沃之，即死。

statement.id: Teks Shenyijing menyebut bahwa dalam api pada pohon yang tak habis terbakar ada seekor tikus seberat seribu jin dengan bulu panjang lebih dari dua chi sehalus sutra; ia tinggal di dalam api, tampak merah menyala, kadang keluar dengan bulu putih, dan mati bila diusir dan disiram air.
statement.en: The Shenyijing text says that in the fire among inexhaustible trees there is a mouse weighing a thousand jin with hair over two chi long, fine as silk; it dwells in the fire, glowing red, sometimes comes out with white hair, and dies if chased and drenched with water.

basis_claims.quote: 南荒之外有火山，長四十里，廣五十里。其中皆生不烬之木，火鼠生其中。

statement.id: Teks Shenyijing menyebut bahwa di luar wilayah liar selatan ada gunung api sepanjang empat puluh li dan selebar lima puluh li, tempat tumbuh pohon-pohon yang tak habis terbakar, dan tikus api (火鼠) hidup di dalamnya.
statement.en: The Shenyijing text says beyond the southern wilds there is a fire mountain forty li long and fifty li wide where inexhaustible trees grow, and the fire rat (火鼠) is born within.

jackalope.depicted_variant: Living jackrabbit with antelope horns, not taxidermy deer-antler variant or Persian unicorn rabbit.

visual_requirements.description: Jackrabbit with antelope horns
Danger of goring expressed in low charge
Old West campfire setting

jackalope.aura: Danger comes from horn-first motion and source goring warning (jackalope-c05, jackalope-c14).

basis_claims.quote: The jackalope is a mythical animal of North American folklore described as a jackrabbit with antelope horns.

statement.id: Jackalope adalah hewan mitos dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Utara yang digambarkan sebagai jackrabbit bertanduk antelop.
statement.en: The jackalope is a mythical animal of North American folklore described as a jackrabbit with antelope horns.

basis_claims.quote: Jackalopes are said to be so dangerous that hunters are advised to wear stovepipes on their legs to keep from being gored.

statement.id: Jackalope dikatakan begitu berbahaya sehingga pemburu dianjurkan memakai pipa cerobong di kaki agar tidak ditanduk.
statement.en: Jackalopes are said to be so dangerous that hunters are advised to wear stovepipes on their legs to keep from being gored.

basis_claims.quote: The jackalope can imitate the human voice, according to legend. During the days of the Old West, when cowboys gathered by the campfires singing at night, jackalopes could be heard mimicking their voices or singing along, usually as a tenor.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, jackalope dapat menirukan suara manusia. Pada masa Wild West, ketika koboi berkumpul di api unggun dan bernyanyi di malam hari, jackalope terdengar menirukan suara mereka atau ikut bernyanyi, biasanya sebagai tenor.
statement.en: According to legend the jackalope can imitate the human voice; in the Old West, when cowboys sang around campfires at night, jackalopes could be heard mimicking them or singing along, usually as a tenor.

jiaotu.depicted_variant: Frog-like living guardian and door-ring account, not mixed with primary-text snail form.

visual_requirements.description: Selected frog-like form, mouth holding door ring
Closed door ring association/aversion to strangers

jiaotu.aura: Awe comes from the unusual live frog-like door-ring guardian confronting an entrant (jiaotu-c02, jiaotu-c03, jiaotu-c04).

basis_claims.quote: 椒図（椒圖、しょうず）は、竜生九子の一つ。姿は蛙にも、タニシやサザエのような巻貝やカラス貝にも似ている。

statement.id: Sumber berbahasa Jepang membandingkan wujudnya dengan katak dan hewan bercangkang.
statement.en: The Japanese-language source compares its forms with frogs and shelled creatures.

basis_claims.quote: 閉じることを好み、他所者が巣穴に入ることを嫌う。故に、門扉の握り輪を咥えているという。

statement.id: Konon ia menyukai tempat tertutup dan menolak orang asing masuk ke tempat tinggalnya.
statement.en: It is said to favor closed places and resist strangers entering its home.

basis_claims.quote: 閉じることを好み、他所者が巣穴に入ることを嫌う。故に、門扉の握り輪を咥えているという。

statement.id: Gambarnya dikaitkan dengan cincin pegangan pada pintu.
statement.en: Its image is associated with a ring held on a door.

joint-snake.depicted_variant: Legendary self-reassembling snake, not a claim that actual glass lizards can rejoin.

visual_requirements.description: Legendary snake, hard smooth stiff skin
Breaks in short clean bloodless segments/reassembles
SouthernUnitedStates, unspecified ground

joint-snake.aura: Threat comes from bloodless pieces actively drawing into a snake behind its poised head (joint-snake-c02, joint-snake-c05).

basis_claims.quote: A joint snake is a legendary creature of the Southern United States, the myth likely having spread elsewhere.

statement.id: Ular sambung adalah makhluk legendaris dari wilayah Amerika Serikat bagian selatan.
statement.en: A joint snake is a legendary creature of the Southern United States.

basis_claims.quote: Supposedly, the joint snake can break itself (or be cut) into pieces and will reassemble itself.

statement.id: Konon ular sambung dapat memutuskan tubuhnya menjadi beberapa bagian lalu menyambungkannya kembali.
statement.en: The snake can supposedly break itself into pieces and reassemble itself.

basis_claims.quote: According to travelers' accounts, their skin is as hard as parchment and as smooth as glass. It is so stiff that it can hardly bend itself. When it is struck it breaks, and you may, with a whip, break it from the tail to the bowels into pieces not an inch long, and not produce the least tincture of blood.

statement.id: Menurut catatan para pelancong, kulitnya sekeras perkamen dan selicin kaca, dan begitu kaku sehingga hampir tak dapat menekuk. Jika dipukul ia pecah; dengan cambuk orang dapat memecahnya dari ekor sampai usus menjadi potongan yang panjangnya kurang dari satu inci, tanpa setetes darah pun.
statement.en: According to travelers' accounts, its skin is as hard as parchment and as smooth as glass, and so stiff that it can hardly bend. When struck it breaks; with a whip it can be broken from tail to bowels into pieces less than an inch long, without the least trace of blood.

kanbari-nyudo.depicted_variant: Sekien monk-like bird-expelling depiction, not severed-head or fox anecdote.

visual_requirements.description: Monk-like figure, bird expelled from mouth
Physical bird exit from mouth
Toilet at year end

kanbari-nyudo.aura: Uncanny threat comes from the monk-like yokai expelling a live bird from his mouth (kanbari-nyudo-c02).

basis_claims.quote: 加牟波理入道（がんばりにゅうどう）は、鳥山石燕の妖怪画集『今昔画図続百鬼』にある日本の妖怪、および日本各地の厠（便所）の俗信に見られる妖怪。

statement.id: Kanbari-nyūdō adalah yōkai yang dikaitkan dengan toilet.
statement.en: Kanbari-nyūdō is a yōkai associated with toilets.

basis_claims.quote: 『今昔画図続百鬼』では、厠に現れる妖怪として口から鳥を吐く入道姿で描かれ、解説文には以下のようにあり、大晦日に「がんばり入道郭公（がんばりにゅうどうほととぎす）」と唱えると、この妖怪が現れないと述べられている。

statement.id: Sekien menggambarkan sosok seperti biksu yang mengeluarkan burung dari mulut.
statement.en: Sekien depicts a monk-like figure expelling a bird from its mouth.

basis_claims.quote: 日本の妖怪。年の暮れに厠に現れるとされ、全国に伝わる。「加牟波理入道ホトトギス」と唱えれば妖怪にあわずにすむという説と、逆に災厄をもたらすという説がある。
basis_claims.locator: 加牟波理(がんばり)入道

statement.id: Kamus Daijisen Plus mencatatnya sebagai yōkai Jepang yang dikatakan muncul di toilet pada akhir tahun dan dikenal di seluruh negeri; ada pendapat bahwa mantra "Kanbari nyūdō hototogisu" membuat orang tidak bertemu dengannya, dan pendapat sebaliknya bahwa mantra itu mendatangkan malapetaka.
statement.en: The Daijisen Plus dictionary records it as a Japanese yōkai said to appear in toilets at year's end and known across the country; one view holds that chanting "Kanbari nyūdō hototogisu" lets one avoid it, while another holds that it brings disaster.

kao-bull.depicted_variant: Untamed great divine bull at Waithou, before the father-name taming.

visual_requirements.description: Divine great bull and natural horns
Waithou waters and reeds

kao-bull.aura: Awe comes from the great horned bull forcefully emerging at Waithou (kao-bull-c13, kao-bull-c15).

basis_claims.quote: Kao (Meitei pronunciation: /káo/) is a legendary divine bull captured by Khuman Khamba in Meitei mythology and folklore of ancient Moirang realm.

statement.id: Kao adalah banteng ilahi dalam mitologi Meitei yang ditangkap Khuman Khamba.
statement.en: Kao is a divine bull in Meitei mythology captured by Khuman Khamba.

basis_claims.quote: There is a great bull that lurks among the reeds that border the waters of Waithou, and already he has killed a man. So we dare not fish there.

statement.id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, para perempuan Khumal berkata bahwa seekor banteng besar mengintai di antara alang-alang di tepi perairan Waithou dan sudah membunuh seorang laki-laki, sehingga mereka tidak berani memancing di sana.
statement.en: In this summary of the epic, the Khumal women say that a great bull lurks among the reeds bordering the waters of Waithou and has already killed a man, so they dare not fish there.

basis_claims.quote: Then he stood on firm ground and caught the bull by the horns, and they swayed together as they strove for the mastery. Then Khamba rested on the neck of the bull, who carried him into the jungle.

statement.id: Dalam ringkasan epos ini, Khamba berdiri di tanah kokoh dan menangkap banteng pada tanduknya; mereka saling mendorong memperebutkan kekuasaan, lalu Khamba bertumpu di leher banteng yang membawanya ke dalam hutan.
statement.en: In this summary of the epic, Khamba stood on firm ground and caught the bull by the horns, they swayed together striving for mastery, and then Khamba rested on the bull's neck as it carried him into the jungle.

kerakera-onna.depicted_variant: Giant kimono-clad middle-aged laughing woman; not a severed head.

visual_requirements.description: Giant middle-aged woman in kimono
Laughing over wall, frightening cackle
Wall on lonely alley

kerakera-onna.aura: Threat comes from enormous laughing woman looming over small wall and alley (kerakera-onna-c03, kerakera-onna-c04, kerakera-onna-c07).

basis_claims.quote: 着物姿の巨大な女性が、塀越しに口をひらいて笑う姿が描かれており、石燕による解説文は以下の通り添えられている。

statement.id: Ilustrasi itu menampilkan perempuan raksasa berkimono.
statement.en: The image shows a giant woman in a kimono.

basis_claims.quote: 着物姿の巨大な女性が、塀越しに口をひらいて笑う姿が描かれており、石燕による解説文は以下の通り添えられている。

statement.id: Ia tampak tertawa dari balik dinding.
statement.en: She is drawn laughing over a wall.

basis_claims.quote: 『今昔百鬼拾遺』には詳細な特徴などは述べられていないが、昭和・平成以降の妖怪関連の文献では、人通りのない道を歩いている者に笑いかけて脅かす者で、笑い声によって人の不安をかきたてるもの、また笑い声はその1人だけにしか聞こえず、気が弱い人は笑い声を聞いただけで気を失ってしまうという解説がなされている。

statement.id: Konkon Hyakki Shūi tidak memerinci ciri-cirinya, tetapi pustaka yōkai sejak era Shōwa dan Heisei menjelaskan bahwa ia menakuti orang yang berjalan di jalan sepi dengan tawa; tawa itu hanya terdengar oleh satu orang dan orang berhati lemah pingsan mendengarnya.
statement.en: The Konjaku Hyakki Shūi gives no detailed features, but yōkai literature from the Shōwa and Heisei eras explains that it frightens people on deserted roads with its laughter, which only that one person can hear, and the faint-hearted faint on hearing it.

basis_claims.quote: 民俗学者・藤沢衛彦の著書『妖怪画談全集 日本篇』（1929年）では「見上ぐれば垣より高く大面相の醜女現はれてげらげらげらと笑ふ」と解説されており、しばしば巨大な女性の妖怪と解説されていることがある。

statement.id: Folklorist Fujisawa Morihiko dalam Yōkai Gadan Zenshū Nihon-hen (1929) menjelaskannya sebagai perempuan buruk rupa bermuka besar yang tampak lebih tinggi dari pagar dan tertawa; karena itu ia sering dijelaskan sebagai yōkai perempuan raksasa.
statement.en: The folklorist Fujisawa Morihiko, in Yōkai Gadan Zenshū Nihon-hen (1929), describes a big-faced ugly woman appearing taller than the fence and laughing; hence it is often explained as a giant female yōkai.

basis_claims.quote: 日本の妖怪。巨大な中年女の姿で、塀越しにけらけらと笑うとされる。江戸時代の画家、鳥山石燕(せきえん)の画集「今昔百鬼拾遺」などに記述がある。
basis_claims.locator: デジタル大辞泉プラス「倩兮女」

statement.id: Kamus menggambarkannya sebagai yōkai berwujud perempuan paruh baya raksasa yang tertawa kerakera dari balik pagar, dengan catatan dalam kumpulan gambar Toriyama Sekien, Konjaku Hyakki Shūi, antara lain.
statement.en: The dictionary describes a yōkai in the form of a giant middle-aged woman who is said to laugh "kerakera" over a wall, recorded in works such as Edo-period painter Toriyama Sekien's Konjaku Hyakki Shūi.

basis_claims.quote: When a man passes a lonely street or alley haunted by a kerakera onna, she unleashes a horrible, shrill cackle that can only be heard by him.

statement.id: Menurut Yokai.com, ketika seorang lelaki melewati jalan atau lorong sepi yang dihantui kerakera onna, ia melepaskan tawa melengking mengerikan yang hanya terdengar olehnya.
statement.en: According to Yokai.com, when a man passes a lonely street or alley haunted by a kerakera onna, she unleashes a horrible shrill cackle that only he can hear.

kinie-ger.depicted_variant: Quoll-headed/quoll-bodied hunter with human limbs before owl/crow ambush.

visual_requirements.description: Quoll head/body, human limbs
Waterhole

kinie-ger.aura: Threat comes from ruthless human-limbed quoll beast confronting at waterhole (kinie-ger-c01, kinie-ger-c02, kinie-ger-c03).

basis_claims.quote: In the traditional stories of Southeastern Australia, Kinie Ger is an evil half-man, half-quoll beast that hunts and kills the innocent with his spear, until he is himself killed in an ambush.

statement.id: Dalam kisah tradisional Southeastern Australia, Kinie Ger adalah binatang buas separuh manusia separuh quoll yang berburu memakai tombak.
statement.en: In traditional stories of Southeastern Australia, Kinie Ger is an evil half-man, half-quoll beast.

basis_claims.quote: It was a ruthless killer with the head and body of a quoll but the limbs of a man.

statement.id: Ia berkepala dan bertubuh quoll tetapi memiliki anggota badan manusia.
statement.en: It had the head and body of a quoll but the limbs of a man.

basis_claims.quote: In the myth, the creature was stated to have been killed by the owl and the crow who ambushed him when he came to drink at a water hole.

statement.id: Makhluk ini dibunuh oleh burung hantu dan burung gagak yang menyergapnya di sumber air.
statement.en: The creature was killed by the owl and the crow who ambushed him at a water hole.

klu.depicted_variant: Ladakh human-torso serpent-tail naga form, not Bon animal-headed composites.

visual_requirements.description: Ladakh naga: human torso with serpent tail
Controls water
Natural spring affinity in Ladakh

klu.aura: Awe comes from documented naga hybrid rising in its physically moving spring water (klu-c05, klu-c06, klu-c08).

basis_claims.quote: These spirits, known locally as lu (klu in Tibetan and Ladakhi)—commonly translated as naga (semi-divine hybrid beings from Indian Mythology who have human torsos with serpent tails), remind us of their contribution to Buddhist practice and role in navigating human relationships with the environment.

statement.id: Roh air yang dikenal di Ladakh sebagai lu (klu dalam bahasa Tibet dan Ladakh) umumnya diterjemahkan sebagai naga; esai ini menggambarkan naga sebagai makhluk hibrida semi-ilahi dari mitologi India dengan batang tubuh manusia dan ekor ular.
statement.en: Water spirits known in Ladakh as lu (klu in Tibetan and Ladakhi) are commonly translated as naga, which the essay describes as semi-divine hybrid beings of Indian mythology with human torsos and serpent tails.

basis_claims.quote: In Ladakh, nagas are temperamental shape-shifting water spirits known as lu, who inhabit various corners of the natural world and can bestow great wealth. From streams and soil to trees and stones, lu are well-known for their abilities to both control water and wreck misfortune when perturbed.

statement.id: Di Ladakh, naga dipandang sebagai roh air pengubah wujud yang mudah tersinggung, disebut lu; mereka mendiami berbagai sudut alam dan dapat memberi kekayaan besar. Dari aliran air dan tanah hingga pohon dan batu, lu terkenal mampu mengendalikan air sekaligus mendatangkan kemalangan bila diusik.
statement.en: In Ladakh, nagas are described as temperamental shape-shifting water spirits called lu, who inhabit various corners of the natural world and can bestow great wealth. From streams and soil to trees and stones, lu are well known for being able both to control water and to bring misfortune when disturbed.

basis_claims.quote: lu are known for their affinity for natural springs and contaminating a spring, even washing one’s hands in the spring, will disrupt the lu and can result in bodily afflictions, such as skin maladies, gastrointestinal discomfort, and joint pain. An unhappy lu can bring illness, hardship, and unending tragedy to an individual, family, or community.

statement.id: Lu dikenal lekat dengan mata air alami; mencemari mata air, bahkan mencuci tangan di sana, dikatakan mengganggu lu dan dapat menimbulkan penyakit kulit, gangguan pencernaan, dan nyeri sendi. Lu yang tidak senang dapat mendatangkan penyakit, kesulitan, dan tragedi tak berkesudahan bagi seseorang, keluarga, atau komunitas.
statement.en: Lu are known for their affinity for natural springs; contaminating a spring, even washing hands in it, is said to disturb the lu and can bring skin ailments, stomach trouble and joint pain. An unhappy lu can bring illness, hardship and unending tragedy to an individual, family or community.

basis_claims.quote: Nagas control water, inhabit aquatic domains, and navigate between realms. In Ladakh, maintaining good relationships with the lu (nagas) is essential for sustaining balance and harmonious in the environment.

statement.id: Naga dikatakan mengendalikan air, mendiami ranah perairan, dan berpindah antar-alam; di Ladakh, menjaga hubungan baik dengan lu dinilai penting untuk menjaga keseimbangan dan keharmonisan lingkungan.
statement.en: Nagas are said to control water, inhabit aquatic domains and move between realms; in Ladakh, keeping good relations with the lu is regarded as essential to sustaining balance and harmony in the environment.

kui-chinese-mythology.depicted_variant: Shanhaijing hornless blue-green one-footed ox form; no musician, red drum or human-faced ape mixture.

visual_requirements.description: Blue-green oxlike body, NOhorns, exactly one foot
Water emergence causes wind/rain; glare like sun/moon, voice like thunder
Liubo mountain East Sea

kui-chinese-mythology.aura: Awe comes from single-footed hornless blue-green ox and emergence bringing wind/rain plus sun/moonlike glare (kui-chinese-mythology-c05, kui-chinese-mythology-c06).

basis_claims.quote: 東海中有流波山，入海七千里。其上有獸，狀如牛，蒼身而無角，一足，出入水則必風雨，其光如日月，其聲如雷，其名曰夔。

statement.id: Teks ini menyebut bahwa di gunung bernama Liubo (流波山) di tengah Laut Timur ada seekor binatang bernama Kui, berbentuk seperti lembu, bertubuh biru kehijauan, tanpa tanduk, dan berkaki satu.
statement.en: The text says that on the mountain called Liubo (流波山) in the East Sea there is a beast named Kui, shaped like an ox, with a blue-green body, no horns, and one foot.

basis_claims.quote: 其上有獸，狀如牛，蒼身而無角，一足，出入水則必風雨，其光如日月，其聲如雷，其名曰夔。

statement.id: Teks ini menyatakan bahwa setiap kali binatang itu keluar masuk air pasti ada angin dan hujan, sinarnya seperti matahari dan bulan, dan suaranya seperti guntur.
statement.en: The text states that whenever the beast goes into or out of the water there is wind and rain, its glare is like the sun and moon, and its voice is like thunder.

langben-rese.depicted_variant: Living intact giant before duel, not the subsequent headless run.

visual_requirements.description: Nordic giant, intact before duel
Skottfjället near Brattön Bohuslän

langben-rese.aura: Threat comes from a giant striding down into a confrontational duel moment (langben-rese-c01, langben-rese-c03).

basis_claims.quote: Långben Rese är en mytologisk jätte i nordiska folkvisor.

statement.id: Långben Rese adalah raksasa mitologis (mytologisk jätte) dalam lagu rakyat Nordik (nordiska folkvisor).
statement.en: Långben Rese is a mythological giant (mytologisk jätte) in Nordic folk ballads (nordiska folkvisor).

basis_claims.quote: Enligt traditionen skall han ha hållit till i Skottfjället nära Brattön i Bro socken i Bohuslän.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi (traditionen), ia tinggal di Skottfjället dekat Brattön di paroki (socken) Bro, Bohuslän.
statement.en: According to tradition (traditionen) he lived at Skottfjället near Brattön in Bro parish (socken), Bohuslän.

basis_claims.quote: Han är mest känd för sin tvekamp med den danska sagohjälten Vidrik Verlandsson, som resulterade till att Vidrik segrar och hugger huvudet av jätten.

statement.id: Ia terkenal karena duelnya (tvekamp) dengan pahlawan Denmark (danska sagohjälten) Vidrik Verlandsson, yang menang dan memenggal kepala (huvudet) sang raksasa (jätten).
statement.en: He is best known for his duel (tvekamp) with the Danish saga hero (danska sagohjälten) Vidrik Verlandsson, who won and cut off the giant's (jätten) head (huvudet).

luduan.depicted_variant: Composite lion/rhino/dragon/bear/fish/ox form from c01/c02; not conflated with Jiaoduan one-horned green deer.

visual_requirements.description: Lionhead/rhinohorn
Dragonbody, bear paws, fishscales, oxtail
Rapid travel
Imperial auspicious throne association

luduan.aura: Awe comes from unmistakable composite anatomy and very swift movement (luduan-c01, luduan-c02, luduan-c03).

basis_claims.quote: Luduan (甪端 pinyin: lùduān) is a legendary Chinese auspicious creature. It has the head of a lion, the horn of a rhino, the body of a dragon, the paws of a bear, the scales of a fish, and the tail of an ox, It can travel 18,000 li (9000 km or 5500 mi) in a single day and speaks all world languages. It appears during the reign of enlightened rulers.

statement.id: Luduan adalah makhluk bertuah legenda Tiongkok dengan kepala singa dan tanduk badak.
statement.en: Luduan is an auspicious Chinese legendary creature with a lion head and rhino horn.

basis_claims.quote: Luduan (甪端 pinyin: lùduān) is a legendary Chinese auspicious creature. It has the head of a lion, the horn of a rhino, the body of a dragon, the paws of a bear, the scales of a fish, and the tail of an ox, It can travel 18,000 li (9000 km or 5500 mi) in a single day and speaks all world languages. It appears during the reign of enlightened rulers.

statement.id: Tubuhnya menggabungkan tubuh naga, telapak beruang, sisik ikan, dan ekor sapi.
statement.en: Its anatomy combines a dragon body, bear paws, fish scales, and an ox tail.

basis_claims.quote: Luduan (甪端 pinyin: lùduān) is a legendary Chinese auspicious creature. It has the head of a lion, the horn of a rhino, the body of a dragon, the paws of a bear, the scales of a fish, and the tail of an ox, It can travel 18,000 li (9000 km or 5500 mi) in a single day and speaks all world languages. It appears during the reign of enlightened rulers.

statement.id: Luduan dipercaya dapat menempuh 18.000 li sehari dan berbicara dalam semua bahasa.
statement.en: Luduan is credited with traveling 18,000 li in a day and speaking every language.

basis_claims.quote: Luduan (甪端 pinyin: lùduān) is a legendary Chinese auspicious creature. It has the head of a lion, the horn of a rhino, the body of a dragon, the paws of a bear, the scales of a fish, and the tail of an ox, It can travel 18,000 li (9000 km or 5500 mi) in a single day and speaks all world languages. It appears during the reign of enlightened rulers.

statement.id: Kemunculannya dikaitkan dengan pemerintahan penguasa yang tercerahkan.
statement.en: Its appearance is associated with enlightened rulers.

basis_claims.quote: The throne of the Emperor in the Hall of Supreme Harmony has two incense burners shaped like the luduan as an auspicious symbol.

statement.id: Singgasana Kaisar di Aula Keharmonisan Tertinggi memiliki dua pedupaan berbentuk luduan sebagai lambang keberuntungan.
statement.en: The Emperor's throne in the Hall of Supreme Harmony has two incense burners shaped like the luduan as an auspicious symbol.

maushop.depicted_variant: Benevolent Aquinnah giant making ocean stepping stones, no whale-killing episode or demonic redesign.

visual_requirements.description: Benevolent giant human hero
Places thrown boulders in ocean as steppingstones
AquinnahCliffs/Ocean/MarthaVineyard

maushop.aura: Reverent awe comes from benevolent giant forming ocean stepping stones with boulders (maushop-c04, maushop-c08).

basis_claims.quote: Maushop or Moshup ... is a mythical hero and giant from Wampanoag folklore.

statement.id: Maushop atau Moshup adalah pahlawan mitos dan raksasa dalam cerita rakyat Wampanoag.
statement.en: Maushop or Moshup is a mythical hero and giant from Wampanoag folklore.

basis_claims.quote: According to legend, he came from Aquinnah on Martha's Vineyard and lived there from before the Wampanoag.

statement.id: Menurut legenda, ia berasal dari Aquinnah di Martha's Vineyard dan tinggal di sana sejak sebelum orang Wampanoag.
statement.en: According to legend, he came from Aquinnah on Martha's Vineyard and lived there from before the Wampanoag.

basis_claims.quote: Maushop was so large that his diet consisted mainly of whales. To catch them, he threw boulders into the water to make stepping stones. During a celebration, he emptied his pipe ashes into the ocean, and they became Nantucket.

statement.id: Maushop begitu besar sehingga makanannya sebagian besar paus; untuk menangkapnya ia melempar batu besar ke air sebagai pijakan, dan abu pipanya yang ia buang ke laut saat perayaan menjadi Nantucket.
statement.en: Maushop was so large that his diet consisted mainly of whales; to catch them he threw boulders into the water as stepping stones, and the ashes he emptied from his pipe into the ocean at a celebration became Nantucket.

basis_claims.quote: Moshup is believed by our tribe to be responsible for the present shapes of Martha's Vineyard, the Elizabeth Islands, Noman's Land, and Nantucket. He is a benevolent being of gigantic frame and supernatural power. He was sometimes thought of as the devil by those who did not understand him.

statement.id: Suku Wampanoag Aquinnah percaya Moshup bertanggung jawab atas bentuk Martha's Vineyard, Kepulauan Elizabeth, Noman's Land, dan Nantucket; ia makhluk baik hati bertubuh raksasa dan berkekuatan gaib, yang kadang dianggap iblis oleh orang yang tidak memahaminya.
statement.en: The tribe believes Moshup is responsible for the present shapes of Martha's Vineyard, the Elizabeth Islands, Noman's Land and Nantucket; he is a benevolent being of gigantic frame and supernatural power, sometimes thought of as the devil by those who did not understand him.

basis_claims.quote: From near the entrance to his den on the Aquinnah Cliffs, Moshup would wade into the ocean, pick up a whale, fling it against the Cliffs to kill it, and then cook it over the fire that burned continually.

statement.id: Dari dekat pintu sarangnya di Tebing Aquinnah, Moshup berjalan ke laut, mengangkat seekor paus, membantingnya ke tebing hingga mati, lalu memasaknya di atas api yang tak pernah padam.
statement.en: From near the entrance to his den on the Aquinnah Cliffs, Moshup would wade into the ocean, pick up a whale, fling it against the Cliffs to kill it and cook it over the fire that burned continually.

basis_claims.quote: Moshup was the first schoolmaster. From his home on the Cliffs he taught the people respect

statement.id: Seorang anggota suku, yang dikutip situs resmi suku, mengatakan bahwa Moshup adalah guru sekolah pertama yang dari rumahnya di tebing mengajarkan rasa hormat kepada orang-orang.
statement.en: A tribal member quoted on the tribe's official site says Moshup was the first schoolmaster, who from his home on the Cliffs taught the people respect.

mikoshi-nyudo.depicted_variant: Late-Edo long thin neck and three-eyed face variant, without iron-rod details from another depiction.

visual_requirements.description: One bald monk-like humanoid head with EXACTLY THREE clearly separated open eyes, two ordinary eyes and one forehead eye; a very long thin extending neck, two arms and two legs in fully opaque worn robes. No iron rod, horns or fangs.
Its documented neck extension and growth make the robed torso far below the looming head, with the neck visibly stretching upward; no other powers or glow.
A night hill road.

mikoshi-nyudo.aura: Bend the long thin neck downward while growing upward over the viewer, all three eyes confronting camera. Visual grounding: mikoshi-nyudo-c01, mikoshi-nyudo-c10, mikoshi-nyudo-c03.

basis_claims.quote: Mikoshi-nyūdō (見越し入道 or 見越入道) is a type of bald-headed yōkai "goblin" with an ever-extending neck.

statement.id: Mikoshi-nyūdō adalah yōkai botak mirip biksu dengan leher yang memanjang.
statement.en: Mikoshi-nyūdō is a long-necked yōkai resembling a bald monk.

basis_claims.quote: When walking to the end of a road at night or a hill road, something the shape of a monk would suddenly appear, and if one looks up, it becomes taller the further one looks up.

statement.id: Beberapa cerita menempatkan kemunculannya mendadak di jalan malam.
statement.en: Some accounts place its sudden appearance on roads at night.

basis_claims.quote: The length of its neck has been exaggerated over the passage of eras, and in the late Edo period, it has become standard for its neck to be long and thin, and for its face to have three eyes.

statement.id: Panjang lehernya dilebih-lebihkan dari zaman ke zaman; pada akhir zaman Edo menjadi baku bahwa lehernya panjang dan kurus serta wajahnya bermata tiga.
statement.en: The length of its neck was exaggerated over the eras, and by the late Edo period it became standard for the neck to be long and thin and the face to have three eyes.

mino-waraji.depicted_variant: Sekien straw-raincoat body, two sandal legs and carried hoe; no sandal-face or horse-headed-staff variant.

visual_requirements.description: An upright STRAW RAINCOAT is the entire body, exactly TWO straw sandals are its legs/feet, and it carries one wooden-handled iron hoe across its shoulder. No human body inside, no human face, no added eyeballs or straw-sandal head; flexible straw bundles support the hoe.
No documented active magical effect; snow is kicked up by the two moving sandals and straw sways physically.
Snow-covered bamboo grove, as in the source depiction.

mino-waraji.aura: Stride out of snowy bamboo toward the viewer, the empty straw body twisting forward and the hoe shifting diagonally across the frame. Visual grounding: mino-waraji-c02.

basis_claims.quote: 雪のつもっている竹林の中を蓑（みの）が胴体、草鞋（わらじ）が両脚となり、鍬（くわ）をかついだ姿で描かれている。

statement.id: Tubuhnya berupa jas hujan jerami, kakinya sandal, dan ia membawa cangkul.
statement.en: Its body is a straw raincoat, its legs are sandals and it carries a hoe.

mintuci.depicted_variant: Reddish turtle-textured, bird-footed aquatic variant; no borrowed kappa anatomy.

visual_requirements.description: One half-human half-beast figure at human-child stature, one head with two ordinary eyes, two arms and two bird-footed legs; reddish skin with sea-turtle-like texture. Fully opaque simple wrapped clothing covers torso and intimate anatomy. No shell, beak, head water-dish, hoof sets or extra limbs.
Physical river water streams off the emerging body; no invented beams, controlled storm or magic aura. The threatening approach evokes the documented underwater dragging, without a victim.
A dark river margin.

mintuci.aura: Rise through river reeds into close confrontation, one hand reaching toward the viewer while bird feet brace on wet stone. Visual grounding: mintuci-c02, mintuci-c08, mintuci-c09, mintuci-c07.

basis_claims.quote: a water sprite or an aquatic supernatural creature, a half-man-half-beast, told in stories of Ainu mythology and folklore.

statement.id: Ia digambarkan sebagai makhluk setengah manusia setengah hewan (half-man-half-beast).
statement.en: It is described as a half-man-half-beast creature.

basis_claims.quote: The mintuci has been defined as "fabulous animal", purported to be "half human and half animal and to inhabit lakes and rivers" in the Ainu dictionary c. 1900 compiled by British missionary John Batchelor.

statement.id: Kamus awal menempatkan makhluk ini di danau dan sungai.
statement.en: An early dictionary locates the creature in lakes and rivers.

basis_claims.quote: The mintuci are said to hunt people and livestock by dragging them underwater, but this prankishness is also a trait frequently ascribed to the kappa

statement.id: Mintuci konon memburu manusia dan ternak dengan menyeretnya ke dalam air, sifat yang juga sering dikaitkan dengan kappa.
statement.en: The mintuci are said to hunt people and livestock by dragging them underwater, a trait also often ascribed to the kappa.

basis_claims.quote: The mintuci are reputed to be of the height and stature of a 3-year-old to a 12-year-old or 13-year-old human.

statement.id: Mintuci dikabarkan setinggi dan sebesar anak manusia berumur 3 hingga 12 atau 13 tahun.
statement.en: The mintuci are reputed to be of the height and stature of a human child of 3 to 12 or 13 years.

basis_claims.quote: The mintuci ... Its skin is purplish or reddish, with sea turtle-like texture, and they have either bird-like feet or four sets of hooves, with one supposed witness discovering sickle-like footprints.

statement.id: Kulit mintuci digambarkan keunguan atau kemerahan dengan tekstur seperti kulit penyu laut, dan kakinya seperti kaki burung atau berupa empat set kuku.
statement.en: The mintuci's skin is described as purplish or reddish with a sea turtle-like texture, and it has either bird-like feet or four sets of hooves.

mo-chinese-zoology.depicted_variant: Bai Juyi elephant-trunk, rhinoceros-eye, cow-tail and tiger-paw chimera, not panda/tapir or Japanese baku.

visual_requirements.description: One composite quadruped with one head bearing an elephant trunk and exactly two rhinoceros-like eyes, FOUR tiger paws and one cow tail with a tuft. No rhinoceros horn, elephant tusks, extra heads or panda form.
Physically bite and bend iron and copper implements, the documented diet; no dream-eating or invented spell.
Mountain valleys of the south named by Bai Juyi.

mo-chinese-zoology.aura: Pull an iron bar into its mouth with its trunk and brace tiger paws toward the viewer. Visual grounding: mo-chinese-zoology-c07, mo-chinese-zoology-c08.

basis_claims.quote: 貘者，象鼻犀目，牛尾虎足，生南方山谷中。寢其皮辟瘟，圖其形辟邪。

statement.id: Dalam pengantar Bai Juyi, Mo digambarkan berbelalai gajah, bermata badak, berekor sapi, dan berkaki harimau, hidup di lembah-lembah pegunungan di selatan; tidur di atas kulitnya menolak wabah dan menggambar rupanya menolak kejahatan.
statement.en: In Bai Juyi's preface the mo has an elephant's nose, rhinoceros eyes, an ox tail and tiger feet, and lives in the mountain valleys of the south; sleeping on its skin averts pestilence and drawing its form averts evil.

basis_claims.quote: 寢其皮辟瘟，圖其形辟邪。予舊病頭風，每寢息，常以小屏衛其首，適遇畫工，偶令寫之。按《山海經》，此獸食鐵與銅，不食他物。

statement.id: Bai Juyi menulis bahwa menurut Shanhaijing binatang ini memakan besi dan tembaga dan tidak makan hal lain.
statement.en: Bai Juyi writes that, according to the Shanhaijing, this beast eats iron and copper and nothing else.

moon-rabbit.depicted_variant: Chinese white lunar hare pounding herbs for immortals; no mochi, sacrificial fire or other traditions merged.

visual_requirements.description: One WHITE hare with one head, two natural eyes, two long hare ears, four hare limbs and a short tail; it grips one pestle over one mortar full of herbs. No clothes, humanoid hands, horns, giant size or aggressive fangs.
Real herbal fragments scatter from the documented pounding for immortals, no invented healing rays or glowing elixir.
The Moon where the hare pounds herbs.

moon-rabbit.aura: Drive the pestle down into the mortar toward camera, ears upright and eyes intensely focused, fur and crushed herbs lifted by the motion. Visual grounding: moon-rabbit-c01, moon-rabbit-c06, moon-rabbit-c20.

basis_claims.quote: In East Asian mythology, the rabbit is seen as pounding with a mortar and pestle, but the contents of the mortar differ among Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese folklore.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Asia Timur, kelinci dilihat sedang menumbuk dengan lesung dan alu, tetapi isi lesung berbeda-beda dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok, Jepang, Korea, dan Vietnam.
statement.en: In East Asian mythology the rabbit is seen pounding with a mortar and pestle, but the contents of the mortar differ among Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese folklore.

basis_claims.quote: An early Chinese source called the Chu Ci, a Western Han anthology of Chinese poems from the Warring States period, notes that along with a toad, there is a hare on the Moon who constantly pounds herbs for the immortals.

statement.id: Sumber Tiongkok awal bernama Chu Ci, antologi puisi Han Barat dari zaman Negara-Negara Berperang, mencatat bahwa di samping seekor kodok, ada seekor hare di Bulan yang terus menumbuk ramuan bagi para makhluk abadi.
statement.en: An early Chinese source, the Chu Ci, a Western Han anthology of poems from the Warring States period, notes that along with a toad there is a hare on the Moon who constantly pounds herbs for the immortals.

basis_claims.quote: The hare in the moon is usually depicted as white.

statement.id: Hare di bulan biasanya digambarkan berwarna putih.
statement.en: The hare in the moon is usually depicted as white.

nuppeppo.depicted_variant: Child-sized intact flabby blob with indistinct face and fingerless undeveloped hands.

visual_requirements.description: One closed rounded flabby flesh-colored organic blob, one head merges into the body through indistinguishable wrinkles; two undeveloped lumpy arms and two undeveloped lumpy feet, NO fingers and no distinct eyes, nose or teeth. Entire skin is intact, without organs, wounds, genitals or anatomical nudity.
No supernatural attack or harmful power; physical mud and dust move from the documented running, with no colored odor cloud.
An old temple graveyard at night.

nuppeppo.aura: Run past the viewer between old grave stones, rounded body leaning into motion and lumpy feet disturbing damp earth. Visual grounding: nuppeppo-c02, nuppeppo-c07, nuppeppo-c12, nuppeppo-c06, nuppeppo-c09.

basis_claims.quote: It is depicted with indistinguishable wrinkles on its face and body as a one head blob of meat.

statement.id: Ia digambarkan dengan kerutan yang tak terbedakan di wajah dan tubuhnya, sebagai gumpalan daging berkepala satu.
statement.en: It is depicted with indistinguishable wrinkles on its face and body as a one-headed blob of meat.

basis_claims.quote: Habitat: graveyards, old temples

statement.id: Habitat nuppeppō disebut pemakaman dan kuil tua.
statement.en: The nuppeppō's habitat is given as graveyards and old temples.

basis_claims.quote: Nuppeppō appear usually only at night, and are not known to cause any particular harm or mischief—other than being disgusting.

statement.id: Nuppeppō biasanya hanya muncul pada malam hari dan tidak dikenal menimbulkan bahaya atau kenakalan tertentu selain menjijikkan.
statement.en: Nuppeppō usually appear only at night and are not known to cause any particular harm or mischief other than being disgusting.

basis_claims.quote: They look like large, flabby, roughly humanoid chunks of flesh about the size of child, with lumpy, undeveloped hands and feet, and vaguely indiscernible facial features.

statement.id: Mereka tampak seperti bongkahan daging besar yang lembek dan kira-kira berbentuk manusia, seukuran anak kecil, dengan tangan dan kaki yang benjol dan belum berkembang serta wajah yang samar.
statement.en: They look like large, flabby, roughly humanoid chunks of flesh about the size of a child, with lumpy, undeveloped hands and feet and vaguely indiscernible facial features.

basis_claims.quote: They can cause chaos and havoc by running around and disgusting people, and outrunning angry villagers who would try to chase them down and kill them.

statement.id: Mereka dapat menimbulkan kekacauan dengan berlari ke sana kemari dan membuat orang jijik, serta mengungguli penduduk desa marah yang mencoba mengejar dan membunuhnya.
statement.en: They can cause chaos by running around and disgusting people, and by outrunning angry villagers who try to chase them down and kill them.

basis_claims.quote: In 1609 (Keichō 14), at the courtyard of Sunpu Castle, someone that looked like a blob of meat appeared. It had the form of a young child, and it had hands but no fingers

statement.id: Pada 1609 (Keichō 14), di halaman Kastil Sunpu muncul sesuatu yang tampak seperti gumpalan daging berbentuk anak kecil, bertangan tetapi tanpa jari.
statement.en: In 1609 (Keichō 14), at the courtyard of Sunpu Castle, something that looked like a blob of meat appeared, with the form of a young child and hands but no fingers.

nyami-nyami.depicted_variant: Protective fish-headed snake river god; no monstrous teeth or supernatural organs.

visual_requirements.description: Exactly one FISH HEAD with two natural fish eyes and one mouth, smoothly joined to ONE long SNAKE BODY with one tail. No horns, legs, humanoid torso or extra heads.
Physical river water surges around the river god; fish and plentiful water in the current express his documented sustenance, no invented lightning or fangs.
The Zambezi at Kariba Gorge.

nyami-nyami.aura: Rise and turn from the Zambezi water toward the viewer, the fish head filling the foreground above a sweeping snake coil. Visual grounding: nyami-nyami-c02, nyami-nyami-c03, nyami-nyami-c14.

basis_claims.quote: Nyami Nyami wird gewöhnlich als männliche Figur dargestellt, die das Volk der Tonga beschützt und ihm Halt in schwierigen Zeiten gibt. Seine äußere Form ist eine Schlange, die den Kopf eines Fisches besitzt.

statement.id: Nyami Nyami biasanya digambarkan sebagai sosok laki-laki yang melindungi (beschützt) orang Tonga dan menopang mereka di masa sulit; wujudnya ular (Schlange) berkepala ikan.
statement.en: Nyami Nyami is usually shown as a male figure who protects (beschützt) the Tonga and sustains them in hard times; his form is a snake (Schlange) with a fish's head.

basis_claims.quote: Er sorgte dafür, dass genügend Wasser für die Bewässerung der Felder und genügend Fische im Fluss vorhanden waren.

statement.id: Ia memastikan cukup air (Wasser) untuk mengairi ladang dan cukup ikan (Fische) di sungai.
statement.en: He made sure there was enough water (Wasser) to irrigate the fields and enough fish (Fische) in the river.

basis_claims.quote: Eine Verbindung zum Gott und seiner Gemahlin, die beide in der Unterwelt in der Kariba-Schlucht wohnten, fand durch die Stammesältesten statt.

statement.id: Dewa ini dan istrinya (Gemahlin) tinggal di dunia bawah (Unterwelt) di Ngarai Kariba, dan hubungan dengan mereka dijalin lewat para tetua suku.
statement.en: The god and his wife (Gemahlin) lived in the underworld (Unterwelt) in the Kariba Gorge, and contact with them was made through the tribal elders.

basis_claims.quote: Nyami Nyami is a famous name given to the river god of the Tonga people; he is believed to be residing in the Zambezi river and the Kariba dam.

statement.id: Nyami Nyami adalah nama terkenal bagi dewa sungai (river god) orang Tonga, yang diyakini tinggal di Sungai Zambezi dan Bendungan Kariba.
statement.en: Nyami Nyami is the well-known name of the Tonga river god, believed to live in the Zambezi river and the Kariba dam.

basis_claims.quote: The nyami nyami on the other hand is seen as the god of the river in charge of the waters of the Zambezi river.

statement.id: Nyami Nyami dipandang sebagai dewa sungai yang menguasai perairan (in charge of the waters) Sungai Zambezi.
statement.en: Nyami Nyami is seen as the god of the river in charge of the waters of the Zambezi.

osan-kitsune.depicted_variant: Yuki-cho three-tailed fox variant; no burning tail or transformed woman merged.

visual_requirements.description: One ordinary fox head with two natural eyes, four fox legs and EXACTLY THREE separate fully visible fox tails. No human face, nine tails, fangs beyond normal fox teeth, flames or crown.
No visual magical effect; three documented tails and close movement distinguish the fox spirit. Do not import tail fire from the separate Hiroshima story.
A dark path in Yuki-cho, Hiroshima, without invented shrine imagery.

osan-kitsune.aura: Step down a shadowy path toward the viewer, the three distinct tails spreading behind its turning body, eyes fixed on camera. Visual grounding: osan-kitsune-c01, osan-kitsune-c13.

basis_claims.quote: Osan Kitsune (Japanese: おさん狐, おさんぎつね, romanized: Osan Fox) is a folktale from Hiroshima Prefecture, Japan.

statement.id: Osan Kitsune adalah dongeng roh rubah dari Hiroshima.
statement.en: Osan Kitsune is a fox-spirit folktale of Hiroshima.

basis_claims.quote: 広島県広島市佐伯郡湯来町では「尾三」と書かれるが、これは尾が3本あるからだという。

statement.id: Di Yuki-chō, Distrik Saeki, Hiroshima, namanya ditulis 尾三 karena konon ia berekor tiga.
statement.en: In Yuki-chō, Saeki District, Hiroshima, the name is written 尾三 because it is said to have three tails.

panlong-mythology.depicted_variant: living aquatic Chinese coiled dragon in its lair

visual_requirements.description: ONE living aquatic CHINESE DRAGON, one head/two eyes and continuous scaled body tightly COILED in water. Broad pronounced dragon muzzle, ridged brow, long wet whiskers and coarse beard/mane are conventional editorial dragon physiognomy, not exact sourced iconography. Hornless rendering; limbs and tail end entirely submerged. Not ordinary python/crocodile/statue.
Moving aquatic coils physically displace water into a bow wave and draining sheets. Source motif used in rain magic is not a claimed rain-control power.
Dark aquatic lair, wet rocks framing tight partly submerged coil.

panlong-mythology.aura: UNCOIL sharply toward the low water-level viewer, head raised out of breaking water while a tight visible circular body pushes water over itself; whiskers whip and jaws open. Supported by panlong-mythology-c01, panlong-mythology-c03, panlong-mythology-c01, panlong-mythology-c01, panlong-mythology-c05.

basis_claims.quote: Panlong (simplified Chinese: 蟠龙; traditional Chinese: 蟠龍; pinyin: pánlóng; Wade–Giles: p'an-lung; lit. "coiled dragon") is an aquatic dragon resembling a jiaolong 蛟龍 "river dragon; crocodile" in Chinese mythology, an ancient motif in Chinese art, and a proper name.

statement.id: Panlong adalah naga air mitologi Tiongkok yang menyerupai jiaolong dan juga menjadi motif seni.
statement.en: Panlong is an aquatic Chinese mythological dragon resembling jiaolong and also serving as an artistic motif.

basis_claims.quote: The materialist philosopher Yang Xiong (53 BCE – 18 CE) used both panlong and longpan. His Fangyan 方言 "Regional Speech" dictionary defined panlong 蟠龍 "coiled/curled dragon", "Dragons which do not yet ascend to heaven [cf. tianlong "heavenly dragon"] are called p'an-lung."

statement.id: Kamus Fangyan (方言) karya Yang Xiong mendefinisikan panlong 蟠龍 sebagai "naga melingkar": naga yang belum naik ke langit disebut p'an-lung.
statement.en: The Fangyan (方言) dictionary of Yang Xiong defined panlong 蟠龍 as a "coiled dragon": dragons which do not yet ascend to heaven are called p'an-lung.

basis_claims.quote: Shangshu dazhuan 尚書大傳 ... commentary to the Classic of History parallels panlong and jiaoyu 鮫魚 ... was greatly trusted in its lair

statement.id: Komentar Shangshu dazhuan (尚書大傳) atas Classic of History memadankan panlong dengan jiaoyu (鮫魚) dan menyebut "naga melingkar" itu sangat dipercaya di sarangnya.
statement.en: The Shangshu dazhuan (尚書大傳) commentary to the Classic of History parallels panlong with jiaoyu (鮫魚) and says the "coiled dragon" was greatly trusted in its lair.

peng.depicted_variant: Fully transformed giant Peng bird of Zhuangzi, not Kun fish or Penghou dog.

visual_requirements.description: ONE colossal bird with one head, two eyes, two immense wings like clouds across the sky, two bird feet and one feather tail; no fish body remains, no human head, horns, phoenix ornaments or flames.
The wings physically beat the sea into a vast wall of spray, as documented water-striking during migration; no lightning or glow.
The sea of the Northern Darkness at the start of migration to the Southern Darkness.

peng.aura: Heave upward from the sea toward the viewer, both wings sweeping the water during migration south. Visual grounding: peng-c01, peng-c05, peng-c06.

basis_claims.quote: A Peng (Chinese: 鵬; pinyin: péng) or Dapeng (大鵬; dàpéng) is a giant bird that transforms from a Kun (鯤; kūn), a giant fish, in Chinese mythology.

statement.id: Peng adalah burung raksasa dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang berubah dari ikan Kun.
statement.en: Peng is a giant Chinese mythological bird transformed from the fish Kun.

basis_claims.quote: 北冥有魚，其名爲鯤。鯤之大，不知其幾千里也，化而爲鳥，其名爲鵬。鵬之背，不知其幾千里也，怒而飛，其翼若垂天之雲。

statement.id: Dalam bab "Xiaoyao You" Zhuangzi, di Lautan Utara ada ikan bernama Kun yang sangat besar; ikan itu berubah menjadi burung bernama Peng, yang punggungnya luas ribuan li dan sayapnya bagai awan yang menggantung dari langit.
statement.en: In the "Xiaoyao You" chapter of the Zhuangzi, a fish named Kun lives in the Northern Darkness and is immensely large; it transforms into a bird named Peng, whose back spans thousands of li and whose wings are like clouds hanging from the sky.

basis_claims.quote: 是鳥也，海運，則將徙於南冥。南冥者，天池也。齊諧者，志怪者也。諧之言曰：「鵬之徙於南冥也，水擊三千里

statement.id: Ketika laut bergolak, burung itu akan berpindah ke Lautan Selatan, yaitu Telaga Langit; Qi Xie, "pencatat hal-hal ganjil", berkata bahwa dalam perpindahan itu ia memukul air sejauh tiga ribu li.
statement.en: When the sea stirs, the bird will migrate to the Southern Darkness, the Pool of Heaven; Qi Xie, "one who records the strange", says that in the migration it beats the water for three thousand li.

penghou.depicted_variant: Wu camphor-tree human-face and dog-body variant; not combined with Baize Tu tailless black-dog version.

visual_requirements.description: Exactly one HUMAN FACE with two ordinary human eyes on one DOG BODY with four canine legs; no separate dog head. Natural short dark fur is an editorial surface choice. Tail region is entirely hidden behind the tree so no tail variant is asserted. No horns or fangs.
Wood splits and chips around the emergence recorded by the tale; no sap blood, wounds or magic glow.
A felled great camphor tree in the Jian'an tale.

penghou.aura: Push its human-faced head and dog forequarters out of the split camphor trunk toward the viewer, forepaws braced at the opening. Visual grounding: penghou-c07.

basis_claims.quote: 吳先主時，陸敬叔為建安郡太守。使人伐大樟樹，不數斧，有血出，樹斷，有物人面狗身，從樹中出。敬叔曰，此名「彭侯」。乃烹食之。

statement.id: Pada masa penguasa pertama Wu, Lu Jingshu, gubernur Jian'an, menyuruh orang menebang pohon kamper besar; darah keluar, dan dari pohon itu keluar makhluk berwajah manusia dan bertubuh anjing. Ia menyebutnya Penghou lalu memasak dan memakannya.
statement.en: In the time of the first ruler of Wu, Lu Jingshu, governor of Jian'an, had a great camphor tree felled; blood came out, and a creature with a human face and a dog's body emerged from the tree. He named it Penghou, then cooked and ate it.

pincoya.depicted_variant: Pincoya, the benevolent Chilotan marine-fertility spirit rising into her sea-facing dance

visual_requirements.description: ONE beautiful adult WOMAN with very long blond-to-reddish hair, ONE head/TWO eyes/TWO arms/TWO HUMAN LEGS. NO fish-tail, gills, scales or mermaidbody. Entire chest/hips covered by FULLY OPAQUE high-neck long-sleeve thick woven flowing dress, opaque wetfabric, no nudity or sheer cloth.

Marine fertility visibly acts as great abundance of living fish: dense schools converge within translucent seawater around her emerging sea-facing dance, some naturally breach surface. Fish never fly orlevitate. Sea water falls physically off her body as she rises from depths. No invented wave-control or luminous energy.
Chilotan ocean close to coast; she emerges IN the sea and dances oriented outward toward open sea, mountains behind camera.

pincoya.aura: RISE from deep seawater and TURN into a sweeping sea-facing fertility dance, one HUMAN knee raised visibly from the wave, both arms sweep toward the open ocean. Bright joyful authoritative face turns threequarters toward viewer; blondhair and opaque dress spiral with dance. Dense fishschools surge toward her below water so she is unmistakably active marine spirit, never a woman strolling on beach. Grounded in pincoya-c02, pincoya-c08, pincoya-c10, pincoya-c03, pincoya-c04, pincoya-c11, pincoya-c01

basis_claims.quote: The Pincoya is, according to local mythology, a female "water spirit" of the Chilotan Seas.

statement.id: Menurut mitologi setempat, Pincoya adalah roh air perempuan dari laut Chiloé.
statement.en: In local mythology, the Pincoya is a female water spirit of the Chilotan seas.

basis_claims.quote: The Pincoya is said to have long blond hair, be of incomparable beauty, be cheerful and sensual, and rise from the depths of the sea.

statement.id: Pincoya konon berambut pirang panjang, sangat cantik, ceria, dan muncul dari kedalaman laut.
statement.en: The Pincoya has long blond hair and incomparable beauty, is cheerful, and rises from the sea's depths.

basis_claims.quote: Naked and pure, she personifies the fertility of marine species.

statement.id: Ia melambangkan kesuburan makhluk laut.
statement.en: She personifies the fertility of marine species.

basis_claims.quote: If she performs her dance facing the sea, it means that these shores will have an abundance of fish.  When she dances facing the mountains, her back to the sea, seafood will be scarce.

statement.id: Jika ia menari menghadap laut, pantai itu akan berlimpah ikan; jika menghadap gunung, hasil laut akan langka.
statement.en: If she dances facing the sea, fish will be plentiful; facing the mountains, seafood will be scarce.

basis_claims.quote: PINCOYA: f. ... Su cuerpo desnudo, su cabellera entre rojiza y rubia, y sus hermosas lineas femeninas

statement.id: Ia digambarkan bertubuh telanjang, berambut antara kemerahan dan pirang, dengan lekuk tubuh perempuan yang indah.
statement.en: She is described with a naked body, hair between reddish and blond, and beautiful feminine lines.

basis_claims.quote: PINCOYA: f. ... A diferencia de la Sirena, ... no posee cola de pescado.

statement.id: Berbeda dengan Sirena, Pincoya tidak berekor ikan.
statement.en: Unlike the Sirena, the Pincoya has no fish tail.

basis_claims.quote: PINCOYA: f. Patrona protectora de ... mariscos y peces de la costa.

statement.id: Pincoya adalah pelindung kerang-kerangan dan ikan di pesisir.
statement.en: The Pincoya is a protective patroness of the shellfish and fish of the coast.

rantas.depicted_variant: Long-haired sharp-toothed backward-feet winter-wanderer variant; not reversed hands or shapeshift transition.

visual_requirements.description: One female humanoid head with two eyes, long dishevelled hair, ordinary human teeth and ordinary human fingers; two arms and two legs. BOTH feet are anatomically rotated180degrees at the ankles: heels point forward toward camera and toes point BACKWARD away from camera while her chest faces camera. Full opaque layered winter dress covers torso and intimate anatomy; bare feet clearly visible.
Physical snow is displaced by her documented winter wandering; no invented ice magic or glowing eyes.
A heavily forested Kashmiri place on a snowy winter night.

rantas.aura: Stride and wail toward the viewer through heavy snow, long nails reaching forward while backward toes leave unmistakable reverse footprints. Visual grounding: rantas-c01, rantas-c05, rantas-c02.

basis_claims.quote: Rantas (Kashmiri pronunciation: [rãːʈas]) is a mythical creature from Kashmiri folklore. She is described as a female with long hair, pointed teeth, long nails, and inverted feet who ventures out during heavily snowy nights. She is invoked to frighten children into staying safely at home during winter.

statement.id: Rantas adalah makhluk perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Kashmir, berambut panjang dan berkaki terbalik.
statement.en: Rantas is a female creature of Kashmiri folklore, with long hair and reversed feet.

basis_claims.quote: Rantas (Kashmiri pronunciation: [rãːʈas]) is a mythical creature from Kashmiri folklore. She is described as a female with long hair, pointed teeth, long nails, and inverted feet who ventures out during heavily snowy nights. She is invoked to frighten children into staying safely at home during winter.

statement.id: Ia digambarkan keluar pada malam bersalju lebat.
statement.en: She is described as venturing out on heavily snowy nights.

basis_claims.quote: Rantas is said to abduct men, keeping them prisoner and later marrying them due to sorrow over the loss of her lover. She wanders and wails on moonless nights, walking on feet that are turned backward.

statement.id: Rantas dikatakan mengembara dan meratap pada malam tanpa bulan sambil berjalan dengan kaki yang menghadap ke belakang.
statement.en: Rantas is said to wander and wail on moonless nights, walking on feet that are turned backward.

basis_claims.quote: The Raantas is basically a mythical creature from Kashmiri folklore. She is usually supposed to reside in heavily forested areas and frequently visits nearby villages during winters.

statement.id: Menurut penulis ini, Raantas adalah makhluk mitos dari cerita rakyat Kashmir yang biasanya dianggap tinggal di kawasan hutan lebat dan sering mengunjungi desa terdekat pada musim dingin.
statement.en: According to this author, the Raantas is a mythical creature from Kashmiri folklore who is usually supposed to reside in heavily forested areas and frequently visits nearby villages during winters.

sasabonsam.depicted_variant: Six-armed iron-toothed hook-legged Asanbosam variant; no bat wings or bidirectional-foot account mixed.

visual_requirements.description: One humanoid head with two ordinary eyes and clearly METALLIC IRON TEETH, EXACTLY SIX ARMS arranged as three pairs, ALL SIX separate arms and hands entirely visible; EXACTLY TWO legs ending in iron-hook feet. Full opaque simple cloth covers torso and intimate anatomy. No wings, backwards human feet, horns or red glowing eyes.
Physical bark chips dislodge under iron hooks; attack from above is documented, without victims, blood or magical effects.
A high branch in dark forest trees.

sasabonsam.aura: Drop and reach toward the viewer from a high tree branch, the six arms spread into distinct spaces while two iron-hook feet grip the branch. Visual grounding: sasabonsam-c24, sasabonsam-c25, sasabonsam-c04.

basis_claims.quote: It is said to have iron teeth and long hair and lives in trees, attacking from above.

statement.id: Konon ia bergigi besi (iron teeth), berambut panjang, tinggal di pohon, dan menyerang dari atas.
statement.en: It is said to have iron teeth and long hair, to live in trees and to attack from above.

basis_claims.quote: They take up territory in the trees in the forests, where they live and feed on people that wander into their home.

statement.id: Mereka menguasai wilayah di pepohonan hutan (forests), tempat mereka hidup dan memangsa orang yang masuk ke wilayahnya.
statement.en: They claim territory in forest trees, where they live and feed on people who wander into their home.

basis_claims.quote: Es soll bei ihnen Männer, Frauen und Kinder geben, die alle Zähne aus Eisen, Beine mit hakenartigen Fortsätzen und sechs Arme haben.

statement.id: Konon di antara mereka ada laki-laki, perempuan, dan anak-anak, semuanya bergigi besi (Zähne aus Eisen), berkaki dengan tonjolan seperti kait, dan berlengan enam (sechs Arme).
statement.en: Among them there are said to be men, women and children, all with iron teeth (Zähne aus Eisen), legs with hook-like projections and six arms (sechs Arme).

basis_claims.quote: Dikatakan bahwa asanbosam memiliki gigi besi dan kakinya berupa pengait besi.

statement.id: Asanbosam dikatakan memiliki gigi besi dan kaki berupa pengait besi.
statement.en: The asanbosam is said to have iron teeth and feet in the form of iron hooks.

lady-in-red.depicted_variant: the distraught gliding ghost reported at Lower Bay transit station

visual_requirements.description: ONE woman ghost wearing fully opaque SCARLET RED DRESS, ONE head/TWO arms. Eye sockets are EMPTY with NO EYES; dress hem ends above ground with NO FEET present or visible. No gore, wounds or rotting tissue.
Reported gliding without feet or eyes; physical floating movement only, no invented attack, energy glow or lightning death.
Closed Lower Bay Toronto transit station: dim tiled platform and dark railway, absolutely no station signs/lettering.

lady-in-red.aura: GLIDE close along empty subway platform toward viewer, red skirt trailing above floor, distraught face inclining and hand reaching toward near empty space. Grounded in lady-in-red-c01, lady-in-red-c02, lady-in-red-c09.

basis_claims.quote: A Lady in Red or Red Lady is a type of female ghost, similar to the White Lady, but according to legend is more specifically attributed to a jilted lover, killed in a fit of passion, or a woman of vanity.

statement.id: Lady in Red adalah jenis hantu perempuan yang mirip White Lady, tetapi menurut legenda lebih khusus dikaitkan dengan kekasih yang dicampakkan, korban pembunuhan karena emosi, atau perempuan yang sombong.
statement.en: The Lady in Red is a type of female ghost like the White Lady, attributed in legend to a jilted lover, a victim of passion, or a vain woman.

basis_claims.quote: In all cases, the Lady in Red is wearing a scarlet or blood red dress.

statement.id: Dalam semua versi, ia bergaun merah tua atau merah darah.
statement.en: In all cases she wears a scarlet or blood-red dress.

basis_claims.quote: Toronto's Lower Bay transit station has been closed since 1966 but has numerous reports of a Lady in Red. According to witnesses, the ghost appears distraught as it glides without feet or eyes.

statement.id: Stasiun transit Lower Bay di Toronto ditutup sejak 1966 tetapi punya banyak laporan Lady in Red; menurut saksi, hantu itu tampak terpukul dan meluncur tanpa kaki atau mata.
statement.en: Toronto's Lower Bay transit station has been closed since 1966 but has numerous reports of a Lady in Red; according to witnesses the ghost appears distraught and glides without feet or eyes.

lake-tianchi-monster.depicted_variant: the reported long-necked smooth grey human-headed lake creature

visual_requirements.description: ONE creature with ONE HUMAN-LIKE HEAD, TWO BIG ROUND EYES and PROTRUDING MOUTH; smooth GREY SKIN; neck1.2-1.5metres long, clear WHITE RING separates neck from barely visible TORSO at waterline. Body below lake water completely obscured, no speculative legs/fins/wings added.
Reported aquatic appearance/swimming; physical wake/splash only, no magical powers or fire.
Heaven Lake/Tianchi at Baekdu-Changbai volcanic peak, distant crater rim subordinate behind water.

lake-tianchi-monster.aura: SURGE head and long neck straight out of dark water toward close viewer, mouth open and big eyes fixed, a heavy sheet of water cascading from white neck-base ring. Grounded in lake-tianchi-monster-c04, lake-tianchi-monster-c09, lake-tianchi-monster-c01.

basis_claims.quote: Lake Tianchi Monster is the name given to what is said to be a cryptid that lives in Heaven Lake (known as Cheonji in Korean) located in the peak of Baekdu Mountain within the Baekdu-daegan and Changbai mountain ranges encompassing Jilin Province of China and Ryanggang Province of North Korea.

statement.id: Lake Tianchi Monster adalah nama untuk kriptid yang konon hidup di Danau Heaven (Cheonji dalam bahasa Korea) di puncak Gunung Baekdu, dalam pegunungan Baekdu-daegan dan Changbai yang mencakup Provinsi Jilin di Tiongkok dan Provinsi Ryanggang di Korea Utara.
statement.en: Lake Tianchi Monster is the name given to a cryptid said to live in Heaven Lake (Cheonji in Korean) at the peak of Baekdu Mountain, within the Baekdu-daegan and Changbai mountain ranges encompassing Jilin Province of China and Ryanggang Province of North Korea.

basis_claims.quote: More recent reports describe the monster as having a human-like head attached to a 1.5-meter (5 ft) neck. It is said to have a white ring around the bottom of its neck, and the rest of its skin is grey and smooth.

statement.id: Laporan lain menggambarkan kepala mirip manusia pada leher sepanjang sekitar 1,5 meter.
statement.en: Other reports describe a human-like head on a neck about 1.5 meters long.

basis_claims.quote: Another sighting compared the head of the monster to that of a human, except with big round eyes, a protruding mouth and a neck 1.2 to 1.5 metres long. It also had a white ring separating its neck and torso and smooth, grey skin.

statement.id: Laporan lain membandingkan kepala makhluk itu dengan kepala manusia, tetapi bermata bulat besar dan berbibir menonjol, berleher 1,2 sampai 1,5 meter, bercincin putih di antara leher dan badan, dan berkulit abu-abu mulus.
statement.en: Another sighting compared the monster's head to a human head but with big round eyes and a protruding mouth, a neck 1.2 to 1.5 metres long, a white ring separating neck and torso, and smooth grey skin.

maero.depicted_variant: the dark-haired giant forest wildman armed with stone club

visual_requirements.description: ONE giant human-shaped forest being, ONE head/TWO eyes/TWO arms/TWO legs, body covered in DARK HAIR; LONG BONY fingers with SHARP FINGERNAILS; exactly five fingers eachhand; one massive STONE CLUB gripped firmly. Fully opaque simple dark waistcloth/legwrappings beneath dense bodyhair.
Documented violence and stone club only; no regeneration shown, no separated parts or magic aura.
Mountain forest in NewZealand SouthIsland/Tararua tradition, dense wet undergrowth and rough rocks.

maero.aura: STRIDE from forest shadow swinging stone club toward low viewer, free long-fingered hand reaching acrossforeground, face fiercely intent; grounded feet throw earth/grit. Grounded in maero-c02, maero-c03, maero-c04.

basis_claims.quote: They are sometimes described as giants or wild men of the woods, and inhabit mountains and forest, particularly in the South Island and Tararua Range.

statement.id: Mereka digambarkan sebagai raksasa atau manusia liar hutan yang mendiami pegunungan dan hutan di South Island serta Tararua Range.
statement.en: They are described as giants or wild men inhabiting mountains and forests in the South Island and Tararua Range.

basis_claims.quote: Maero are characterised as wild, malevolent and often violent, carrying stone clubs as weapons.

statement.id: Maero memiliki sifat liar, jahat, dan membawa gada batu sebagai senjata.
statement.en: Maero are characterised as wild, malevolent and violent, carrying stone clubs as weapons.

basis_claims.quote: They are covered in dark body hair and have long, bony fingers with sharp fingernails. They kill and eat humans and other animals.

statement.id: Tubuh mereka tertutup rambut hitam dan memiliki jari kurus panjang dengan kuku tajam.
statement.en: They are covered in dark body hair and have long bony fingers with sharp fingernails.

African ocean shore where she ventures to comb herhair.
